<h1 id="lithic-developer-api">Lithic Developer API v1.0.0</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

The Lithic Developer API is designed to provide a predictable programmatic interface for accessing your Lithic account through an API and transaction webhooks.
Note that your API key is a secret and should be treated as such. Don't share it with anyone, including us. We will never ask you for it.

Base URLs:

* <a href="https://sandbox.lithic.com">https://sandbox.lithic.com</a> - Sandbox environment that provides key functionality mirroring production

<a href="https://lithic.com/legal/terms">Terms of service</a>
Web: <a href="https://support.lithic.com/">https://support.lithic.com/</a>

# Authentication

* API Key (ApiKeyAuth)
    - Parameter Name: **Authorization**, in: header.

<h1 id="lithic-developer-api-3ds">3DS</h1>

## Simulate 3DS authentication

<a id="opIdpostSimulateAuthentication"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/three_ds_authentication/simulate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "merchant": {
      "country": "USA",
      "id": "OODKZAPJVN4YS7O",
      "mcc": "5812",
      "name": "COFFEE SHOP"
    },
    "pan": "4111111289144142",
    "transaction": {
      "amount": 0,
      "currency": "GBP"
    },
    "card_expiry_check": "MATCH"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/three_ds_authentication/simulate`

Simulates a 3DS authentication request from the payment network as if it came from an ACS. If you're configured for 3DS Customer Decisioning, simulating authentications requires your customer decisioning endpoint to be set up properly (respond with a valid JSON). If the authentication decision is to challenge, ensure that the account holder associated with the card transaction has a valid phone number configured to receive the OTP code via SMS. 

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "merchant": {
    "country": "USA",
    "id": "OODKZAPJVN4YS7O",
    "mcc": "5812",
    "name": "COFFEE SHOP"
  },
  "pan": "4111111289144142",
  "transaction": {
    "amount": 0,
    "currency": "GBP"
  },
  "card_expiry_check": "MATCH"
}
```

<h3 id="simulate-3ds-authentication-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[simulate-authentication-request](#schemasimulate-authentication-request)|true|none|
|» merchant|body|object|true|Merchant information for the simulated transaction|
|» » country|body|string|true|Country of the address provided by the cardholder in ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 format (e.g. USA)|
|» » id|body|string|true|Unique identifier to identify the payment card acceptor. Corresponds to `merchant_acceptor_id` in authorization.|
|» » mcc|body|string|true|Merchant category code for the transaction to be simulated. A four-digit number listed in ISO 18245. Supported merchant category codes can be found [here](https://docs.lithic.com/docs/transactions#merchant-category-codes-mccs).|
|» » name|body|string|true|Merchant descriptor, corresponds to `descriptor` in authorization. If CHALLENGE keyword is included, Lithic will trigger a challenge.|
|» pan|body|string|true|Sixteen digit card number.|
|» transaction|body|object|true|Transaction details for the simulation|
|» » amount|body|integer|true|Amount (in cents) to authenticate.|
|» » currency|body|string|true|3-character alphabetic ISO 4217 currency code.|
|» card_expiry_check|body|string|false|When set will use the following values as part of the Simulated Authentication. When not set defaults to MATCH|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» card_expiry_check|MATCH|
|» card_expiry_check|MISMATCH|
|» card_expiry_check|NOT_PRESENT|

```json
}
```

## Simulate entering OTP into 3DS Challenge UI

<a id="opIdpostSimulateEnterOtp"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/three_ds_decisioning/simulate/enter_otp \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "token": "fabd829d-7f7b-4432-a8f2-07ea4889aaac",
    "otp": "123456"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/three_ds_decisioning/simulate/enter_otp`

Endpoint for simulating entering OTP into 3DS Challenge UI. A call to [/v1/three_ds_authentication/simulate](https://docs.lithic.com/reference/postsimulateauthentication) that resulted in triggered SMS-OTP challenge must precede. Only a single attempt is supported; upon entering OTP, the challenge is either approved or declined.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "token": "fabd829d-7f7b-4432-a8f2-07ea4889aaac",
  "otp": "123456"
}
```

<h3 id="simulate-entering-otp-into-3ds-challenge-ui-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» token|body|string(uuid)|true|A unique token returned as part of a /v1/three_ds_authentication/simulate call that resulted in PENDING_CHALLENGE authentication result.|
|» otp|body|string|true|The OTP entered by the cardholder|

## Retrieve the 3DS Decisioning HMAC secret key

<a id="opIdgetThreeDsDecisioningSecret"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/three_ds_decisioning/secret \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v1/three_ds_decisioning/secret`

Retrieve the 3DS Decisioning HMAC secret key. If one does not exist for your program yet, calling this endpoint will create one for you. The headers (which you can use to verify 3DS Decisioning requests) will begin appearing shortly after calling this endpoint for the first time. See [this page](https://docs.lithic.com/docs/3ds-decisioning#3ds-decisioning-hmac-secrets) for more detail about verifying 3DS Decisioning requests.


> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "secret": "whsec_1NDsYinMGr951KuDEaj78VtWzlyPaOnwUVagFiWIPJs="
}
```

> 401 Response

```json

  "message": "string"
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
  "debugging_request_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
```

## Rotate the 3DS Decisioning HMAC secret key

<a id="opIdrotateThreeDsDecisioningSecret"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/three_ds_decisioning/secret/rotate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`POST /v1/three_ds_decisioning/secret/rotate`

Generate a new 3DS Decisioning HMAC secret key. The old secret key will be deactivated 24 hours after a successful request to this endpoint. Make a [`GET /three_ds_decisioning/secret`](https://docs.lithic.com/reference/getthreedsdecisioningsecret) request to retrieve the new secret key.


> Example responses

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "debugging_request_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "message": "string"
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "debugging_request_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "message": "string"
}
```

## Respond to a Challenge Request

<a id="opIdpostThreeDsChallengeResponse"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/three_ds_decisioning/challenge_response \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "challenge_response": "APPROVE"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/three_ds_decisioning/challenge_response`

Card program's response to a 3DS Challenge Request.
Challenge Request is emitted as a webhook [three_ds_authentication.challenge](https://docs.lithic.com/reference/threedsauthenticationchallengewebhook) and your Card Program needs to be configured with Out of Band (OOB) Challenges in order to receive it (see https://docs.lithic.com/docs/3ds-challenge-flow for more information).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "challenge_response": "APPROVE"
}
```

<h3 id="respond-to-a-challenge-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[challenge-response](#schemachallenge-response)|false|none|
|» token|body|string(uuid)|true|Globally unique identifier for 3DS Authentication that resulted in PENDING_CHALLENGE authentication result.|
|» challenge_response|body|string|true|Whether the Cardholder has approved or declined the issued Challenge|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» challenge_response|APPROVE|
|» challenge_response|DECLINE_BY_CUSTOMER|

> Example responses

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="respond-to-a-challenge-request-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Challenge Response was received and forwarded to the ACS|None|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request body|None|
|404|Not Found|The provided token was not found|None|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Challenge Response could not be actioned because a response was already set, or the status was updated by the upstream 3DS Service|[challenge-response-unprocessable](#schemachallenge-response-unprocessable)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Lithic Error|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth
</aside>

<h1 id="lithic-developer-api-account">Account</h1>

## List accounts

<a id="opIdgetAccounts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/accounts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v1/accounts`

List account configurations.


<h3 id="list-accounts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|begin|query|string(date-time)|false|Date string in RFC 3339 format. Only entries created on or after the specified time will be included. UTC time zone.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|Date string in RFC 3339 format. Only entries created before the specified time will be included. UTC time zone.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor representing an item's token before which a page of results should end. Used to retrieve the previous page of results before this item.|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Page size (for pagination).|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor representing an item's token after which a page of results should begin. Used to retrieve the next page of results after this item.|

## Update account

<a id="opIdpatchAccountByToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/accounts/d86a0a4d-7459-471a-83b4-431136320828 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "daily_spend_limit": 1000
  }'
```

`PATCH /v1/accounts/{account_token}`

Update account configuration such as state or spend limits. Can only be run on accounts that are part of the program managed by this API key.
Accounts that are in the `PAUSED` state will not be able to transact or create new cards.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "daily_spend_limit": 1000
}
```

<h3 id="update-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_token|path|string(uuid)|true|Globally unique identifier for account.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» daily_spend_limit|body|integer|false|Amount (in cents) for the account's daily spend limit (e.g. 100000 would be a $1,000 limit). A spend limit of 0 means that no daily spend limit is enforced.<br>Clients onboarded on or after February 1, 2026 have no default account spend limits. For clients onboarded before that date that do not use Auth Stream Access, new accounts have a default daily spend limit of $1,250<br>|
|» lifetime_spend_limit|body|integer|false|Amount (in cents) for the account's lifetime spend limit (e.g. 100000 would be a $1,000 limit). Once this limit is reached, no transactions will be accepted on any card created for this account until the limit is updated. A spend limit of 0 means that no lifetime spend limit is enforced<br>|
|» monthly_spend_limit|body|integer|false|Amount (in cents) for the account's monthly spend limit (e.g. 100000 would be a $1,000 limit). A spend limit of 0 means that no monthly spend limit is enforced.<br>Clients onboarded on or after February 1, 2026 have no default account spend limits. For clients onboarded before that date that do not use Auth Stream Access, new accounts have a default monthly spend limit of $5,000<br>|
|» state|body|string|false|Account states.|
|» substatus|body|string \| null|false|Account state substatus values:<br>* `FRAUD_IDENTIFIED` - The account has been recognized as being created or used with stolen or fabricated identity information, encompassing both true identity theft and synthetic identities.<br>* `SUSPICIOUS_ACTIVITY` - The account has exhibited suspicious behavior, such as unauthorized access or fraudulent transactions, necessitating further investigation.<br>* `RISK_VIOLATION` - The account has been involved in deliberate misuse by the legitimate account holder. Examples include disputing valid transactions without cause, falsely claiming non-receipt of goods, or engaging in intentional bust-out schemes to exploit account services.<br>* `END_USER_REQUEST` - The account holder has voluntarily requested the closure of the account for personal reasons. This encompasses situations such as bankruptcy, other financial considerations, or the account holder's death.<br>* `ISSUER_REQUEST` - The issuer has initiated the closure of the account due to business strategy, risk management, inactivity, product changes, regulatory concerns, or violations of terms and conditions.<br>* `NOT_ACTIVE` - The account has not had any transactions or payment activity within a specified period. This status applies to accounts that are paused or closed due to inactivity.<br>* `INTERNAL_REVIEW` - The account is temporarily paused pending further internal review. In future implementations, this status may prevent clients from activating the account via APIs until the review is completed.<br>* `OTHER` - The reason for the account's current status does not fall into any of the above categories. A comment should be provided to specify the particular reason.<br>|
|» comment|body|string|false|Additional context or information related to the account.|
|» verification_address|body|object|false|**Deprecated.** Address used during Address Verification Service (AVS) checks during transactions if enabled via Auth Rules. This field is deprecated as AVS checks are no longer supported by Auth Rules. The field will be removed from the schema in a future release.|
|» » address1|body|string|false|none|
|» » address2|body|string|false|none|
|» » city|body|string|false|none|
|» » country|body|string|false|none|
|» » postal_code|body|string|false|none|
|» » state|body|string|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» state|ACTIVE|
|» state|PAUSED|
|» state|CLOSED|
|» substatus|FRAUD_IDENTIFIED|
|» substatus|SUSPICIOUS_ACTIVITY|
|» substatus|RISK_VIOLATION|
|» substatus|END_USER_REQUEST|
|» substatus|ISSUER_REQUEST|
|» substatus|NOT_ACTIVE|
|» substatus|INTERNAL_REVIEW|
|» substatus|OTHER|

> 200 Response

```json
  "spend_limit": {
    "daily": 1000,

  },
  "state": "ACTIVE",
```

## Get account's available spend limits

<a id="opIdgetAccountSpendLimits"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/accounts/d86a0a4d-7459-471a-83b4-431136320828/spend_limits \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v1/accounts/{account_token}/spend_limits`

Get an Account's available spend limits, which is based on the spend limit configured on the Account and the amount already spent over the spend limit's duration. For example, if the Account has a daily spend limit of $1000 configured, and has spent $600 in the last 24 hours, the available spend limit returned would be $400.

<h3 id="get-accounts-available-spend-limits-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_token|path|string(uuid)|true|Globally unique identifier for account.|

```json
    "lifetime": 300000,
    "monthly": 200000

  "spend_limit": {
    "daily": 500000,
    "lifetime": 500000,
    "monthly": 500000
  },
  "spend_velocity": {
    "daily": 40000,
    "lifetime": 20000,
    "monthly": 30000
  }
}
```

## Fetch account signals

<a id="opIdgetAccountSignals"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/accounts/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/signals \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v1/accounts/{account_token}/signals`

Returns behavioral feature state derived from an account's transaction history.

These signals expose the same data used by behavioral rule attributes (e.g. `AMOUNT_Z_SCORE`
with `scope: ACCOUNT`, `IS_NEW_COUNTRY` with `scope: ACCOUNT`) and custom code
`TRANSACTION_HISTORY_SIGNALS` features, allowing clients to inspect feature values before
writing rules and debug rule behavior.

Note: 3DS fields are not available at the account scope and will be null.


<h3 id="fetch-account-signals-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_token|path|string(uuid)|true|The token of the account to fetch signals for.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "avg_transaction_amount": 0,
  "stdev_transaction_amount": 0,
  "approved_txn_count": 0,
  "avg_transaction_amount_7d": 0,
  "stdev_transaction_amount_7d": 0,
  "approved_txn_count_7d": 0,

  "stdev_transaction_amount_30d": 0,
```

<h1 id="lithic-developer-api-account-holder">Account Holder</h1>

## Get a list of individual or business account holders

<a id="opIdgetAccountHolders"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/account_holders \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v1/account_holders`

Get a list of individual or business account holders and their KYC or KYB evaluation status.

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-individual-or-business-account-holders-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|external_id|query|string(uuid)|false|If applicable, represents the external_id associated with the account_holder.|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of account_holders to limit the response to.|
|first_name|query|string|false|(Individual Account Holders only) The first name of the account holder. The query is case insensitive and supports partial matches.|
|last_name|query|string|false|(Individual Account Holders only) The last name of the account holder. The query is case insensitive and supports partial matches.|
|legal_business_name|query|string|false|(Business Account Holders only) The legal business name of the account holder. The query is case insensitive and supports partial matches.|
|phone_number|query|string|false|Phone number of the account holder. The query must be an exact match.|
|email|query|string|false|Email address of the account holder. The query must be an exact match, case insensitive.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor representing an item's token before which a page of results should end. Used to retrieve the previous page of results before this item.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor representing an item's token after which a page of results should begin. Used to retrieve the next page of results after this item.|

`POST /v1/account_holders`

Create an account holder and initiate the appropriate onboarding workflow.  Account holders and accounts have a 1:1 relationship. When an account holder is successfully created an associated account is also created.
All calls to this endpoint will return a synchronous response. The response time will depend on the workflow. In some cases, the response may indicate the workflow is under review or further action will be needed to complete the account creation process.
This endpoint can only be used on accounts that are part of the program that the calling API key manages.

## Update account holder information and possibly resubmit for evaluation

<a id="opIdpatchAccountHolder"></a>

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/account_holders/65db64b2-ae89-491a-97d9-f64788f8b2ab \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "business_entity": {
      "entity_token": "83cf25ae-c14f-4d10-9fa2-0119f36c7286",
      "address": {
        "postal_code": "61023"
      }
    },
    "control_person": {
      "entity_token": "fd771a07-c5c2-42f3-a53c-a6c79c6c0d07",
      "address": {
        "postal_code": "68023"
      }
    },
    "naics_code": "541512",
    "website_url": "https://www.mynewbusiness.com"
  }'
```

`PATCH /v1/account_holders/{account_holder_token}`

Update the information associated with a particular account holder (including business owners and control persons associated to a business account).
If Lithic is performing KYB or KYC and additional verification is required we will run the individual's or business's updated information again and return whether the status is accepted or pending (i.e., further action required).
All calls to this endpoint will return a synchronous response. The response time will depend on the workflow. In some cases, the response may indicate the workflow is under review or further action will be needed to complete the account creation process.
This endpoint can only be used on existing accounts that are part of the program that the calling API key manages.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "business_entity": {
    "entity_token": "83cf25ae-c14f-4d10-9fa2-0119f36c7286",
    "address": {
      "postal_code": "61023"
    }
  },
  "control_person": {
    "entity_token": "fd771a07-c5c2-42f3-a53c-a6c79c6c0d07",
    "address": {
      "postal_code": "68023"
    }
  },
  "naics_code": "541512",
  "website_url": "https://www.mynewbusiness.com"
}
```

<h3 id="update-account-holder-information-and-possibly-resubmit-for-evaluation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_holder_token|path|string(uuid)|true|Globally unique identifier for the account holder.|
|body|body|[kyb-patch-request](#schemakyb-patch-request) \| [kyc-patch-request](#schemakyc-patch-request) \| [patch-request](#schemapatch-request)|true|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|[kyb-patch-request](#schemakyb-patch-request)|false|The KYB request payload for updating a business.|
|» *anyOf*|body|[kyc-patch-request](#schemakyc-patch-request)|false|The KYC request payload for updating an account holder.|
|» *anyOf*|body|[patch-request](#schemapatch-request)|false|The legacy request for updating an account holder.|

```json
  "token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "account_token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "business_account_token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "created": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "exemption_type": "AUTHORIZED_USER",
  "external_id": "string",
  "user_type": "BUSINESS",

    "created": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "status": "ACCEPTED",
    "status_reasons": [
      "ADDRESS_VERIFICATION_FAILURE"
```

## Get account holder document uploads

<a id="opIdgetAccountHolderDocuments"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/account_holders/65db64b2-ae89-491a-97d9-f64788f8b2ab/documents \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v1/account_holders/{account_holder_token}/documents`

Retrieve the status of account holder document uploads, or retrieve the upload URLs to process your image uploads.

Note that this is not equivalent to checking the status of the KYC evaluation overall (a document may be successfully uploaded but not be sufficient for KYC to pass).

In the event your upload URLs have expired, calling this endpoint will refresh them.
Similarly, in the event a previous account holder document upload has failed, you can use this endpoint to get a new upload URL for the failed image upload.

When a new document upload is generated for a failed attempt, the response will show an additional entry in the `required_document_uploads` list
in a `PENDING` state for the corresponding `image_type`.


<h3 id="get-account-holder-document-uploads-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_holder_token|path|string(uuid)|true|Globally unique identifier for the account holder.|

## Initiate account holder document upload

<a id="opIdpostAccountHolderDocuments"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/account_holders/65db64b2-ae89-491a-97d9-f64788f8b2ab/documents \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "entity_token": "83cf25ae-c14f-4d10-9fa2-0119f36c7286",
    "document_type": "EIN_LETTER"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/account_holders/{account_holder_token}/documents`

Use this endpoint to identify which type of supported government-issued documentation you will upload for further verification.
It will return two URLs to upload your document images to - one for the front image and one for the back image.

This endpoint is only valid for evaluations in a `PENDING_DOCUMENT` state.

Supported file types include `jpg`, `png`, and `pdf`. Each file must be less than 15 MiB. Once both required uploads have been successfully completed, your document will be run through KYC verification.

If you have registered a webhook, you will receive evaluation updates for any document submission evaluations, as well as for any failed document uploads.

Two document submission attempts are permitted via this endpoint before a `REJECTED` status is returned and the account creation process is ended. Currently only one type of
account holder document is supported per KYC verification.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "entity_token": "83cf25ae-c14f-4d10-9fa2-0119f36c7286",
  "document_type": "EIN_LETTER"
}
```

<h3 id="initiate-account-holder-document-upload-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_holder_token|path|string(uuid)|true|Globally unique identifier for the account holder.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» document_type|body|string|true|The type of document to upload|
|» entity_token|body|string(uuid)|true|Globally unique identifier for the entity.|

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/account_holders/65db64b2-ae89-491a-97d9-f64788f8b2ab/entities \
```

`POST /v1/account_holders/{account_holder_token}/entities`

Create a new beneficial owner individual or replace the control person entity on an existing KYB account holder. This endpoint is only applicable for account holders enrolled through a KYB workflow with the Persona KYB provider.
A new control person can only replace the existing one. A maximum of 4 beneficial owners can be associated with an account holder.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "BENEFICIAL_OWNER_INDIVIDUAL",
  "first_name": "Timmy",
  "last_name": "Turner",
  "dob": "1991-03-08T08:00:00Z",
  "email": "tim@left-earth.com",
  "phone_number": "+15555555555",
  "government_id": "211-23-1412",
  "address": {
    "address1": "300 Normal Forest Way",
    "city": "Portland",
    "country": "USA",
    "postal_code": "90210",
    "state": "OR"
  }
}
```

|body|body|[create-entity-request](#schemacreate-entity-request)|true|none|
|» address|body|[address2](#schemaaddress2)|true|Individual's current address - PO boxes, UPS drops, and FedEx drops are not acceptable; APO/FPO are acceptable. Only USA addresses are supported for the KYB and KYC workflows.|
|» dob|body|string|true|Individual's date of birth, as an RFC 3339 date.|
|» email|body|string|true|Individual's email address. If utilizing Lithic for chargeback processing, this customer email address may be used to communicate dispute status and resolution.|
|» first_name|body|string|true|Individual's first name, as it appears on government-issued identity documents.|
|» last_name|body|string|true|Individual's last name, as it appears on government-issued identity documents.|
|» phone_number|body|string|true|Individual's phone number, entered in E.164 format.|
|» government_id|body|string|true|Government-issued identification number (required for identity verification and compliance with banking regulations). Social Security Numbers (SSN) and Individual Taxpayer Identification Numbers (ITIN) are currently supported, entered as full nine-digits, with or without hyphens|
|» type|body|[entity-type](#schemaentity-type)|true|The type of entity to create on the account holder|

## Retrieve the ASA HMAC secret key

<a id="opIdgetAuthStreamSecret"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/auth_stream/secret \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v1/auth_stream/secret`

Retrieve the ASA HMAC secret key. If one does not exist for your program yet, calling this endpoint will create one for you. The headers (which you can use to verify webhooks) will begin appearing shortly after calling this endpoint for the first time. See [this page](https://docs.lithic.com/docs/auth-stream-access-asa#asa-webhook-verification) for more detail about verifying ASA webhooks.

## Rotate the ASA HMAC secret key

<a id="opIdrotateAuthStreamSecret"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/auth_stream/secret/rotate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`POST /v1/auth_stream/secret/rotate`

Generate a new ASA HMAC secret key. The old ASA HMAC secret key will be deactivated 24 hours after a successful request to this endpoint. Make a [`GET /auth_stream/secret`](https://docs.lithic.com/reference/getauthstreamsecret) request to retrieve the new secret key.

<h1 id="lithic-developer-api-auth-rules">Auth Rules</h1>

## List rules

<a id="opIdgetAuthRules"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v2/auth_rules \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v2/auth_rules`

Lists V2 Auth rules

<h3 id="list-rules-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ending_before|query|string(uuid)|false|A cursor representing an item's token before which a page of results should end. Used to retrieve the previous page of results before this item.|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Page size (for pagination).|
|starting_after|query|string(uuid)|false|A cursor representing an item's token after which a page of results should begin. Used to retrieve the next page of results after this item.|
|card_token|query|string(uuid)|false|Only return Auth Rules that are bound to the provided card token.|
|account_token|query|string(uuid)|false|Only return Auth Rules that are bound to the provided account token.|
|business_account_token|query|string(uuid)|false|Only return Auth Rules that are bound to the provided business account token.|
|scope|query|string|false|Only return Auth Rules that are bound to the provided scope. When no token is provided, `CARD` also returns Auth Rules that include a `CARD_TAG` entity.|
|event_stream|query|[event-stream](#schemaevent-stream)|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated: Use event_streams instead. Only return Auth rules that are executed during the provided event stream.|
|event_streams|query|[[event-stream](#schemaevent-stream)]|false|Only return Auth rules that are executed during any of the provided event streams. If event_streams and event_stream are specified, the values will be combined.|

## Create a new rule

<a id="opIdpostAuthRules"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v2/auth_rules \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "entities": {
      "include": [
        {
          "type": "PROGRAM"
        }
      ],
      "exclude": [
        {
          "type": "PROGRAM"
        }
      ]
    },
    "type": "VELOCITY_LIMIT",
    "parameters": {
      "scope": "CARD",
      "period": {
        "duration": 10,
        "type": "CUSTOM"
      },
      "filters": {
        "include_mccs": [
          "5542"
        ],
        "exclude_mccs": [
          "5542"
        ],
        "include_countries": [
          "USA"
        ],
        "exclude_countries": [
          "USA"
        ],
        "include_pan_entry_modes": [
          "AUTO_ENTRY"
        ]
      },
      "limit_amount": 10000,
      "limit_count": 0,
      "limit_cash_amount": 5000,
      "limit_cash_count": 0
    },
    "name": "string",
    "event_stream": "AUTHORIZATION"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/auth_rules`

Creates a new V2 Auth rule in draft mode


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "entities": {
    "include": [
      {
        "type": "PROGRAM"
      }
    ],
    "exclude": [
      {
        "type": "PROGRAM"
      }
    ]
  },
  "type": "VELOCITY_LIMIT",
  "parameters": {
    "scope": "CARD",
    "period": {
      "duration": 10,
      "type": "CUSTOM"
    },
    "filters": {
      "include_mccs": [
        "5542"
      ],
      "exclude_mccs": [
        "5542"
      ],
      "include_countries": [
        "USA"
      ],
      "exclude_countries": [
        "USA"
      ],
      "include_pan_entry_modes": [
        "AUTO_ENTRY"
      ]
    },
    "limit_amount": 10000,
    "limit_count": 0,
    "limit_cash_amount": 5000,
    "limit_cash_count": 0
  },
  "name": "string",
  "event_stream": "AUTHORIZATION"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-rule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[create-auth-rule-request](#schemacreate-auth-rule-request)|true|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» entities|body|[auth-rule-entities](#schemaauth-rule-entities)|true|The entities an Auth Rule applies to (`include`) and does not apply to (`exclude`). An exclusion overrides an inclusion, so a card excluded here is skipped even when the program, its account or one of its tags is included.<br><br>The rule's resulting entities must satisfy these constraints after any write:<br><br>- `include` must contain at least one entity.<br>- If `PROGRAM` is included, it must be the only included entity.<br>- `PROGRAM` cannot be excluded.<br>- An entity cannot appear in both `include` and `exclude`, or twice in the same list.<br>- A rule can have at most 1,000 entities across `include` and `exclude`, not counting `PROGRAM`.<br>- Entity types must be valid for the rule's event stream.<br>- `CARD`, `ACCOUNT` and `BUSINESS_ACCOUNT` tokens must belong to your program.<br>|
|» type|body|[auth-rule-type](#schemaauth-rule-type)|true|The type of Auth Rule. For certain rule types, this determines the event stream during which it will be evaluated. For rules that can be applied to one of several event streams, the effective one is defined by the separate `event_stream` field.<br><br>- `VELOCITY_LIMIT`: AUTHORIZATION event stream.<br>- `MERCHANT_LOCK`: AUTHORIZATION event stream.<br>- `CONDITIONAL_ACTION`: AUTHORIZATION, THREE_DS_AUTHENTICATION, TOKENIZATION, ACH_CREDIT_RECEIPT, ACH_DEBIT_RECEIPT, CARD_TRANSACTION_UPDATE, or ACH_PAYMENT_UPDATE event stream.<br>- `TYPESCRIPT_CODE`: AUTHORIZATION, THREE_DS_AUTHENTICATION, TOKENIZATION, ACH_CREDIT_RECEIPT, ACH_DEBIT_RECEIPT, CARD_TRANSACTION_UPDATE, or ACH_PAYMENT_UPDATE event stream.<br>- `OTHER`: A rule whose type is not exposed through this API. Rules of this type are read-only; `OTHER` cannot be used when creating a rule.|
|» parameters|body|[auth-rule-parameters](#schemaauth-rule-parameters)|true|Parameters for the Auth Rule|
|» name|body|[auth-rule-name](#schemaauth-rule-name)|false|Auth Rule Name|
|» event_stream|body|[event-stream](#schemaevent-stream)|false|The event stream during which the rule will be evaluated.|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated: Use `entities` instead. Cannot be combined with `entities`.|

|» business_account_tokens|body|[business-account-tokens](#schemabusiness-account-tokens)|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated: Use `entities.include` with `BUSINESS_ACCOUNT` entities instead.<br><br>Business Account tokens to which the Auth Rule applies.|
|» type|body|[auth-rule-type](#schemaauth-rule-type)|true|The type of Auth Rule. For certain rule types, this determines the event stream during which it will be evaluated. For rules that can be applied to one of several event streams, the effective one is defined by the separate `event_stream` field.<br><br>- `VELOCITY_LIMIT`: AUTHORIZATION event stream.<br>- `MERCHANT_LOCK`: AUTHORIZATION event stream.<br>- `CONDITIONAL_ACTION`: AUTHORIZATION, THREE_DS_AUTHENTICATION, TOKENIZATION, ACH_CREDIT_RECEIPT, ACH_DEBIT_RECEIPT, CARD_TRANSACTION_UPDATE, or ACH_PAYMENT_UPDATE event stream.<br>- `TYPESCRIPT_CODE`: AUTHORIZATION, THREE_DS_AUTHENTICATION, TOKENIZATION, ACH_CREDIT_RECEIPT, ACH_DEBIT_RECEIPT, CARD_TRANSACTION_UPDATE, or ACH_PAYMENT_UPDATE event stream.<br>- `OTHER`: A rule whose type is not exposed through this API. ## Update a rule

<a id="opIdpatchAuthRuleByToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v2/auth_rules/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "entities": {
      "include": [
        {
          "type": "PROGRAM"
        }
      ],
      "exclude": [
        {
          "type": "PROGRAM"
        }
      ]
    },
    "state": "INACTIVE",
    "name": "string"
  }'
```

`PATCH /v2/auth_rules/{auth_rule_token}`

Updates a V2 Auth rule's properties

If `entities` is provided, this will replace the rule's existing entities with the provided `include` and `exclude` lists. To change entities incrementally, use `PATCH /v2/auth_rules/{auth_rule_token}/entities` instead.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "entities": {
    "include": [
      {
        "type": "PROGRAM"
      }
    ],
    "exclude": [
      {
        "type": "PROGRAM"
      }
    ]
  },
  "state": "INACTIVE",
  "name": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-rule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|auth_rule_token|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|[patch-auth-rule-request](#schemapatch-auth-rule-request)|true|none|
|» state|body|string|false|The desired state of the Auth Rule.<br><br>Note that only deactivating an Auth Rule through this endpoint is supported at this time. If you need to (re-)activate an Auth Rule the /promote endpoint should be used to promote a draft to the currently active version.|
|» name|body|[auth-rule-name](#schemaauth-rule-name)|false|Auth Rule Name|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|Replaces the rule's existing entities with the provided `include` and `exclude` lists. A missing list is treated as empty, so `include` must always be provided.<br>|
|» entities|body|[auth-rule-entities](#schemaauth-rule-entities)|false|The entities an Auth Rule applies to (`include`) and does not apply to (`exclude`). An exclusion overrides an inclusion, so a card excluded here is skipped even when the program, its account or one of its tags is included.<br><br>The rule's resulting entities must satisfy these constraints after any write:<br><br>- `include` must contain at least one entity.<br>- If `PROGRAM` is included, it must be the only included entity.<br>- `PROGRAM` cannot be excluded.<br>- An entity cannot appear in both `include` and `exclude`, or twice in the same list.<br>- A rule can have at most 1,000 entities across `include` and `exclude`, not counting `PROGRAM`.<br>- Entity types must be valid for the rule's event stream.<br>- `CARD`, `ACCOUNT` and `BUSINESS_ACCOUNT` tokens must belong to your program.<br>|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated: Use `entities` instead. Cannot be combined with `entities`.|
|» account_tokens|body|[account-tokens](#schemaaccount-tokens)|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated: Use `entities.include` with `ACCOUNT` entities instead.<br><br>Account tokens to which the Auth Rule applies.|
|» business_account_tokens|body|[business-account-tokens](#schemabusiness-account-tokens)|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated: Use `entities.include` with `BUSINESS_ACCOUNT` entities instead.<br><br>Business Account tokens to which the Auth Rule applies.|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated: Use `entities` instead. Cannot be combined with `entities`.|
|» card_tokens|body|[card-tokens](#schemacard-tokens)|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated: Use `entities.include` with `CARD` entities instead.<br><br>Card tokens to which the Auth Rule applies. Cards the rule applies to through a `CARD_TAG` entity are not listed.|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated: Use `entities` instead. Cannot be combined with `entities`.|
|» program_level|body|[program-level](#schemaprogram-level)|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated: Use `entities.include` with a `PROGRAM` entity instead.<br><br>Whether the Auth Rule applies to all authorizations on the card program.|
|» excluded_card_tokens|body|[excluded-card-tokens](#schemaexcluded-card-tokens)|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated: Use `entities.exclude` with `CARD` entities instead.<br><br>Card tokens to which the Auth Rule does not apply. Cards excluded through a `CARD_TAG` entity are not listed.|
|» excluded_account_tokens|body|[excluded-account-tokens](#schemaexcluded-account-tokens)|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated: Use `entities.exclude` with `ACCOUNT` entities instead.<br><br>Account tokens to which the Auth Rule does not apply.|
|» excluded_business_account_tokens|body|[excluded-business-account-tokens](#schemaexcluded-business-account-tokens)|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated: Use `entities.exclude` with `BUSINESS_ACCOUNT` entities instead.<br><br>Business account tokens to which the Auth Rule does not apply.|

> Example responses

## Calculated Feature values

<a id="opIdgetAuthRuleFeatures"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v2/auth_rules/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/features \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v2/auth_rules/{auth_rule_token}/features`

Fetches the current calculated Feature values for the given Auth Rule

This only calculates the features for the active version.
- VelocityLimit Rules calculates the current Velocity Feature data. This requires a `card_token` or `account_token` matching what the rule is Scoped to.
- ConditionalAction Rules calculates the CARD_TRANSACTION_COUNT_* attributes on the rule. This requires a `card_token`


<h3 id="calculated-feature-values-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|auth_rule_token|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|account_token|query|string(uuid)|false|none|
|card_token|query|string(uuid)|false|none|

## Retrieve a performance report

<a id="opIdgetAuthRuleReport"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://sandbox.lithic.com/v2/auth_rules/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/report?begin=1970-01-01&end=1970-01-01' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v2/auth_rules/{auth_rule_token}/report`

Retrieves a performance report for an Auth rule containing daily statistics and evaluation outcomes.

**Time Range Limitations:**
- Reports are supported for the past 3 months only
- Maximum interval length is 1 month
- Report data is available only through the previous day in UTC (current day data is not available)

The report provides daily statistics for both current and draft versions of the Auth rule, including approval, decline, and challenge counts along with sample events.

|end|query|string(date)|true|End date for the report|

## Request a backtest

<a id="opIdpostAuthRuleBacktest"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v2/auth_rules/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/backtests \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "start": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "end": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/auth_rules/{auth_rule_token}/backtests`

Initiates a request to asynchronously generate a backtest for an Auth rule. During backtesting, both the active version (if one exists) and the draft version of the Auth Rule are evaluated by replaying historical transaction data against the rule's conditions. This process allows customers to simulate and understand the effects of proposed rule changes before deployment.
The generated backtest report provides detailed results showing whether the draft version of the Auth Rule would have approved or declined historical transactions which were processed during the backtest period. These reports help evaluate how changes to rule configurations might affect overall transaction approval rates.

The generated backtest report will be delivered asynchronously through a webhook with `event_type` = `auth_rules.backtest_report.created`. See the docs on setting up [webhook subscriptions](https://docs.lithic.com/docs/events-api).
It is also possible to request backtest reports on-demand through the `/v2/auth_rules/{auth_rule_token}/backtests/{auth_rule_backtest_token}` endpoint.

Lithic currently supports backtesting for `CONDITIONAL_ACTION` rules. Backtesting for `VELOCITY_LIMIT` rules is generally not supported. In specific cases (i.e. where Lithic has pre-calculated the requested velocity metrics for historical transactions), a backtest may be feasible. However, such cases are uncommon and customers should not anticipate support for velocity backtests under most configurations.
If a historical transaction does not feature the required inputs to evaluate the rule, then it will not be included in the final backtest report.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "start": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "end": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="request-a-backtest-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|auth_rule_token|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|[backtest-request](#schemabacktest-request)|true|none|
|» start|body|string(date-time)|false|The start time of the backtest.|
|» end|body|string(date-time)|false|The end time of the backtest.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "backtest_token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": "Invalid input"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": "Invalid input"
}
```

<h3 id="request-a-backtest-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Backtest request received|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|[Error2](#schemaerror2)|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|[Error2](#schemaerror2)|

<h3 id="request-a-backtest-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|backtest_token|[backtest-token](#schemabacktest-token)|false|none|Auth Rule Backtest Token|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth
</aside>

## Retrieve backtest results

<a id="opIdgetAuthRuleBacktestByToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v2/auth_rules/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/backtests/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v2/auth_rules/{auth_rule_token}/backtests/{auth_rule_backtest_token}`

Returns the backtest results of an Auth rule (if available).

Backtesting is an asynchronous process that requires time to complete. If a customer retrieves the backtest results using this endpoint before the report is fully generated, the response will return null for `results.current_version` and `results.draft_version`. Customers are advised to wait for the backtest creation process to complete (as indicated by the webhook event auth_rules.backtest_report.created) before retrieving results from this endpoint.

Backtesting is an asynchronous process, while the backtest is being processed, results will not be available which will cause `results.current_version` and `results.draft_version` objects to contain `null`.
The entries in `results` will also always represent the configuration of the rule at the time requests are made to this endpoint. For example, the results for `current_version` in the served backtest report will be consistent with which version of the rule is currently activated in the respective event stream, regardless of which version of the rule was active in the event stream at the time a backtest is requested.


<h3 id="retrieve-backtest-results-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|auth_rule_token|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|auth_rule_backtest_token|path|string(uuid)|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "backtest_token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "simulation_parameters": {
    "start": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "end": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  },
  "results": {
    "current_version": {
      "version": 0,
      "approved": 0,
      "declined": 0,
      "challenged": 0,
      "examples": [
        {
          "event_token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
          "transaction_token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
          "timestamp": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
          "decision": "APPROVED"
        }
      ]
    },
    "draft_version": {
      "version": 0,
      "approved": 0,
      "declined": 0,
      "challenged": 0,
      "examples": [
        {
          "event_token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
          "transaction_token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
          "timestamp": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
          "decision": "APPROVED"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "created": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

```json
  "error": "Invalid input"
}
```

`GET /v2/auth_rules/results`

Lists Auth Rule evaluation results.

**Limitations:**
- Results are available for the past 3 months only
- At least one filter (`event_token` or `auth_rule_token`) must be provided
- When filtering by `event_token`, pagination is not supported


<h3 id="list-rule-evaluation-results-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ending_before|query|string(uuid)|false|A cursor representing an item's token before which a page of results should end. Used to retrieve the previous page of results before this item.|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Page size (for pagination).|
|starting_after|query|string(uuid)|false|A cursor representing an item's token after which a page of results should begin. Used to retrieve the next page of results after this item.|
|event_token|query|string(uuid)|false|Filter by event token|
|auth_rule_token|query|string(uuid)|false|Filter by Auth Rule token|
|begin|query|string(date-time)|false|Date string in RFC 3339 format. Only events evaluated on or after the specified time will be included. UTC time zone.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|Date string in RFC 3339 format. Only events evaluated before the specified time will be included. UTC time zone.|
|has_actions|query|boolean|false|Filter by whether the rule evaluation produced any actions. When not provided, all results are returned.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "token": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",

        }

  ],
  "has_more": false
}
```

```json
}
```

```json
}
```

## Get open to buy

<a id="opIdgetOpenToBuy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/financial_accounts/3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6/open_to_buy \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v1/financial_accounts/{financial_account_token}/open_to_buy`

Get the funds available for card spend backed by a given Security Account, along with the
balances that amount is derived from.

Open to buy is the amount Lithic authorizes card spend against. It is not a stored balance,
so it is recalculated on every request from the Security Account, the funds held against spend
Lithic has already paid out to the networks on your behalf, and the spend that has not yet been
collected. The accounts that feed the calculation depend on your program setup, so
`summary.settled_funds` is `null` outside Commercial Charge.

Supported for Commercial Charge, Dynamic Reserve, and Secured Charge programs. Returns `404`
if `financial_account_token` is not a Security Account you own, or if your program setup does
not use an open to buy calculation.


<h3 id="get-open-to-buy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|financial_account_token|path|string(uuid)|true|Globally unique identifier for the Security Account to price|

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "open_to_buy": 350000,
  "summary": {
    "security": 300000,
    "settled_funds": 300000,
    "total_outstanding_spend": -250000
  }
}
```

<h1 id="lithic-developer-api-blockchain-recipient">Blockchain Recipient</h1>

## Create blockchain recipient

<a id="opIdcreateBlockchainRecipient"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/blockchain_recipients \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "account_token": "dabadb3b-700c-41e3-8801-d5dfc84ebea0",
    "address": "0x45bfcf1a6289a0b77b4d3f7d12005a05949fd8c3",
    "chain": "ETHEREUM",
    "name": "Cold wallet",
    "owner": "John Doe",
    "owner_type": "INDIVIDUAL"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/blockchain_recipients`

Register a blockchain address as a withdrawal destination for a financial account

The recipient is created with a `PENDING` verification state and cannot receive a payout until
screening of the address completes. Registering an address that is already registered to the same
financial account returns the existing recipient and its current verification state, rather than
creating a second one


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "account_token": "dabadb3b-700c-41e3-8801-d5dfc84ebea0",
  "address": "0x45bfcf1a6289a0b77b4d3f7d12005a05949fd8c3",
  "chain": "ETHEREUM",
  "name": "Cold wallet",
  "owner": "John Doe",
  "owner_type": "INDIVIDUAL"
}
```

<h3 id="create-blockchain-recipient-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[blockchain_recipient_request](#schemablockchain_recipient_request)|true|none|
|» chain|body|string|true|The blockchain network that the address belongs to|
|» address|body|string|true|The blockchain address funds will be withdrawn to|
|» address_tag|body|string|false|An optional tag or memo used by some chains to identify the destination of a transfer within a shared address|
|» name|body|string|false|The nickname for this blockchain recipient|
|» owner|body|string|true|Legal name of the business or individual who owns the blockchain address|
|» owner_type|body|[owner_type](#schemaowner_type)|true|Owner Type|
|» account_token|body|string(uuid)|true|The financial account the blockchain recipient belongs to|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» owner_type|INDIVIDUAL|
|» owner_type|BUSINESS|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
  "chain": "string",
  "address_tag": "string",

  "updated": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "state": "ENABLED",
  "verification_state": "PENDING"
}
```

Transfer funds between two financial accounts or between a financial account and card

## Create book transfer

<a id="opIdpostBookTransfers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/book_transfers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "amount": 1,
    "category": "ADJUSTMENT",
    "from_financial_account_token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "memo": "string",
    "subtype": "string",
    "to_financial_account_token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "type": "ATM_BALANCE_INQUIRY",
    "external_id": "string",
    "on_closed_account": "FAIL",
    "hold_token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/book_transfers`

Book transfer funds between two financial accounts or between a financial account and card

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "amount": 1,
  "category": "ADJUSTMENT",
  "from_financial_account_token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "memo": "string",
  "subtype": "string",
  "to_financial_account_token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "type": "ATM_BALANCE_INQUIRY",
  "external_id": "string",
  "on_closed_account": "FAIL",
  "hold_token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
}
```

<h3 id="create-book-transfer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[create_book_transfer_request](#schemacreate_book_transfer_request)|true|none|
|» amount|body|integer|true|Amount to be transferred in the currency's smallest unit (e.g., cents for USD). This should always be a positive value.|
|» category|body|[book_transfer_category](#schemabook_transfer_category)|true|none|
|» from_financial_account_token|body|string(uuid)|true|Globally unique identifier for the financial account or card that will send the funds. Accepted type dependent on the program's use case.|
|» memo|body|string|false|Optional descriptor for the transfer.|
|» subtype|body|string|true|The program specific subtype code for the specified category/type.|
|» to_financial_account_token|body|string(uuid)|true|Globally unique identifier for the financial account or card that will receive the funds. Accepted type dependent on the program's use case.|
|» token|body|string(uuid)|false|Customer-provided token that will serve as an idempotency token. This token will become the transaction token.|
|» type|body|[book_transfer_type](#schemabook_transfer_type)|true|Type of the book transfer|
|» external_id|body|string|false|External ID defined by the customer|
|» on_closed_account|body|[on_closed_account](#schemaon_closed_account)|false|What to do if the financial account is closed when posting an operation|
|» hold_token|body|string(uuid)|false|Token of an existing hold to settle when this transfer is initiated|

## Fetch card signals

<a id="opIdgetCardSignals"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/cards/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/signals \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v1/cards/{card_token}/signals`

Returns behavioral feature state derived from a card's transaction history.

These signals expose the same data used by behavioral rule attributes (e.g. `AMOUNT_Z_SCORE` with `scope: CARD`, `IS_NEW_COUNTRY` with `scope: CARD`) and custom code `TRANSACTION_HISTORY_SIGNALS` features, allowing clients to inspect feature values before writing rules and debug rule behavior.


<h3 id="fetch-card-signals-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|card_token|path|string(uuid)|true|The token of the card to fetch signals for.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "avg_transaction_amount": 0,
  "stdev_transaction_amount": 0,
  "approved_txn_count": 0,
  "avg_transaction_amount_7d": 0,
  "stdev_transaction_amount_7d": 0,
  "approved_txn_count_7d": 0,
  "avg_transaction_amount_30d": 0,
  "stdev_transaction_amount_30d": 0,

  "distinct_country_count": 0,
  "distinct_mcc_count": 0,
  "seen_countries": [
    "string"
  ],
  "seen_mccs": [
    "string"
  ],
  "seen_merchants": [
    "string"
  ],
  "first_txn_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "last_txn_approved_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "last_cp_country": "string",
  "last_cp_postal_code": "string",

  "approved_txn_amount_m2": 0,
```

## Create card

<a id="opIdpostCards"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/cards \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "memo": "New Card",
    "spend_limit": 1000,
    "spend_limit_duration": "TRANSACTION",
    "state": "OPEN",
    "tags": {
      "risk-level": "high"
    },
    "type": "VIRTUAL"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/cards`

Create a new virtual or physical card. Parameters `shipping_address` and `product_id` only apply to physical cards.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "memo": "New Card",
  "spend_limit": 1000,
  "spend_limit_duration": "TRANSACTION",
  "state": "OPEN",
  "tags": {
    "risk-level": "high"
  },
  "type": "VIRTUAL"
}
```

<h3 id="create-card-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string(uuid)|false|Idempotency key for the request|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» account_token|body|string(uuid)|false|Globally unique identifier for the account that the card will be associated with. Required for programs enrolling users using the [/account\_holders endpoint](https://docs.lithic.com/docs/account-holders-kyc). See [Managing Your Program](doc:managing-your-program) for more information.<br>|
|» card_program_token|body|string(uuid)|false|For card programs with more than one BIN range. This must be configured with Lithic before use. Identifies the card program/BIN range under which to create the card. If omitted, will utilize the program's default `card_program_token`. In Sandbox, use 00000000-0000-0000-1000-000000000000 and 00000000-0000-0000-2000-000000000000 to test creating cards on specific card programs.|
|» bulk_order_token|body|string(uuid)|false|Globally unique identifier for an existing bulk order to associate this card with. When specified, the card will be added to the bulk order for batch shipment. Only applicable to cards of type PHYSICAL|
|» carrier|body|[Carrier](#schemacarrier)|false|none|
|» digital_card_art_token|body|string(uuid)|false|Specifies the digital card art to be displayed in the user’s digital wallet after tokenization. This artwork must be approved by Mastercard and configured by Lithic to use. See [Flexible Card Art Guide](https://docs.lithic.com/docs/about-digital-wallets#flexible-card-art).|
|» exp_month|body|string|false|Two digit (MM) expiry month. If neither `exp_month` nor `exp_year` is provided, an expiration date five years in the future will be generated. Five years is the maximum expiration date.|
|» exp_year|body|string|false|Four digit (yyyy) expiry year. If neither `exp_month` nor `exp_year` is provided, an expiration date five years in the future will be generated. Five years is the maximum expiration date.|
|» memo|body|string|false|Friendly name to identify the card.|
|» pin|body|string|false|Encrypted PIN block (in base64). Applies to cards of type `PHYSICAL` and `VIRTUAL`. See [Encrypted PIN Block](https://docs.lithic.com/docs/cards#encrypted-pin-block).|
|» product_id|body|string|false|Only applicable to cards of type `PHYSICAL`. This must be configured with Lithic before use. Specifies the configuration (i.e., physical card art) that the card should be manufactured with.|
|» replacement_for|body|string(uuid)|false|Globally unique identifier for the card that this card will replace. If the card type is `PHYSICAL` it will be replaced by a `PHYSICAL` card. If the card type is `VIRTUAL` it will be replaced by a `VIRTUAL` card.|
|» replacement_substatus|body|string|false|Card state substatus values for the card that this card will replace:<br>* `LOST` - The physical card is no longer in the cardholder's possession due to being lost or never received by the cardholder.<br>* `COMPROMISED` - Card information has been exposed, potentially leading to unauthorized access. This may involve physical card theft, cloning, or online data breaches.<br>* `DAMAGED` - The physical card is not functioning properly, such as having chip failures or a demagnetized magnetic stripe.<br>* `END_USER_REQUEST` - The cardholder requested the closure of the card for reasons unrelated to fraud or damage, such as switching to a different product or closing the account.<br>* `ISSUER_REQUEST` - The issuer closed the card for reasons unrelated to fraud or damage, such as account inactivity, product or policy changes, or technology upgrades.<br>* `NOT_ACTIVE` - The card hasn’t had any transaction activity for a specified period, applicable to statuses like `PAUSED` or `CLOSED`.<br>* `SUSPICIOUS_ACTIVITY` - The card has one or more suspicious transactions or activities that require review. This can involve prompting the cardholder to confirm legitimate use or report confirmed fraud.<br>* `INTERNAL_REVIEW` - The card is temporarily paused pending further internal review.<br>* `EXPIRED` - The card has expired and has been closed without being reissued.<br>* `UNDELIVERABLE` - The card cannot be delivered to the cardholder and has been returned.<br>* `OTHER` - The reason for the status does not fall into any of the above categories. A comment should be provided to specify the reason.<br>|
|» replacement_comment|body|string|false|Additional context or information related to the card that this card will replace.|
|» replacement_account_token|body|string(uuid)|false|Restricted field limited to select use cases. Lithic will reach out directly if this field should be used. Globally unique identifier for the replacement card's account. If this field is specified, `replacement_for` must also be specified. If `replacement_for` is specified and this field is omitted, the replacement card's account will be inferred from the card being replaced.|
|» shipping_address|body|[ShippingAddress](#schemashippingaddress)|false|none|
|» shipping_method|body|string|false|Shipping method for the card. Only applies to cards of type PHYSICAL.<br>Use of options besides `STANDARD` require additional permissions.<br><br>* `STANDARD` - USPS regular mail or similar international option, with no tracking<br>* `STANDARD_WITH_TRACKING` - USPS regular mail or similar international option, with tracking<br>* `PRIORITY` - USPS Priority, 1-3 day shipping, with tracking<br>* `EXPRESS` - FedEx or UPS depending on card manufacturer, Express, 3-day shipping, with tracking<br>* `2_DAY` - FedEx or UPS depending on card manufacturer, 2-day shipping, with tracking<br>* `EXPEDITED` - FedEx or UPS depending on card manufacturer, Standard Overnight or similar international option, with tracking<br>* `BULK` - Card will be shipped as part of a bulk fulfillment order. The shipping method and timeline are inherited from the parent bulk order.<br>|
|» spend_limit|body|integer|false|Amount (in cents) to limit approved authorizations (e.g. 100000 would be a $1,000 limit). Transaction requests above the spend limit will be declined. Note that a spend limit of 0 is effectively no limit, and should only be used to reset or remove a prior limit. Only a limit of 1 or above will result in declined transactions due to checks against the card limit.|
|» spend_limit_duration|body|[spend_limit_duration](#schemaspend_limit_duration)|false|Spend limit duration values:<br><br>* `ANNUALLY` - Card will authorize transactions up to spend limit for the trailing year.<br>* `FOREVER` - Card will authorize only up to spend limit for the entire lifetime of the card.<br>* `MONTHLY` - Card will authorize transactions up to spend limit for the trailing month. To support recurring monthly payments, which can occur on different day every month, the time window we consider for monthly velocity starts 6 days after the current calendar date one month prior.<br>* `TRANSACTION` - Card will authorize multiple transactions if each individual transaction is under the spend limit.|
|» state|body|string|false|Card state values:<br>* `OPEN` - Card will approve authorizations (if they match card and account parameters).<br>* `PAUSED` - Card will decline authorizations, but can be resumed at a later time.<br>|
|» tags|body|[tags](#schematags)|false|Key-value pairs to tag the card with. A replacement card does not inherit tags from the card it replaces. A card can have at most 50 tags, with keys up to 40 characters and values up to 500 characters<br>|
|» type|body|string|true|Card types:<br>* `VIRTUAL` - Card will authorize at any merchant and can be added to a digital wallet like Apple Pay or Google Pay (if the card program is digital wallet-enabled).<br>* `PHYSICAL` - Manufactured and sent to the cardholder. We offer white label branding, credit, ATM, PIN debit, chip/EMV, NFC and magstripe functionality. Reach out at [lithic.com/contact](https://lithic.com/contact) for more information.<br>* `SINGLE_USE` - Card is closed upon first successful authorization.<br>* `MERCHANT_LOCKED` - Card is locked to the first merchant that successfully authorizes the card.<br>* `UNLOCKED` - *[Deprecated]* Similar behavior to VIRTUAL cards, please use VIRTUAL instead.<br>* `DIGITAL_WALLET` - *[Deprecated]* Similar behavior to VIRTUAL cards, please use VIRTUAL instead.<br>|

## Update card

<a id="opIdpatchCardByToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/cards/73ca53a1-ae89-491a-97d9-f64788f8b2ab \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "memo": "Updated Name",
    "spend_limit": 100,
    "spend_limit_duration": "FOREVER",
    "state": "OPEN",
    "tags": {
      "risk-level": "high"
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /v1/cards/{card_token}`

Update the specified properties of the card. Unsupplied properties will remain unchanged.

*Note: setting a card to a `CLOSED` state is a final action that cannot be undone.*


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "memo": "Updated Name",
  "spend_limit": 100,
  "spend_limit_duration": "FOREVER",
  "state": "OPEN",
  "tags": {
    "risk-level": "high"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-card-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|card_token|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» digital_card_art_token|body|string(uuid)|false|Specifies the digital card art to be displayed in the user’s digital wallet after tokenization. This artwork must be approved by Mastercard and configured by Lithic to use. See [Flexible Card Art Guide](https://docs.lithic.com/docs/about-digital-wallets#flexible-card-art).|
|» memo|body|string|false|Friendly name to identify the card.|
|» network_program_token|body|string(uuid)|false|Globally unique identifier for the card's network program. Currently applicable to Visa cards participating in Account Level Management only.|
|» pin|body|string|false|Encrypted PIN block (in base64). Only applies to cards of type `PHYSICAL` and `VIRTUAL`. Changing PIN also resets PIN status to `OK`. See [Encrypted PIN Block](https://docs.lithic.com/docs/cards#encrypted-pin-block).|
|» pin_status|body|string|false|Indicates if a card is blocked due a PIN status issue (e.g. excessive incorrect attempts). Can only be set to `OK` to unblock a card.|
|» spend_limit|body|integer|false|Amount (in cents) to limit approved authorizations (e.g. 100000 would be a $1,000 limit). Transaction requests above the spend limit will be declined. Note that a spend limit of 0 is effectively no limit, and should only be used to reset or remove a prior limit. Only a limit of 1 or above will result in declined transactions due to checks against the card limit.|
|» spend_limit_duration|body|[spend_limit_duration](#schemaspend_limit_duration)|false|Spend limit duration values:<br><br>* `ANNUALLY` - Card will authorize transactions up to spend limit for the trailing year.<br>* `FOREVER` - Card will authorize only up to spend limit for the entire lifetime of the card.<br>* `MONTHLY` - Card will authorize transactions up to spend limit for the trailing month. To support recurring monthly payments, which can occur on different day every month, the time window we consider for monthly velocity starts 6 days after the current calendar date one month prior.<br>* `TRANSACTION` - Card will authorize multiple transactions if each individual transaction is under the spend limit.|
|» state|body|string|false|Card state values:<br>* `CLOSED` - Card will no longer approve authorizations. Closing a card cannot be undone.<br>* `OPEN` - Card will approve authorizations (if they match card and account parameters).<br>* `PAUSED` - Card will decline authorizations, but can be resumed at a later time.<br>|
|» tags|body|[tags-patch](#schematags-patch)|false|Key-value pairs to merge into the card's tags. Supplied keys are added or overwritten, a key with a `null` value is removed, and omitted keys remain unchanged. A card can have at most 50 tags, with keys up to 40 characters and values up to 500 characters<br>|
|» substatus|body|string|false|Card state substatus values:<br>* `LOST` - The physical card is no longer in the cardholder's possession due to being lost or never received by the cardholder.<br>* `COMPROMISED` - Card information has been exposed, potentially leading to unauthorized access. This may involve physical card theft, cloning, or online data breaches.<br>* `DAMAGED` - The physical card is not functioning properly, such as having chip failures or a demagnetized magnetic stripe.<br>* `END_USER_REQUEST` - The cardholder requested the closure of the card for reasons unrelated to fraud or damage, such as switching to a different product or closing the account.<br>* `ISSUER_REQUEST` - The issuer closed the card for reasons unrelated to fraud or damage, such as account inactivity, product or policy changes, or technology upgrades.<br>* `NOT_ACTIVE` - The card hasn’t had any transaction activity for a specified period, applicable to statuses like `PAUSED` or `CLOSED`.<br>* `SUSPICIOUS_ACTIVITY` - The card has one or more suspicious transactions or activities that require review. This can involve prompting the cardholder to confirm legitimate use or report confirmed fraud.<br>* `INTERNAL_REVIEW` - The card is temporarily paused pending further internal review.<br>* `EXPIRED` - The card has expired and has been closed without being reissued.<br>* `UNDELIVERABLE` - The card cannot be delivered to the cardholder and has been returned.<br>* `OTHER` - The reason for the status does not fall into any of the above categories. A comment should be provided to specify the reason.<br>|
|» comment|body|string|false|Additional context or information related to the card.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|

|» spend_limit_duration|ANNUALLY|
|» spend_limit_duration|FOREVER|
|» spend_limit_duration|MONTHLY|
|» spend_limit_duration|TRANSACTION|
|» state|CLOSED|
|» state|OPEN|
|» state|PAUSED|
|» substatus|LOST|
|» substatus|COMPROMISED|
|» substatus|DAMAGED|
|» substatus|END_USER_REQUEST|
|» substatus|ISSUER_REQUEST|
|» substatus|NOT_ACTIVE|
|» substatus|SUSPICIOUS_ACTIVITY|

|» substatus|OTHER|

`GET /v1/cards/{card_token}/financial_transactions`

List the financial transactions for a given card.

<h3 id="list-card-financial-transactions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|status|query|string|false|Financial Transaction status to be returned.|
|begin|query|string(date-time)|false|Date string in RFC 3339 format. Only entries created on or after the specified time will be included. UTC time zone.|
|card_token|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|Date string in RFC 3339 format. Only entries created before the specified time will be included. UTC time zone.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor representing an item's token before which a page of results should end. Used to retrieve the previous page of results before this item.|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Page size (for pagination).|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor representing an item's token after which a page of results should begin. Used to retrieve the next page of results after this item.|

## Provision card (Digital Wallet)

<a id="opIdpostCardProvision"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/cards/73ca53a1-ae89-491a-97d9-f64788f8b2ab/provision \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "digital_wallet": "GOOGLE_PAY",
    "client_device_id": "d3538acf-e5df-4446-8ce6-588fa4472ac1",
    "client_wallet_account_id": "d3538acf-e5df-4446-8ce6-588fa4472ac1"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/cards/{card_token}/provision`

Allow your cardholders to directly add payment cards to the device's digital wallet (e.g. Apple Pay) with one touch from your app.

This requires some additional setup and configuration. Please [Contact Us](https://lithic.com/contact) or your Customer Success representative for more information.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "digital_wallet": "GOOGLE_PAY",
  "client_device_id": "d3538acf-e5df-4446-8ce6-588fa4472ac1",
  "client_wallet_account_id": "d3538acf-e5df-4446-8ce6-588fa4472ac1"
}
```

<h3 id="provision-card-digital-wallet-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|card_token|path|string(uuid)|true|The unique token of the card to add to the device's digital wallet.|
|body|body|object|true|Update request.|
|» certificate|body|string(byte)|false|Only applicable if `digital_wallet` is `APPLE_PAY`. Omit to receive only `activationData` in the response. Apple's public leaf certificate. Base64 encoded in PEM format with headers `(-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----)` and trailers omitted. Provided by the device's wallet.|
|» client_wallet_account_id|body|string|false|Only applicable if `digital_wallet` is `GOOGLE_PAY` or `SAMSUNG_PAY`. Consumer ID that identifies the wallet account holder entity. Required for both wallets regardless of network, though the value is only used for cards on the Visa network and is ignored on Amex and Mastercard.|
|» client_device_id|body|string|false|Only applicable if `digital_wallet` is `GOOGLE_PAY` or `SAMSUNG_PAY`. Stable device identification set by the wallet provider. Required for both wallets regardless of network, though the value is only used for cards on the Visa network and is ignored on Amex and Mastercard.|
|» digital_wallet|body|string|false|Name of digital wallet provider.|
|» nonce|body|string(byte)|false|Only applicable if `digital_wallet` is `APPLE_PAY`. Omit to receive only `activationData` in the response. Base64 cryptographic nonce provided by the device's wallet.|

## Web Push Provision card (Digital Wallet)

`POST /v1/cards/{card_token}/web_provision`

Allow your cardholders to directly add payment cards to the device's digital wallet from a browser on the web.

This requires some additional setup and configuration. Please [Contact Us](https://lithic.com/contact) or your Customer Success representative for more information.

```json
}
```

|» client_wallet_account_id|body|string(uuid)|false|Only applicable if `digital_wallet` is GOOGLE_PAY. Google Pay Web Push Provisioning wallet account identifier required for the tokenization flow|
