## Reissue physical card

<a id="opIdpostCardReissue"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/cards/73ca53a1-ae89-491a-97d9-f64788f8b2ab/reissue \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "carrier": {
      "qr_code_url": "https://lithic.com/activate-card/1"
    },
    "product_id": "100",
    "shipping_address": {
      "address1": "5 Broad Street",
      "address2": "Unit 5A",
      "city": "NEW YORK",
      "country": "USA",
      "first_name": "Janet",
      "last_name": "Yellen",
      "postal_code": "10001",
      "state": "NY"
    },
    "shipping_method": "STANDARD"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/cards/{card_token}/reissue`

Initiate print and shipment of a duplicate physical card (e.g. card is physically damaged).  The PAN, expiry, and CVC2 will remain the same and the original card can continue to be used until the new card is activated.
Only applies to cards of type `PHYSICAL`.  A card can be reissued or renewed a total of 8 times.
Returns `409` if the card is still ongoing manufacturing when using Thales as a manufacturer.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "carrier": {
    "qr_code_url": "https://lithic.com/activate-card/1"
  },
  "product_id": "100",
  "shipping_address": {
    "address1": "5 Broad Street",
    "address2": "Unit 5A",
    "city": "NEW YORK",
    "country": "USA",
    "first_name": "Janet",
    "last_name": "Yellen",
    "postal_code": "10001",
    "state": "NY"
  },
  "shipping_method": "STANDARD"
}
```

<h3 id="reissue-physical-card-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|card_token|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» carrier|body|[Carrier](#schemacarrier)|false|If omitted, the previous carrier will be used.|
|» product_id|body|string|false|Specifies the configuration (e.g. physical card art) that the card should be manufactured with, and only applies to cards of type `PHYSICAL`. This must be configured with Lithic before use.<br>|
|» shipping_address|body|[ShippingAddress](#schemashippingaddress)|false|If omitted, the previous shipping address will be used.|
|» shipping_method|body|string|false|Shipping method for the card. Only applies to cards of type PHYSICAL.<br>Use of options besides `STANDARD` require additional permissions.<br><br>* `STANDARD` - USPS regular mail or similar international option, with no tracking<br>* `STANDARD_WITH_TRACKING` - USPS regular mail or similar international option, with tracking<br>* `PRIORITY` - USPS Priority, 1-3 day shipping, with tracking<br>* `EXPRESS` - FedEx or UPS depending on card manufacturer, Express, 3-day shipping, with tracking<br>* `2_DAY` - FedEx or UPS depending on card manufacturer, 2-day shipping, with tracking<br>* `EXPEDITED` - FedEx or UPS depending on card manufacturer, Standard Overnight or similar international option, with tracking<br>* `BULK` - Card will be shipped as part of a bulk fulfillment order. The shipping method and timeline are inherited from the parent bulk order.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» shipping_method|2_DAY|
|» shipping_method|BULK|
|» shipping_method|EXPEDITED|
|» shipping_method|EXPRESS|
|» shipping_method|PRIORITY|
|» shipping_method|STANDARD|
|» shipping_method|STANDARD_WITH_TRACKING|

## Renew a card

<a id="opIdpostCardRenew"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/cards/73ca53a1-ae89-491a-97d9-f64788f8b2ab/renew \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "carrier": {
      "qr_code_url": "https://lithic.com/activate-card/1"
    },
    "product_id": "100",
    "shipping_address": {
      "address1": "5 Broad Street",
      "address2": "Unit 5A",
      "city": "NEW YORK",
      "country": "USA",
      "first_name": "Janet",
      "last_name": "Yellen",
      "postal_code": "10001",
      "state": "NY"
    },
    "shipping_method": "STANDARD"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/cards/{card_token}/renew`

Applies to card types `PHYSICAL` and `VIRTUAL`.
For `PHYSICAL`, creates a new card with the same card token and PAN, but updated expiry and CVC2 code. The original card will keep working for card-present transactions until the new card is activated. For card-not-present transactions, the original card details (expiry, CVC2) will also keep working until the new card is activated.
A `PHYSICAL` card can be reissued or renewed a total of 8 times.
For `VIRTUAL`, the card will retain the same card token and PAN and receive an updated expiry and CVC2 code.
`product_id`, `shipping_method`, `shipping_address`, `carrier` are only relevant for renewing `PHYSICAL` cards.
Returns `409` if the card is still ongoing manufacturing when using Thales as a manufacturer.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "carrier": {
    "qr_code_url": "https://lithic.com/activate-card/1"
  },
  "product_id": "100",
  "shipping_address": {
    "address1": "5 Broad Street",
    "address2": "Unit 5A",
    "city": "NEW YORK",
    "country": "USA",
    "first_name": "Janet",
    "last_name": "Yellen",
    "postal_code": "10001",
    "state": "NY"
  },
  "shipping_method": "STANDARD"
}
```

<h3 id="renew-a-card-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|card_token|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» carrier|body|[Carrier](#schemacarrier)|false|If omitted, the previous carrier will be used.|
|» exp_month|body|string|false|Two digit (MM) expiry month. If neither `exp_month` nor `exp_year` is provided, an expiration date five years in the future will be generated. Five years is the maximum expiration date.|
|» exp_year|body|string|false|Four digit (yyyy) expiry year. If neither `exp_month` nor `exp_year` is provided, an expiration date five years in the future will be generated. Five years is the maximum expiration date.|
|» product_id|body|string|false|Specifies the configuration (e.g. physical card art) that the card should be manufactured with, and only applies to cards of type `PHYSICAL`. This must be configured with Lithic before use.<br>|
|» shipping_address|body|[ShippingAddress](#schemashippingaddress)|true|The shipping address this card will be sent to.|
|» shipping_method|body|string|false|Shipping method for the card. Only applies to cards of type PHYSICAL.<br>Use of options besides `STANDARD` require additional permissions.<br><br>* `STANDARD` - USPS regular mail or similar international option, with no tracking<br>* `STANDARD_WITH_TRACKING` - USPS regular mail or similar international option, with tracking<br>* `PRIORITY` - USPS Priority, 1-3 day shipping, with tracking<br>* `EXPRESS` - FedEx or UPS depending on card manufacturer, Express, 3-day shipping, with tracking<br>* `2_DAY` - FedEx or UPS depending on card manufacturer, 2-day shipping, with tracking<br>* `EXPEDITED` - FedEx or UPS depending on card manufacturer, Standard Overnight or similar international option, with tracking<br>* `BULK` - Card will be shipped as part of a bulk fulfillment order. The shipping method and timeline are inherited from the parent bulk order.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» shipping_method|2_DAY|
|» shipping_method|BULK|
|» shipping_method|EXPEDITED|
|» shipping_method|EXPRESS|
|» shipping_method|PRIORITY|
|» shipping_method|STANDARD|
|» shipping_method|STANDARD_WITH_TRACKING|

`POST /v1/cards/{card_token}/reassign_account`

Reassigns a card to another account. The card must be in an `OPEN` or `PAUSED` state, and the destination account must be in an `ACTIVE` state.

Clients must contact their Lithic account manager for access to this endpoint.

## Convert virtual to physical card

<a id="opIdpostConvertPhysical"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/cards/73ca53a1-ae89-491a-97d9-f64788f8b2ab/convert_physical \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "carrier": {
      "qr_code_url": "https://lithic.com/activate-card/1"
    },
    "product_id": "100",
    "shipping_address": {
      "address1": "5 Broad Street",
      "address2": "Unit 5A",
      "city": "NEW YORK",
      "country": "USA",
      "first_name": "Janet",
      "last_name": "Yellen",
      "postal_code": "10001",
      "state": "NY"
    },
    "shipping_method": "STANDARD"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/cards/{card_token}/convert_physical`

Convert a virtual card into a physical card and manufacture it.
Customer must supply relevant fields for physical card creation including `product_id`, `carrier`, `shipping_method`, and `shipping_address`.
The card token will be unchanged.  The card's type will be altered to `PHYSICAL`.
The card will be set to state `PENDING_FULFILLMENT` and fulfilled at next fulfillment cycle.
Virtual cards created on card programs which do not support physical cards cannot be converted.  The card program cannot be changed as part of the conversion.  Cards must be in an `OPEN` state to be converted.
Only applies to cards of type `VIRTUAL` (or existing cards with deprecated types of `DIGITAL_WALLET` and `UNLOCKED`).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "carrier": {
    "qr_code_url": "https://lithic.com/activate-card/1"
  },
  "product_id": "100",
  "shipping_address": {
    "address1": "5 Broad Street",
    "address2": "Unit 5A",
    "city": "NEW YORK",
    "country": "USA",
    "first_name": "Janet",
    "last_name": "Yellen",
    "postal_code": "10001",
    "state": "NY"
  },
  "shipping_method": "STANDARD"
}
```

<h3 id="convert-virtual-to-physical-card-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|card_token|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» carrier|body|[Carrier](#schemacarrier)|false|If omitted, the previous carrier will be used.|
|» product_id|body|string|false|Specifies the configuration (e.g. physical card art) that the card should be manufactured with, and only applies to cards of type `PHYSICAL`. This must be configured with Lithic before use.<br>|
|» shipping_address|body|[ShippingAddress](#schemashippingaddress)|true|The shipping address this card will be sent to.|
|» shipping_method|body|string|false|Shipping method for the card. Only applies to cards of type PHYSICAL.<br>Use of options besides `STANDARD` require additional permissions.<br><br>* `STANDARD` - USPS regular mail or similar international option, with no tracking<br>* `STANDARD_WITH_TRACKING` - USPS regular mail or similar international option, with tracking<br>* `PRIORITY` - USPS Priority, 1-3 day shipping, with tracking<br>* `EXPRESS` - FedEx or UPS depending on card manufacturer, Express, 3-day shipping, with tracking<br>* `2_DAY` - FedEx or UPS depending on card manufacturer, 2-day shipping, with tracking<br>* `EXPEDITED` - FedEx or UPS depending on card manufacturer, Standard Overnight or similar international option, with tracking<br>* `BULK` - Card will be shipped as part of a bulk fulfillment order. The shipping method and timeline are inherited from the parent bulk order.<br>|

|» shipping_method|EXPEDITED|
|» shipping_method|EXPRESS|
|» shipping_method|PRIORITY|
|» shipping_method|STANDARD|
|» shipping_method|STANDARD_WITH_TRACKING|

`GET /v1/cards/{card_token}/spend_limits`

Get a Card's available spend limit, which is based on the spend limit configured on the Card and the amount already spent over the spend limit's duration. For example, if the Card has a monthly spend limit of $1000 configured, and has spent $600 in the last month, the available spend limit returned would be $400.

## Create card embed session

<a id="opIdcreateCardEmbedSession"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/cards/73ca53a1-ae89-491a-97d9-f64788f8b2ab/embed \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "target_origin": "https://example.com",
    "type": "CARD_EMBED"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/cards/{card_token}/embed`

Creates a short-lived session for displaying card details or setting a card PIN in
Lithic-hosted iframes. Create the session on your backend to not expose your API key in browser code.

A session token can only be used to reveal card details (per embed type) or submit a pin a single time. Attempting to
re-use session tokens will result in 401's.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "target_origin": "https://example.com",
  "type": "CARD_EMBED"
}
```

<h3 id="create-card-embed-session-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|card_token|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|[create-embed-session-request](#schemacreate-embed-session-request)|true|Card embed session parameters.|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of card embed session to create.<br><br>`CARD_EMBED` sessions can load `PAN`, `CVV`, `EXP_MONTH`, and `EXP_YEAR` iframes.<br><br>`PIN_SETTING_EMBED` sessions can load only the `PIN_SETTING` iframe.<br>|
|» expiration|body|integer(int64)|false|Unix timestamp at which the session expires. The value must be in the future and no more than<br>10 minutes after the request. If omitted, the session expires 10 minutes after the request.<br>|
|» max_pin_length|body|integer|false|Maximum number of digits accepted by a `PIN_SETTING_EMBED`. The value must be from 4 through 8<br>and defaults to 8. This parameter is not supported for `CARD_EMBED` sessions and will be rejected<br>|
|» target_origin|body|string(uri)|true|Canonical HTTPS origin of the page that will embed the iframe. Lithic embeds will verify the `target_origin` against the parent application's origin.<br>The origin must not contain a path, query parameters, fragment, or credentials.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|CARD_EMBED|
|» type|PIN_SETTING_EMBED|

## Embedded card UI

<a id="opIdgetEmbedCard"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/embed/card?embed_request=string&hmac=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v1/embed/card`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

**Deprecated.** Use the modern embedded card flow instead: create a session with `POST /v1/cards/{card_token}/embed` and render it via `GET /v1/embed`.

Handling full card PANs and CVV codes requires that you comply with the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standards (PCI DSS). Some clients choose to reduce their compliance obligations by leveraging our embedded card UI solution documented below.

In this setup, PANs and CVV codes are presented to the end-user via a card UI that we provide, optionally styled in the customer's branding using a specified css stylesheet. A user's browser makes the request directly to api.lithic.com, so card PANs and CVVs never touch the API customer's servers while full card data is displayed to their end-users. The response contains an HTML document (see Embedded Card UI or Changelog for upcoming changes in January). This means that the url for the request can be inserted straight into the `src` attribute of an iframe.

```html
<iframe id="card-iframe"
        src="https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/embed/card?embed_request=eyJjc3MiO...;hmac=r8tx1..."
        allow="clipboard-write" class="content"></iframe>
```

You should compute the request payload on the server side. You can render it (or the whole iframe) on the server or make an ajax call from your front end code, but **do not ever embed your API key into front end code, as doing so introduces a serious security vulnerability**.


<h3 id="embedded-card-ui-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|embed_request|query|string|true|A base64 encoded JSON string of an EmbedRequest to specify which card to load.|
|hmac|query|string|true|SHA256 HMAC of the embed_request JSON string with base64 digest.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```text
<html>
<head>
<link rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" href="https://demo.lithic.com/backend/embedded.css">
<style>
    #alert { display: none; }
</style>
<script type="text/javascript">
    var timeout;

    function clearAlertDelay() {
        clearTimeout(timeout);
        var messageDiv = document.getElementById('alert');
        timeout = window.setTimeout(
            function() {
                messageDiv.className = "empty";
                messageDiv.innerText = "";
            },
            1200
        );
    }

    function copySuccess(divId) {
        var messageDiv = document.getElementById('alert');
        messageDiv.innerText = divId + " copied to clipboard";
        messageDiv.className = "success";
        console.log('Copying to clipboard was successful!');
        clearAlertDelay();
    }

    function copyFailed(divId) {
        var messageDiv = document.getElementById('alert');
        messageDiv.innerText = "error copying " + divId;
        messageDiv.className = "error";
        console.error('Copying to clipboard failed');
        clearAlertDelay();
    }

    function copyToClip(divId) {
        var messageDiv = document.getElementById('alert');
        var copyEl = document.getElementById(divId);
        var copyText = copyEl.textContent;
        navigator.clipboard.writeText(copyText)
            .then(function () {
                copySuccess(divId);
                clearAlertDelay();
            })
            .catch(function(err) {
                try {
                    var copied = false;
                    if (document.createRange) {
                        range = document.createRange();
                        range.selectNode(copyEl)
                        select = window.getSelection();
                        select.removeAllRanges();
                        select.addRange(range);
                        copied = document.execCommand('copy');
                        select.removeAllRanges();
                    }
                    else {
                        range = document.body.createTextRange();
                        range.moveToElementText(copyEl);
                        range.select();
                        copied = document.execCommand('copy');
                    }

                    if (copied) {
                        copySuccess(divId);
                    }
                    else {
                        copyFailed(divId);
                    }
                }
                catch (err) {
                    copyFailed(divId);
                }
                clearAlertDelay();
            })
    }
</script>
</head>
<body>
    <div id="card">
        <div id="pan" onclick="copyToClip('pan')">9999<span class='pan-separator'></span>9999<span class='pan-separator'></span>9999<span class='pan-separator'></span>9999</div>
        <div id="expiry">
            <span id="month" onclick="copyToClip('month')">08</span>
            <span id="separator">/</span>
            <span id="year" onclick="copyToClip('year')">27</span>
        </div>
        <div id="cvv" onclick="copyToClip('cvv')">574</div>
        <div id="alert" class="empty"></div>
    </div>
</body>
</html>

```

## Get card embed iframe

<a id="opIdgetCardEmbed"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/embed?session=eyJhb...&type=PAN' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /v1/embed`

Returns a Lithic-hosted HTML document for a single card detail or PIN setting control. Use
the URL, including its query parameters, as the `src` of an iframe. The session must be created
on your server with `POST /v1/cards/{card_token}/embed`.


<h3 id="get-card-embed-iframe-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|session|query|string|true|The short-lived credential returned by the session creation endpoint. Treat it as<br>sensitive and use it only in the iframe `src`.<br>|
|type|query|string|true|The type of embed to return.<br>`CARD_EMBED` sessions support `PAN`, `CVV`, `EXP_MONTH`, and `EXP_YEAR`.<br>`PIN_SETTING_EMBED` sessions support only `PIN_SETTING`.<br>|
|styles|query|string(byte)|false|Optional base64-encoded JSON object containing base CSS declarations and nested<br>pseudo-class declarations to apply to the iframe. URL-encode the base64 value when<br>adding it to the query string. Styles that load external resources are not permitted.<br>The encoded value cannot exceed 4096 characters.<br><br>Supported pseudo-classes are `:first-child`, `:last-child`, `:enabled`, `:read-write`,<br>`:read-only`, `:placeholder-shown`, `:valid`, `:invalid`, `:disabled`, `:hover`,<br>`:focus-within`, `:focus`, `:focus-visible`, and `:active`.<br>|
|configuration|query|string(byte)|false|Optional standard base64-encoded JSON configuration for the requested iframe. URL-encode<br>the base64 value when adding it to the query string. The encoded value cannot exceed 4096<br>characters; malformed or oversized values are rejected with a `400` response.<br><br>`PIN_SETTING` supports a `pin_setting` object with an optional `placeholder` string and an<br>optional `layout`. `placeholder` defaults to an empty string and applies only to the<br>single-input layout. `layout` accepts `SINGLE_INPUT` or `MULTI_INPUT` and defaults to<br>`SINGLE_INPUT`. The multi-input layout renders one single-digit input for each digit allowed<br>by the embed session's `max_pin_length`.<br><br>Decoded example: `{"pin_setting":{"layout":"MULTI_INPUT"}}`<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|type|PAN|
|type|CVV|
|type|EXP_MONTH|
|type|EXP_YEAR|
|type|PIN_SETTING|

## Respond to Authorization Challenge

<a id="opIdrespondToAuthorizationChallenge"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/card_authorizations/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/challenge_response \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "response": "APPROVE"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/card_authorizations/{event_token}/challenge_response`

Card program's response to Authorization Challenge.
Programs that have Authorization Challenges configured as Out of Band receive a [card_authorization.challenge](https://docs.lithic.com/reference/cardauthorizationchallengewebhook) webhook when an authorization attempt triggers a challenge.
The card program should respond using this endpoint after the cardholder completes the challenge.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "response": "APPROVE"
}
```

<h3 id="respond-to-authorization-challenge-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event_token|path|string(uuid)|true|Globally unique identifier for the authorization event that triggered the challenge|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» response|body|string|true|Whether the cardholder has approved or declined the issued challenge|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» response|APPROVE|
|» response|DECLINE|

<h3 id="respond-to-authorization-challenge-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Challenge response recorded|None|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request (e.g. challenge method does not support this endpoint)|None|
|404|Not Found|Challenge not found|None|
|409|Conflict|Challenge has already been completed|None|
|410|Gone|Challenge has expired|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Lithic Error|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth
</aside>

`POST /v1/card_bulk_orders`

Create a new bulk order for physical card shipments. Cards can be added to the order via the POST /v1/cards endpoint by specifying the bulk_order_token. Lock the order via PATCH /v1/card_bulk_orders/{bulk_order_token} to prepare for shipment. Please work with your Customer Success Manager and card personalization bureau to ensure bulk shipping is supported for your program.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "shipping_address": {
    "address1": "123 Main Street",
    "city": "NEW YORK",
    "country": "USA",
    "first_name": "Johnny",
    "last_name": "Appleseed",
    "postal_code": "10001",
    "state": "NY"
  },
  "shipping_method": "BULK_EXPEDITED",
  "customer_product_id": "custom-card-design-123"
}
```

|» shipping_method|body|string|true|Shipping method for all cards in this bulk order. BULK_PRIORITY, BULK_2_DAY, and BULK_EXPRESS are only available with Perfect Plastic Printing|
|» customer_product_id|body|string|true|Customer-specified product configuration for physical card manufacturing. This must be configured with Lithic before use|

`POST /v1/disputes/{dispute_token}/evidences`

Use this endpoint to upload evidence for a chargeback request. It will return a URL to upload your documents to. The URL will expire in 30 minutes.

Uploaded documents must either be a `jpg`, `png` or `pdf` file, and each must be less than 5 GiB.

```json
}
```

## Set verification method

<a id="opIdsetVerificationMethod"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/external_bank_accounts/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/set_verification_method \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "verification_method": "MICRO_DEPOSIT",

  }'
```

`POST /v1/external_bank_accounts/{external_bank_account_token}/set_verification_method`

Update the verification method for an external bank account. Verification method can only be updated
if the `verification_state` is `PENDING`.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "verification_method": "MICRO_DEPOSIT",
  "financial_account_token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
}
```

|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor representing an item's token before which a page of results should end. Used to retrieve the previous page of results before this item.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|Date string in RFC 3339 format. Only entries created before the specified time will be included. UTC time zone.|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Page size (for pagination).|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor representing an item's token after which a page of results should begin. Used to retrieve the next page of results after this item.|

```bash
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /v1/financial_accounts/{financial_account_token}/credit_configuration`

Update an account's credit configuration. A credit product can only be
attached while the financial account is in the `PENDING` state; once a
credit product has been assigned the account transitions to `OPEN` and
`credit_product_token` can no longer be changed

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "credit_limit": 0,
  "external_bank_account_token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "credit_product_token": "string",
  "tier": "string",
  "auto_collection_configuration": {
    "auto_collection_enabled": true
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-account-credit-configuration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|financial_account_token|path|string(uuid)|true|Globally unique identifier for financial account.|
|body|body|[financial-account-credit-config-request](#schemafinancial-account-credit-config-request)|false|none|
|» credit_limit|body|integer|false|none|
|» external_bank_account_token|body|string(uuid)|false|none|
|» credit_product_token|body|string|false|Globally unique identifier for the credit product. This can only be set<br>while the financial account is in the `PENDING` state. Because assigning a<br>credit product transitions the account to `OPEN`, a credit product can be<br>attached only once; updating it on an account in any other state returns a<br>`403`|
|» tier|body|string|false|Tier to assign to a financial account|
|» auto_collection_configuration|body|[auto-collection-configuration-request](#schemaauto-collection-configuration-request)|false|none|

## Create or update a fraud report for a transaction

<a id="opIdcreateUpdateFraudReport"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/fraud/transactions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "fraud_status": "SUSPECTED_FRAUD",
    "fraud_type": "FIRST_PARTY_FRAUD",
    "comment": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/fraud/transactions/{transaction_token}`

Report fraud for a specific transaction token by providing details such as fraud type, fraud status, and any additional comments.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "fraud_status": "SUSPECTED_FRAUD",
  "fraud_type": "FIRST_PARTY_FRAUD",
  "comment": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-a-fraud-report-for-a-transaction-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|transaction_token|path|string(uuid)|true|The token of the transaction that the enhanced data is associated with.|
|body|body|[fraud-report-request](#schemafraud-report-request)|true|The details of the fraud report to create or update.|
|» fraud_status|body|string|true|The fraud status of the transaction, string (enum) supporting the following values:<br><br> - `SUSPECTED_FRAUD`: The transaction is suspected to be fraudulent, but this hasn’t been confirmed.<br> - `FRAUDULENT`: The transaction is confirmed to be fraudulent. A transaction may immediately be moved into this state, or be graduated into this state from the `SUSPECTED_FRAUD` state.<br> - `NOT_FRAUDULENT`: The transaction is (explicitly) marked as not fraudulent. A transaction may immediately be moved into this state, or be graduated into this state from the `SUSPECTED_FRAUD` state.|
|» fraud_type|body|string|false|Specifies the type or category of fraud that the transaction is suspected or confirmed to involve, string (enum) supporting the following values:<br><br> - `FIRST_PARTY_FRAUD`: First-party fraud occurs when a legitimate account or cardholder intentionally misuses financial services for personal gain. This includes actions such as disputing legitimate transactions to obtain a refund, abusing return policies, or defaulting on credit obligations without intent to repay.<br> - `ACCOUNT_TAKEOVER`: Account takeover fraud occurs when a fraudster gains unauthorized access to an existing account, modifies account settings, and carries out fraudulent transactions.<br> - `CARD_COMPROMISED`: Card compromised fraud occurs when a fraudster gains access to card details without taking over the account, such as through physical card theft, cloning, or online data breaches.<br> - `IDENTITY_THEFT`: Identity theft fraud occurs when a fraudster uses stolen personal information, such as Social Security numbers or addresses, to open accounts, apply for loans, or conduct financial transactions in someone's name.<br> - `CARDHOLDER_MANIPULATION`: This type of fraud occurs when a fraudster manipulates or coerces a legitimate cardholder into unauthorized transactions, often through social engineering tactics.|
|» comment|body|string|false|Optional field providing additional information or context about why the transaction is considered fraudulent.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» fraud_status|SUSPECTED_FRAUD|
|» fraud_status|FRAUDULENT|
|» fraud_status|NOT_FRAUDULENT|
|» fraud_type|FIRST_PARTY_FRAUD|
|» fraud_type|ACCOUNT_TAKEOVER|
|» fraud_type|CARD_COMPROMISED|
|» fraud_type|IDENTITY_THEFT|
|» fraud_type|CARDHOLDER_MANIPULATION|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "transaction_token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "fraud_status": "SUSPECTED_FRAUD",
  "fraud_type": "FIRST_PARTY_FRAUD",
  "comment": "string",
  "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",

}
```

## Create hold

<a id="opIdcreateHold"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/financial_accounts/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/holds \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "amount": 1,
    "memo": "string",
    "token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "expiration_datetime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "user_defined_id": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/financial_accounts/{financial_account_token}/holds`

Create a hold on a financial account. Holds reserve funds by moving them
from available to pending balance. They can be resolved via settlement
(linked to a payment or book transfer), voiding, or expiration.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "amount": 1,
  "memo": "string",
  "token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "expiration_datetime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "user_defined_id": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-hold-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|financial_account_token|path|string(uuid)|true|Globally unique identifier for the financial account.|
|body|body|[create_hold_request](#schemacreate_hold_request)|true|none|
|» amount|body|integer|true|Amount to hold in cents|
|» memo|body|string \| null|false|Reason for the hold|
|» token|body|string(uuid)|false|Customer-provided token for idempotency. Becomes the hold token.|
|» expiration_datetime|body|string(date-time)|false|When the hold should auto-expire|
|» user_defined_id|body|string|false|User-provided identifier for the hold|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "created": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "updated": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "family": "HOLD",
  "result": "APPROVED",
  "status": "PENDING",
  "financial_account_token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "pending_amount": 0,
  "currency": "string",
  "events": [
    {
      "token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
      "type": "HOLD_INITIATED",
      "result": "APPROVED",
      "detailed_results": [
        "APPROVED"
      ],
      "amount": 0,
      "created": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "memo": "string",
      "settling_transaction_token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
    }
  ],
  "user_defined_id": "string",
  "expiration_datetime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json

  "debugging_request_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "message": "string"
}
```

## Void hold

<a id="opIdvoidHold"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/holds/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/void \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "memo": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/holds/{hold_token}/void`

Void an active hold. This returns the held funds from pending back to
available balance. Only holds in PENDING status can be voided.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "memo": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="void-hold-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|hold_token|path|string(uuid)|true|Globally unique identifier for the hold.|
|body|body|[void_hold_request](#schemavoid_hold_request)|true|none|
|» memo|body|string \| null|false|Reason for voiding the hold|

> Example responses

## List disputes

<a id="opIdgetDisputesV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v2/disputes \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v2/disputes`

Returns a paginated list of disputes.

<h3 id="list-disputes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|begin|query|string(date-time)|false|RFC 3339 timestamp for filtering by created date, inclusive.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|RFC 3339 timestamp for filtering by created date, inclusive.|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Number of items to return.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor representing an item's token after which a page of results should begin. Used to retrieve the next page of results after this item.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor representing an item's token before which a page of results should end. Used to retrieve the previous page of results before this item.|
|disputed_transaction_token|query|string(uuid)|false|Filter by the token of the transaction being disputed. Corresponds with transaction_series.related_transaction_token in the Dispute.|
|claim_token|query|string(uuid)|false|Filter by the token of the claim the dispute was filed under. Returns the disputes created from that claim's disputed transaction events.|
|card_token|query|string(uuid)|false|Filter by card token.|
|account_token|query|string(uuid)|false|Filter by account token.|

## Create payment

<a id="opIdcreatePayment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/payments \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "amount": 1,
    "external_bank_account_token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "financial_account_token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "memo": "string",
    "method": "ACH_NEXT_DAY",
    "method_attributes": {
      "sec_code": "CCD",
      "ach_hold_period": 0,
```

`POST /v1/payments`

Initiates an ACH payment between a financial account and an external bank account.

This endpoint originates on the ACH rail only. To send a stablecoin payout, use the
[Create stablecoin payment](https://docs.lithic.com/reference/createstablecoinpayment)
endpoint. Payments on every rail are read back through
[List payments](https://docs.lithic.com/reference/searchpayments).


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "amount": 1,
  "external_bank_account_token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "financial_account_token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "memo": "string",
  "method": "ACH_NEXT_DAY",
  "method_attributes": {
    "sec_code": "CCD",
    "ach_hold_period": 0,
    "addenda": "string",
    "override_company_name": "string"

  "token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "type": "COLLECTION",
  "user_defined_id": "string",
  "hold": {

}
```

## Create stablecoin payment

<a id="opIdcreateStablecoinPayment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/payments/stablecoin \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "amount": 1588,
    "blockchain_recipient_token": "1e3fdb71-4b52-4a30-a7a9-52c85e26a1d9",
    "financial_account_token": "35b0c466-a3e3-519a-9549-ead6a6a2277d",
    "memo": "Vendor payout",
    "type": "PAYMENT"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/payments/stablecoin`

Initiates a stablecoin payout from a financial account to a registered blockchain recipient.

The recipient must have been registered with
[Create blockchain recipient](https://docs.lithic.com/reference/createblockchainrecipient) and
have completed address screening — only a recipient in the `ENABLED` verification state can
receive a payout. The destination address and chain come from the recipient, so they are not
supplied here.

Only payouts are initiated through this endpoint. Stablecoin pay-ins are credited from
on-chain deposits to a financial account's deposit address and are not created through the
API. Funds are placed on hold when the payout is initiated, and a payout that fails on chain
reverses that hold. A payout cannot be cancelled once it has been submitted on chain.

This endpoint is only available to stablecoin-enabled programs. Contact your customer success
manager to learn more.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "amount": 1588,
  "blockchain_recipient_token": "1e3fdb71-4b52-4a30-a7a9-52c85e26a1d9",
  "financial_account_token": "35b0c466-a3e3-519a-9549-ead6a6a2277d",
  "memo": "Vendor payout",
  "type": "PAYMENT"
}
```

<h3 id="create-stablecoin-payment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateStablecoinPaymentRequest](#schemacreatestablecoinpaymentrequest)|true|none|
|» amount|body|integer|true|Payout amount in cents|
|» blockchain_recipient_token|body|string(uuid)|true|Token of the blockchain recipient to send the payout to. The recipient must be in the `ENABLED` verification state|
|» financial_account_token|body|string(uuid)|true|Token of the financial account the payout is funded from|
|» hold|body|object|false|Optional hold to settle when this payout is initiated|
|» » token|body|string(uuid)|true|Token of the hold to settle when this payout is initiated|
|» memo|body|string|false|Memo recorded on the payout. Defaults to `Stablecoin payout on <chain>` when omitted|
|» token|body|string(uuid)|false|Customer-provided token that will serve as an idempotency token. This token will become the transaction token|
|» type|body|string|true|Direction of the payment. Stablecoin supports payouts only|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|PAYMENT|

## Return payment

<a id="opIdreturnPayment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/payments/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/return \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "financial_account_token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "return_reason_code": "R01",
    "memo": "string",
    "addenda": "string",
    "date_of_death": "2025-01-15"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/payments/{payment_token}/return`

Return an ACH payment with a specified return reason code. Returns must be initiated
within the time window specified by NACHA rules for each return code (typically 2 banking
days for most codes, 60 calendar days for unauthorized debits). For a complete list of
return codes and their meanings, see the [ACH Return Reasons documentation](https://docs.lithic.com/docs/ach-overview#ach-return-reasons).

Note:
  * This endpoint does not modify the state of the financial account associated with the payment. If you would like to change the account state, use the [Update financial account status](https://docs.lithic.com/reference/updatefinancialaccountstatus) endpoint.
  * By default this endpoint is not enabled for your account. Please contact your implementations manager to enable this feature.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "financial_account_token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "return_reason_code": "R01",
  "memo": "string",
  "addenda": "string",
  "date_of_death": "2025-01-15"
}
```

<h3 id="return-payment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|payment_token|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|[payment_return_request](#schemapayment_return_request)|false|none|
|» financial_account_token|body|string(uuid)|true|Globally unique identifier for the financial account|
|» return_reason_code|body|string|true|ACH return reason code indicating the reason for returning the payment. Supported codes include R01-R53 and R80-R85. For a complete list of return codes and their meanings, see [ACH Return Reasons](https://docs.lithic.com/docs/ach-overview#ach-return-reasons)|
|» memo|body|string \| null|false|Optional memo for the return. Limited to 10 characters|
|» addenda|body|string \| null|false|Optional additional information about the return. Limited to 44 characters|
|» date_of_death|body|string \| null(date)|false|Date of death in YYYY-MM-DD format. Required when using return codes **R14** (representative payee deceased) or **R15** (beneficiary or account holder deceased)|

> Example responses

## List Lithic IP ranges

<a id="opIdgetIpRanges"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/ip_ranges \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /v1/ip_ranges`

Returns the IP addresses Lithic sends responder requests from (Auth Stream Access, 3DS decisioning, and tokenization decisioning), so you can allowlist them in your firewall. Each environment returns its own set of addresses. Lithic announces new addresses at least 30 days before sending traffic from them. Event webhooks are not sent from these addresses

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "responders": [
    "3.130.20.154/32",
    "18.227.57.16/32"
  ],
  "updated": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "debugging_request_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "message": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="list-lithic-ip-ranges-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Lithic IP ranges|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Client has exceeded the number of allowed requests in a given time period.<br><br>\|   \|   \|<br>\|---\|---\|<br>\| Rate limited, too many requests per second \| User has exceeded their per second rate limit \|<br>\| Rate limited, reached daily limit \| User has exceeded their daily rate limit \|<br>\| Rate limited, too many keys tried \| One IP has queried too many different API keys \|<br>|[error](#schemaerror)|

<h3 id="list-lithic-ip-ranges-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|responders|[string]|true|none|IP ranges that responder requests are sent from, in CIDR notation|
|updated|string(date-time)|true|none|Date and time the IP ranges were last changed|

`GET /v1/reports/settlement/network_totals`

List network total records with optional filters. Not available in sandbox.

<h3 id="list-network-totals-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|report_date|query|string(date)|false|Singular report date to filter on (YYYY-MM-DD). Cannot be populated in conjunction with report_date_begin or report_date_end.|
|report_date_begin|query|string(date)|false|Earliest report date to filter on, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD).|
|report_date_end|query|string(date)|false|Latest report date to filter on, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD).|
|network|query|string|false|Network to filter on.|
|institution_id|query|string|false|Institution ID to filter on.|
|settlement_institution_id|query|string|false|Settlement institution ID to filter on.|
|begin|query|string(date-time)|false|Datetime in RFC 3339 format. Only entries created on or after the specified time will be included. UTC time zone.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|Datetime in RFC 3339 format. Only entries created before the specified time will be included. UTC time zone.|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Number of records per page.|
|starting_after|query|string(uuid)|false|A cursor representing an item's token after which a page of results should begin. Used to retrieve the next page of results after this item.|
|ending_before|query|string(uuid)|false|A cursor representing an item's token before which a page of results should end. Used to retrieve the previous page of results before this item.|

## List interest tier schedules

<a id="opIdlistInterestTierSchedules"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/financial_accounts/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/interest_tier_schedule \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v1/financial_accounts/{financial_account_token}/interest_tier_schedule`

List interest tier schedules for a financial account with optional date filtering.

If no date parameters are provided, returns all tier schedules.
If date parameters are provided, uses filtering to return matching schedules (max 100).
- for_date: Returns exact match (takes precedence over other dates)
- before_date: Returns schedules with effective_date <= before_date
- after_date: Returns schedules with effective_date >= after_date
- Both before_date and after_date: Returns schedules in range

<h3 id="list-interest-tier-schedules-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|after_date|query|string(date)|false|Return schedules with effective_date >= after_date (ISO format YYYY-MM-DD)|
|before_date|query|string(date)|false|Return schedules with effective_date <= before_date (ISO format YYYY-MM-DD)|
|financial_account_token|path|string(uuid)|true|Globally unique identifier for financial account|
|for_date|query|string(date)|false|Return schedule with effective_date == for_date (ISO format YYYY-MM-DD)|

> Example responses

## Delete interest tier schedule

<a id="opIddeleteInterestTierSchedule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/financial_accounts/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/interest_tier_schedule/1970-01-01 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /v1/financial_accounts/{financial_account_token}/interest_tier_schedule/{effective_date}`

Delete an interest tier schedule entry.

Returns:
- 400 Bad Request: Invalid effective_date format OR attempting to delete the earliest
  tier schedule entry for a non-PENDING account
- 404 Not Found: Tier schedule entry not found for the given effective_date OR ledger account not found

Note: PENDING accounts can delete the earliest tier schedule entry (account hasn't opened yet).
Active/non-PENDING accounts cannot delete the earliest entry to prevent orphaning the account.

If the deleted tier schedule has a past effective_date and the account is ACTIVE,
the loan tape rebuild configuration will be updated to trigger rebuilds from that date.

<h3 id="delete-interest-tier-schedule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|effective_date|path|string(date)|true|Effective date in ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD)|
|financial_account_token|path|string(uuid)|true|Globally unique identifier for financial account|

## Simulate a card's tokenization

<a id="opIdpostSimulateTokenizations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/simulate/tokenizations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "account_score": 5,
    "cvv": "776",
    "device_score": 5,
    "expiration_date": "08/29",
    "pan": "4111111289144142",
    "tokenization_source": "APPLE_PAY",
    "wallet_recommended_decision": "APPROVED"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/simulate/tokenizations`

This endpoint is used to simulate a card's tokenization in the Digital Wallet and merchant tokenization ecosystem.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "account_score": 5,
  "cvv": "776",
  "device_score": 5,
  "expiration_date": "08/29",
  "pan": "4111111289144142",
  "tokenization_source": "APPLE_PAY",
  "wallet_recommended_decision": "APPROVED"
}
```

<h3 id="simulate-a-cards-tokenization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» account_score|body|integer|false|The account score (1-5) that represents how the Digital Wallet's view on how reputable an end user's account is.|
|» cvv|body|string|true|The three or four digit CVV for the card. AMEX cards use four digit CVVs.|
|» device_score|body|integer|false|The device score (1-5) that represents how the Digital Wallet's view on how reputable an end user's device is.|
|» entity|body|string|false|Optional field to specify the token requestor name for a merchant token simulation. Ignored when tokenization_source is not MERCHANT.|
|» expiration_date|body|string|true|The expiration date of the card in 'MM/YY' format.|
|» pan|body|string|true|The sixteen digit card number.|
|» tokenization_source|body|string|true|The source of the tokenization request.|
|» wallet_recommended_decision|body|string|false|The decision that the Digital Wallet's recommend|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» tokenization_source|APPLE_PAY|
|» tokenization_source|GOOGLE|
|» tokenization_source|SAMSUNG_PAY|
|» tokenization_source|MERCHANT|
|» wallet_recommended_decision|APPROVED|
|» wallet_recommended_decision|DECLINED|
|» wallet_recommended_decision|REQUIRE_ADDITIONAL_AUTHENTICATION|

`GET /v1/tokenization_decisioning/secret`

Retrieve the Tokenization Decisioning secret key. If one does not exist your program yet, calling this endpoint will create one for you. The headers of the Tokenization Decisioning request will contain a hmac signature which you can use to verify requests originate from Lithic. See [this page](https://docs.lithic.com/docs/events-api#verifying-webhooks) for more detail about verifying Tokenization Decisioning requests.

## Create a tokenization

<a id="opIdcreateTokenization"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/cards/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/tokenizations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "AGENT",
    "agent_token": "20f418a7-27c2-486c-aeee-3ad2beb87c91"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/cards/{card_token}/tokenizations`

> 🚧 Beta API
>
> This endpoint is in beta and subject to change.

Create a tokenization for an OPEN card. Contact your Lithic representative to configure tokenization for your program and card network.

If the status is PENDING_2FA, select an available tfa_methods entry and submit the cardholder's authentication code. An ACTIVE tokenization can then be used to create payment credentials.

Additional attempts to create the same tokenizations on a card will result in a 409 Conflict.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "AGENT",
  "agent_token": "20f418a7-27c2-486c-aeee-3ad2beb87c91"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-tokenization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|card_token|path|string(uuid)|true|Card token|
|body|body|[create-tokenization-request](#schemacreate-tokenization-request)|true|none|
|» type|body|string|true|Type of tokenization to create|
|» agent_token|body|string(uuid)|true|Globally unique identifier for the active agent configured for your program|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|AGENT|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "account_token": "61c3acef-3c2c-4d61-9352-941397b92ca3",
  "card_token": "16a410c9-7f5c-43e9-8108-bb8a72c063f7",
  "created_at": "2026-10-28T15:00:00Z",
  "device_id": null,
  "digital_card_art_token": null,
  "events": [
    {
      "created_at": "2026-10-28T15:00:00Z",
      "result": "REQUIRE_ADDITIONAL_AUTHENTICATION",
      "token": "a690b617-d3d4-4976-82f6-901f817ad98a",
      "type": "TOKENIZATION_AUTHORIZATION",
      "tokenization_decline_reasons": [],
      "tokenization_tfa_reasons": [],

    }
  ],

    {
      "method": "SMS",

    },
```

## Select a tokenization authentication method

<a id="opIdselectTfaMethodForTokenization"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/tokenizations/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/select_tfa_method \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "method": "SMS"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/tokenizations/{tokenization_token}/select_tfa_method`

> 🚧 Beta API
>
> This endpoint is in beta and subject to change.

Select an available SMS or EMAIL authentication method for a tokenization with status PENDING_2FA. Use a method returned in the tokenization's list of tfa_methods. The card network initiates delivery of the authentication code to the corresponding destination.

A successful response confirms method selection, not tokenization activation. Submit the code using submit_tfa after the cardholder receives it.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "method": "SMS"
}
```

<h3 id="select-a-tokenization-authentication-method-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tokenization_token|path|string(uuid)|true|Tokenization token|
|body|body|[select-tfa-method-request](#schemaselect-tfa-method-request)|true|none|
|» method|body|[method](#schemamethod)|true|An available method from the tokenization's list of tfa_methods|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» method|SMS|
|» method|EMAIL|

## Submit a tokenization authentication code

<a id="opIdsubmitTfaForTokenization"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/tokenizations/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/submit_tfa \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "value": "01929"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/tokenizations/{tokenization_token}/submit_tfa`

> 🚧 Beta API
>
> This endpoint is in beta and subject to change.

Submit the cardholder's one-time authentication code for a tokenization with status PENDING_2FA. A successful select_tfa_method request must precede submission. Send the code as a string to preserve leading zeros.

A successful response means that the network accepted the authentication code. The activation of a tokenization will occur asynchronously initiated by the card network.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "value": "01929"
}
```

<h3 id="submit-a-tokenization-authentication-code-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tokenization_token|path|string(uuid)|true|Tokenization token|
|body|body|[submit-tfa-request](#schemasubmit-tfa-request)|true|none|
|» value|body|string|true|One-time authentication code received by the cardholder, including any leading zeros|

## Create payment credentials

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/tokenizations/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/payment_credentials \

```

`POST /v1/tokenizations/{tokenization_token}/payment_credentials`

> 🚧 Beta API
>
> This endpoint is in beta and subject to change.

```json
  "device": {

    "type": "Mobile",
    "brand": "Example brand",
    "application_name": "Example app"
  }
}
```

## Get a card's tokenizations

<a id="opIdgetTokenizations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/tokenizations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v1/tokenizations`

List card tokenizations

<h3 id="get-a-cards-tokenizations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_token|query|string(uuid)|false|Filters for tokenizations associated with a specific account.|
|begin|query|string(date)|false|Filter for tokenizations created on or after this date.|
|card_token|query|string(uuid)|false|Filters for tokenizations associated with a specific card.|
|end|query|string(date)|false|Filter for tokenizations created before this date.|
|tokenization_channel|query|string|false|Filter for tokenizations by tokenization channel. If this is not specified, only DIGITAL_WALLET tokenizations will be returned.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor representing an item's token before which a page of results should end. Used to retrieve the previous page of results before this item.|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Page size (for pagination).|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor representing an item's token after which a page of results should begin. Used to retrieve the next page of results after this item.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|tokenization_channel|DIGITAL_WALLET|
|tokenization_channel|MERCHANT|
|tokenization_channel|AGENT_PAY|
|tokenization_channel|ALL|

## Pause a card tokenization

<a id="opIdpauseTokenization"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/tokenizations/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/pause \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`POST /v1/tokenizations/{tokenization_token}/pause`

This endpoint is used to ask the card network to pause a tokenization. A successful response indicates that the request was successfully delivered to the card network. When the card network pauses the tokenization, the state will be updated and a tokenization.updated event will be sent. The endpoint may only be used on tokenizations with status `ACTIVE`.
A paused token will prevent merchants from sending authorizations, and is a temporary status that can be changed.
Reach out at [lithic.com/contact](https://lithic.com/contact) for more information.

<h3 id="pause-a-card-tokenization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tokenization_token|path|string(uuid)|true|Tokenization token|

`POST /v1/tokenizations/{tokenization_token}/unpause`

This endpoint is used to ask the card network to unpause a tokenization. A successful response indicates that the request was successfully delivered to the card network. When the card network unpauses the tokenization, the state will be updated and a tokenization.updated event will be sent. The endpoint may only be used on tokenizations with status `PAUSED`.

## Deactivate a card tokenization

<a id="opIddeactivateTokenization"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/tokenizations/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/deactivate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`POST /v1/tokenizations/{tokenization_token}/deactivate`

This endpoint is used to ask the card network to deactivate a tokenization. A successful response indicates that the request was successfully delivered to the card network. When the card network deactivates the tokenization, the state will be updated and a tokenization.updated event will be sent.
Authorizations attempted with a deactivated tokenization will be blocked and will not be forwarded to Lithic from the network. Deactivating the token is a permanent operation. If the target is a digital wallet tokenization, it will be removed from its device.
Reach out at [lithic.com/contact](https://lithic.com/contact) for more information.

<h3 id="deactivate-a-card-tokenization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

## Activate a card tokenization

<a id="opIdactivateTokenization"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/tokenizations/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/activate \
```

`POST /v1/tokenizations/{tokenization_token}/activate`

This endpoint is used to ask the card network to activate a tokenization. A successful response indicates that the request was successfully delivered to the card network. When the card network activates the tokenization, the state will be updated and a tokenization.updated event will be sent. The endpoint may only be used on digital wallet tokenizations with status `INACTIVE`, `PENDING_ACTIVATION`, or `PENDING_2FA`.
This will put the tokenization in an active state, and transactions will be allowed.
Reach out at [lithic.com/contact](https://lithic.com/contact) for more information.

## Resend activation code for a card tokenization

<a id="opIdresendActivationCodeForTokenization"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/tokenizations/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/resend_activation_code \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "activation_method_type": "TEXT_TO_CARDHOLDER_NUMBER"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/tokenizations/{tokenization_token}/resend_activation_code`

This endpoint is used to ask the card network to send another activation code to a cardholder that has already tried tokenizing a card. A successful response indicates that the request was successfully delivered to the card network.
The endpoint may only be used on Mastercard digital wallet tokenizations with status `INACTIVE`, `PENDING_ACTIVATION`, or `PENDING_2FA`. The network will send a new activation code to the one of the contact methods provided in the initial tokenization flow. If a user fails to enter the code correctly 3 times, the contact method will not be eligible for resending the activation code, and the cardholder must restart the provision process.
Reach out at [lithic.com/contact](https://lithic.com/contact) for more information.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "activation_method_type": "TEXT_TO_CARDHOLDER_NUMBER"
}
```

<h3 id="resend-activation-code-for-a-card-tokenization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tokenization_token|path|string(uuid)|true|Tokenization token|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» activation_method_type|body|string|false|The communication method that the user has selected to use to receive the authentication code.<br>Supported Values: Sms = "TEXT_TO_CARDHOLDER_NUMBER". Email = "EMAIL_TO_CARDHOLDER_ADDRESS"|

#### Enumerated Values

|» activation_method_type|EMAIL_TO_CARDHOLDER_ADDRESS|
|» activation_method_type|TEXT_TO_CARDHOLDER_NUMBER|

## Update digital card art for a card tokenization

<a id="opIdupdateDigitalCardArtForTokenization"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/tokenizations/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/update_digital_card_art \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "digital_card_art_token": "5e9483eb-8103-4e16-9794-2106111b2eca"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/tokenizations/{tokenization_token}/update_digital_card_art`

This endpoint is used update the digital card art for a digital wallet tokenization. A successful response indicates that the card network has updated the tokenization's art, and the tokenization's `digital_cart_art_token` field was updated.
The endpoint may not be used on tokenizations with status `DEACTIVATED`.
Note that this updates the art for one specific tokenization, not all tokenizations for a card. New tokenizations for a card will be created with the art referenced in the card object's `digital_card_art_token` field.
Reach out at [lithic.com/contact](https://lithic.com/contact) for more information.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "digital_card_art_token": "5e9483eb-8103-4e16-9794-2106111b2eca"
}
```

<h3 id="update-digital-card-art-for-a-card-tokenization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tokenization_token|path|string(uuid)|true|Tokenization token|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» digital_card_art_token|body|string(uuid)|false|Specifies the digital card art to be displayed in the user’s digital wallet for a tokenization. This artwork must be approved by the network and configured by Lithic to use. See [Flexible Card Art Guide](https://docs.lithic.com/docs/about-digital-wallets#flexible-card-art).|

`POST /v1/simulate/authorization_advice`

Simulates an authorization advice from the card network as if it came from a merchant acquirer. An authorization advice changes the pending amount of the transaction.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "amount": 3831,
  "token": "fabd829d-7f7b-4432-a8f2-07ea4889aaac"
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» amount|body|integer|true|Amount (in cents) to authorize. This amount will override the transaction's amount that was originally set by /v1/simulate/authorize.|
|» token|body|string(uuid)|true|The transaction token returned from the /v1/simulate/authorize. response.|

## Simulate authorization

<a id="opIdpostSimulateAuthorize"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/simulate/authorize \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "amount": 3831,
    "descriptor": "COFFEE SHOP",
    "merchant_acceptor_city": "LOS ANGELES",
    "merchant_acceptor_state": "CA",
    "merchant_acceptor_country": "USA",
    "pan": "4111111289144142"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/simulate/authorize`

Simulates an authorization request from the card network as if it came from a merchant acquirer.
If you are configured for ASA, simulating authorizations requires your ASA client to be set up properly, i.e. be able to respond to the ASA request with a valid JSON. For users that are not configured for ASA, a daily transaction limit of $5000 USD is applied by default. You can update this limit via the [update account](https://docs.lithic.com/reference/patchaccountbytoken) endpoint.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "amount": 3831,
  "descriptor": "COFFEE SHOP",
  "merchant_acceptor_city": "LOS ANGELES",
  "merchant_acceptor_state": "CA",
  "merchant_acceptor_country": "USA",
  "pan": "4111111289144142"
}
```

<h3 id="simulate-authorization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» amount|body|integer|true|Amount (in cents) to authorize. For credit authorizations and financial credit authorizations, any value entered will be converted into a negative amount in the simulated transaction. For example, entering 100 in this field will result in a -100 amount in the transaction. For balance inquiries, this field must be set to 0.|
|» billing_currency|body|string|false|3-character alphabetic ISO 4217 currency code for the cardholder billing amount. Permitted values are USD, GBP, EUR and CAD, and any other ISO 4217 code returns a 422. Defaults to USD|
|» descriptor|body|string|true|Merchant descriptor.|
|» mcc|body|string|false|Merchant category code for the transaction to be simulated. A four-digit number listed in ISO 18245.<br>Supported merchant category codes can be found [here](https://docs.lithic.com/docs/transactions#merchant-category-codes-mccs).<br>|
|» merchant_acceptor_id|body|string|false|Unique identifier to identify the payment card acceptor.|
|» merchant_acceptor_city|body|string|false|Merchant acceptor city|
|» merchant_acceptor_state|body|string|false|Merchant acceptor state/province (ISO 3166-2 subdivision code)|
|» merchant_acceptor_country|body|string|false|Merchant acceptor country code (ISO 3166-1 alpha-3)|
|» merchant_amount|body|integer|false|Amount of the transaction to be simulated in currency specified in merchant_currency, including any acquirer fees.|
|» merchant_currency|body|string|false|3-character alphabetic ISO 4217 currency code for the merchant amount. Only used when merchant_amount is set, and defaults to GBP in that case. Without merchant_amount, the merchant amount uses the billing currency. Permitted values are USD, GBP, EUR and CAD, and any other ISO 4217 code returns a 422|
|» pan|body|string|true|Sixteen digit card number.|
|» partial_approval_capable|body|boolean|false|Set to true if the terminal is capable of partial approval otherwise false.<br>Partial approval is when part of a transaction is approved and another<br>payment must be used for the remainder.<br>|
|» pin|body|string|false|Simulate entering a PIN. If omitted, PIN check will not be performed.|
|» settlement_currency|body|string|false|3-character alphabetic ISO 4217 currency code for the settlement amount. Permitted values are USD, GBP, EUR and CAD, and any other ISO 4217 code returns a 422. Defaults to the value of billing_currency. Only single message (financial) authorizations carry a settlement amount, and the value is ignored for dual message authorizations|
|» status|body|string|false|Type of event to simulate.<br>* `AUTHORIZATION` is a dual message purchase authorization, meaning a subsequent clearing step is required to settle the transaction.<br>* `BALANCE_INQUIRY` is a $0 authorization requesting the balance held on the card, and is most often observed when a cardholder requests to view a card's balance at an ATM.<br>* `CREDIT_AUTHORIZATION` is a dual message request from a merchant to authorize a refund, meaning a subsequent clearing step is required to settle the transaction.<br>* `FINANCIAL_AUTHORIZATION` is a single message request from a merchant to debit funds immediately (such as an ATM withdrawal), and no subsequent clearing is required to settle the transaction.<br>* `FINANCIAL_CREDIT_AUTHORIZATION` is a single message request from a merchant to credit funds immediately, and no subsequent clearing is required to settle the transaction.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» status|AUTHORIZATION|
|» status|BALANCE_INQUIRY|
|» status|CREDIT_AUTHORIZATION|
|» status|FINANCIAL_AUTHORIZATION|
|» status|FINANCIAL_CREDIT_AUTHORIZATION|

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "debugging_request_id": "d31645af-da9e-4952-b7dc-3ffb06618b39",
  "token": "fabd829d-7f7b-4432-a8f2-07ea4889aaac"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "debugging_request_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "message": "string"
}
```

```json
{
  "debugging_request_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "message": "string"
}
```

```json
{
  "debugging_request_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "message": "string",
  "token": "b68ba424-ab69-4cbc-a946-30d90181b621"
}
```

## Simulate clearing

<a id="opIdpostSimulateClearing"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/simulate/clearing \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "amount": 0,
    "token": "fabd829d-7f7b-4432-a8f2-07ea4889aaac"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/simulate/clearing`

Clears an existing authorization, either debit or credit. After this event, the transaction transitions from `PENDING` to `SETTLED` status.

If `amount` is not set, the full amount of the transaction will be cleared. This endpoint may be called multiple times against the same authorization to simulate a multiple-completion scenario, with each call creating a separate clearing event.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "amount": 0,
  "token": "fabd829d-7f7b-4432-a8f2-07ea4889aaac"
}
```

<h3 id="simulate-clearing-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» amount|body|integer|false|Amount (in cents) to clear. Typically this will match the amount in the original authorization, but can be higher or lower. The sign of this amount will automatically match the sign of the original authorization's amount. For example, entering 100 in this field will result in a -100 amount in the transaction, if the original authorization is a credit authorization.<br><br>If `amount` is not set, the full amount of the transaction will be cleared. This endpoint may be called multiple times against the same authorization to simulate a multiple-completion scenario, with each call creating a separate clearing event.<br>|
|» token|body|string(uuid)|true|The transaction token returned from the /v1/simulate/authorize response.|

```json
}
```

|token|string(uuid)|false|none|A unique token to reference this transaction.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth
</aside>

## Simulate return reversal

<a id="opIdpostSimulateReturnReversal"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/simulate/return_reversal \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "token": "fabd829d-7f7b-4432-a8f2-07ea4889aaac"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/simulate/return_reversal`

Reverses a return, i.e. a credit transaction with a `SETTLED` status. Returns can be financial credit authorizations, or credit authorizations that have cleared.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "token": "fabd829d-7f7b-4432-a8f2-07ea4889aaac"
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» token|body|string(uuid)|true|The transaction token returned from the /v1/simulate/authorize response.|

## Simulate void

<a id="opIdpostSimulateVoid"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/simulate/void \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "amount": 100,
    "token": "fabd829d-7f7b-4432-a8f2-07ea4889aaac",
    "type": "AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRY"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/simulate/void`

Voids a pending authorization. If `amount` is not set, the full amount will be voided. Can be used on partially voided transactions but not partially cleared transactions. _Simulating an authorization expiry on credit authorizations or credit authorization advice is not currently supported but will be added soon._


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "amount": 100,
  "token": "fabd829d-7f7b-4432-a8f2-07ea4889aaac",
  "type": "AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRY"
}
```

<h3 id="simulate-void-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» amount|body|integer|false|Amount (in cents) to void. Typically this will match the amount in the original authorization, but can be less. Applies to authorization reversals only. An authorization expiry will always apply to the full pending amount.|
|» token|body|string(uuid)|true|The transaction token returned from the /v1/simulate/authorize response.|
|» type|body|string|false|Type of event to simulate. Defaults to `AUTHORIZATION_REVERSAL`.<br><br>* `AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRY` indicates authorization has expired and been reversed by Lithic.<br>* `AUTHORIZATION_REVERSAL` indicates authorization was reversed by the merchant.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRY|
|» type|AUTHORIZATION_REVERSAL|

## List card transactions

<a id="opIdgetTransactions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/transactions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v1/transactions`

List card transactions. All amounts are in the smallest unit of their respective currency (e.g., cents for USD) and inclusive of any acquirer fees.


<h3 id="list-card-transactions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_token|query|string(uuid)|false|Filters for transactions associated with a specific account.<br>|
|card_token|query|string(uuid)|false|Filters for transactions associated with a specific card.|
|result|query|string|false|Filters for transactions using transaction result field. Can filter by `APPROVED`, and `DECLINED`.|
|status|query|[card_transaction_status_filter](#schemacard_transaction_status_filter)|false|Filters for transactions using transaction status field.|
|begin|query|string(date-time)|false|Date string in RFC 3339 format. Only entries created on or after the specified time will be included. UTC time zone.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|Date string in RFC 3339 format. Only entries created before the specified time will be included. UTC time zone.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor representing an item's token before which a page of results should end. Used to retrieve the previous page of results before this item.|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Page size (for pagination).|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor representing an item's token after which a page of results should begin. Used to retrieve the next page of results after this item.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|result|APPROVED|
|result|DECLINED|
|status|PENDING|
|status|VOIDED|
|status|SETTLED|
|status|DECLINED|
|status|EXPIRED|
