<h1 id="lithic-developer-api-transaction-monitoring">Transaction Monitoring</h1>

## List cases

<a id="opIdlistTransactionMonitoringCases"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/transaction_monitoring/cases \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v1/transaction_monitoring/cases`

Lists transaction monitoring cases, optionally filtered.

<h3 id="list-cases-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|queue_token|query|string(uuid)|false|Only return cases belonging to the provided queue.|
|status|query|[case-status](#schemacase-status)|false|Only return cases with the provided status.|
|assignee|query|string|false|Only return cases assigned to the provided value. Pass an empty string to return only unassigned cases.|
|rule_token|query|string(uuid)|false|Only return cases triggered by the provided transaction monitoring rule.|
|transaction_token|query|string(uuid)|false|Only return cases that include the provided transaction.|
|card_token|query|string(uuid)|false|Only return cases that include transactions on the provided card.|
|account_token|query|string(uuid)|false|Only return cases that include transactions on the provided account.|
|entity_token|query|string(uuid)|false|Only return cases associated with the provided entity. Accepts a card, account, or financial account token. Cases with a `PROGRAM` entity have no entity token and are never returned by this filter.|
|sort_by|query|[case-sort-by](#schemacase-sort-by)|false|Sort order for the returned cases.|
|begin|query|string(date-time)|false|Date string in RFC 3339 format. Only entries created on or after the specified time will be included. UTC time zone.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|Date string in RFC 3339 format. Only entries created before the specified time will be included. UTC time zone.|
|starting_after|query|string(uuid)|false|A cursor representing an item's token after which a page of results should begin. Used to retrieve the next page of results after this item.|
|ending_before|query|string(uuid)|false|A cursor representing an item's token before which a page of results should end. Used to retrieve the previous page of results before this item.|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Page size (for pagination).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|OPEN|
|status|ASSIGNED|
|status|IN_REVIEW|
|status|ESCALATED|
|status|RESOLVED|
|status|CLOSED|
|sort_by|CREATED_ASC|
|sort_by|CREATED_DESC|
|sort_by|PRIORITY_DESC|
|sort_by|PRIORITY_ASC|
|sort_by|STATUS_DESC|
|sort_by|STATUS_ASC|

## Update case

<a id="opIdupdateTransactionMonitoringCase"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.lithic.com/v1/transaction_monitoring/cases/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \

  -d '{
    "status": "OPEN",

    "resolution_notes": "string",
    "tags": {
      "property1": "string",

    },

    "sla_deadline": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "actor_token": "string"
  }'
```

`PATCH /v1/transaction_monitoring/cases/{case_token}`

Updates a transaction monitoring case.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "status": "OPEN",
  "title": "string",
  "assignee": "string",
  "resolution": "string",
  "resolution_notes": "string",
  "tags": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "priority": "LOW",
  "sla_deadline": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "actor_token": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="update-case-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|case_token|path|string(uuid)|true|Globally unique identifier for the case.|
|body|body|[update-case-request](#schemaupdate-case-request)|true|none|
|» status|body|[case-status](#schemacase-status)|false|Status of a case as it progresses through the review workflow:<br>  - `OPEN` - The case has been created and is still collecting matching transactions<br>  - `ASSIGNED` - An analyst has been assigned and transaction collection has stopped<br>  - `IN_REVIEW` - The case is actively being investigated<br>  - `ESCALATED` - The case has been reviewed and requires additional oversight<br>  - `RESOLVED` - A determination has been made and a resolution recorded<br>  - `CLOSED` - The case is finalized<br>|
|» title|body|string \| null|false|New title for the case, or `null` to clear it|
|» assignee|body|string \| null|false|New assignee for the case, or `null` to unassign|
|» resolution|body|string|false|Resolution to record on the case. Must be one of the<br>`allowed_resolutions` configured on the case's queue, otherwise the request is<br>rejected with a `400`|
|» resolution_notes|body|string|false|Notes describing the resolution|
|» tags|body|object|false|Arbitrary key-value metadata to set on the case|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» priority|body|[priority](#schemapriority)|false|Priority level of a case, controlling queue ordering and SLA urgency|
|» sla_deadline|body|string \| null(date-time)|false|New SLA deadline for the case, or `null` to clear it|
|» actor_token|body|string|false|Optional client-provided identifier for the actor performing this action,<br>recorded on the resulting activity entry. This value is supplied by the<br>client (for example, your own internal user ID) and is not authenticated<br>by Lithic<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» status|OPEN|
|» status|ASSIGNED|
|» status|IN_REVIEW|
|» status|ESCALATED|
|» status|RESOLVED|
|» status|CLOSED|
|» priority|LOW|
|» priority|MEDIUM|
|» priority|HIGH|
|» priority|CRITICAL|

> Example responses

```json
        "country": "USA",
        "state": "IL",

      }

  },
```

<h3 id="accountholderupdated-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» event_type|body|string|true|The type of event that occurred.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|KYB payload for an updated account holder.|
|» token|body|string(uuid)|true|The token of the account_holder that was created.|
|» update_request|body|object|true|Original request to update the account holder.|
|» » beneficial_owner_individuals|body|[[individual2](#schemaindividual2)]|false|You must submit a list of all direct and indirect individuals with 25% or more ownership in the company. A maximum of 4 beneficial owners can be submitted. If no individual owns 25% of the company you do not need to send beneficial owner information.<br>See [FinCEN requirements](https://www.fincen.gov/sites/default/files/shared/CDD_Rev6.7_Sept_2017_Certificate.pdf) (Section I) for more background on individuals that should be included.|
|» » business_entity|body|[kyb-business-entity](#schemakyb-business-entity)|false|Information for business for which the account is being opened and KYB is being run.|
|» » control_person|body|[individual2](#schemaindividual2)|false|An individual with significant responsibility for managing the legal entity (e.g., a Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, Chief Operating Officer, Managing Member, General Partner, President, Vice President, or Treasurer). This can be an executive, or someone who will have program-wide access to the cards that Lithic will provide. In some cases, this individual could also be a beneficial owner listed above. See [FinCEN requirements](https://www.fincen.gov/sites/default/files/shared/CDD_Rev6.7_Sept_2017_Certificate.pdf) (Section II) for more background.|
|» external_id|body|string|false|A user provided id that can be used to link an account holder with an external system|
|» naics_code|body|string|false|6-digit North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the business. Only present if naics_code was included in the update request.|
|» nature_of_business|body|string|false|Short description of the company's line of business (i.e., what does the company do?). Values longer than 255 characters will be truncated before KYB verification|
|» website_url|body|string|false|Company website URL.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|KYC payload for an updated account holder.|

Note that the `merchant_amount` is in the local currency and the amount is in the settlement currency.|

|» status_reason|body|string|true|The reason for the PIN update:<br>  * `PIN_SET` - The PIN was set for the first time; `pin_status` is `OK`<br>  * `PIN_CHANGED` - The PIN was changed, including when changing a blocked PIN; `pin_status` is `OK`<br>  * `PIN_UNBLOCKED` - The PIN was unblocked without changing it; `pin_status` is `OK`<br>  * `EXCESSIVE_PIN_ATTEMPTS` - The PIN was blocked due to excessive incorrect PIN attempts; `pin_status` is `BLOCKED`<br>|

```json
      ]
```

```json
  "upload_constraints": {
    "accepted_mime_types": [
      "string"
    ],
    "max_size_bytes": 0
  },
  "download_url": "string",
  "download_url_expires_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="claimdocumentuploaded-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|» updated|body|string(date-time)|true|When the document was last updated|

<a id="opIddigitalWalletTokenizationApprovalRequestWebhook"></a>

`POST digital_wallet.tokenization_approval_request`

Tokenization Customer Decisioning Request. Use `tokenization.approval_request` for notification webhooks.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "account_token": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002",
  "card_token": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001",
  "created": "2023-09-18T12:34:56Z",
  "device": {
    "imei": "123456789012345",
    "ip_address": "1.1.1.1",
    "location": "37.3860517/-122.0838511"
  },
  "digital_wallet_token_metadata": {
    "payment_account_info": {
      "account_holder_data": {
        "phone_number": "+15555555555"
      },
      "pan_unique_reference": "pan_unique_ref_1234567890123456789012345678",
      "payment_account_reference": "ref_1234567890123456789012",
      "token_unique_reference": "token_unique_ref_1234567890123456789012345678"
    },
    "payment_app_instance_id": "app_instance_123456789012345678901234567890",
    "status": "Pending",
    "token_requestor_id": "12345678901",
    "token_requestor_name": "APPLE_PAY"
  },
  "event_type": "digital_wallet.tokenization_approval_request",
  "issuer_decision": "APPROVED",
  "tokenization_channel": "DIGITAL_WALLET",
  "tokenization_source": "PUSH_PROVISION",
  "tokenization_token": "tok_1234567890abcdef",
  "wallet_decisioning_info": {
    "account_score": "100",
    "device_score": "100",
    "recommendation_reasons": [
      "Reason1"
    ],
    "recommended_decision": "Decision1"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="tokenization-decisioning-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|webhook-id|header|string(uuid)|false|Webhook ID|
|webhook-timestamp|header|integer|false|Unix timestamp used for HMAC verification|
|webhook-signature|header|string|false|A list of HMAC signatures encoded in Base64 and separated by spaces. Can contain multiple HMAC signatures as a result of key rotation.|
|body|body|[digital-wallet-tokenization-approval-request](#schemadigital-wallet-tokenization-approval-request)|false|none|
|» account_token|body|string|true|Unique identifier for the user tokenizing a card|
|» card_token|body|string|true|Unique identifier for the card being tokenized|
|» created|body|string(date-time)|true|Indicate when the request was received from Mastercard or Visa|
|» device|body|[device](#schemadevice)|false|none|
|» issuer_decision|body|string|true|Whether Lithic decisioned on the token, and if so, what the decision was. APPROVED/VERIFICATION_REQUIRED/DENIED.|
|» tokenization_channel|body|string|true|The channel through which the tokenization was made.|
|» tokenization_source|body|string|false|The source of the tokenization.|
|» tokenization_token|body|string|true|Unique identifier for the digital wallet token attempt|
|» wallet_decisioning_info|body|[wallet-decisioning-info](#schemawallet-decisioning-info)|true|none|
|» digital_wallet_token_metadata|body|[digital-wallet-token-metadata](#schemadigital-wallet-token-metadata)|true|Contains the metadata for the digital wallet being tokenized.|
|» customer_tokenization_decision|body|null \| [customer-tokenization-decision](#schemacustomer-tokenization-decision)|false|The customer's tokenization decision outcome. Only populated in webhook events (after decisioning), not in the initial decisioning request|
|» » *oneOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[customer-tokenization-decision](#schemacustomer-tokenization-decision)|false|Contains the metadata for the customer tokenization decision.|
|» event_type|body|string|true|The name of this event|
|» tokenization_decline_reasons|body|[[tokenization-decline-reason](#schematokenization-decline-reason)]|false|List of reasons why the tokenization was declined. Only populated in webhook events, not in the initial decisioning request|
|» tokenization_tfa_reasons|body|[[tokenization-tfa-reason](#schematokenization-tfa-reason)]|false|List of reasons why two-factor authentication was required. Only populated in webhook events, not in the initial decisioning request|
|» rule_results|body|[[tokenization-rule-result](#schematokenization-rule-result)]|false|Results from rules that were evaluated for this tokenization. Only populated in webhook events, not in the initial decisioning request|

## digital_wallet.tokenization_two_factor_authentication_code

<a id="opIddigitalWalletTokenizationTwoFactorAuthenticationCodeWebhook"></a>

`POST digital_wallet.tokenization_two_factor_authentication_code`

Occurs when a tokenization request 2FA code is sent to the Lithic customer for self serve delivery.

This event will be deprecated in the future. We recommend using `tokenization.two_factor_authentication_code` instead.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "event_type": "digital_wallet.tokenization_two_factor_authentication_code",
  "account_token": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002",
  "activation_method": {
    "type": "TEXT_TO_CARDHOLDER_NUMBER",
    "value": "+15555555555"
  },
  "authentication_code": "123456",
  "card_token": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001",
  "created": "2020-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "tokenization_token": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000003"
}
```

<h3 id="digitalwallettokenizationtwofactorauthenticationcode-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» event_type|body|string|true|The type of event that occurred.|
|» account_token|body|string|true|Unique identifier for the user tokenizing a card|
|» activation_method|body|object|true|none|
|» » type|body|string|true|The communication method that the user has selected to use to receive the authentication code.<br>Supported Values: Sms = "TEXT_TO_CARDHOLDER_NUMBER". Email = "EMAIL_TO_CARDHOLDER_ADDRESS"|
|» » value|body|string|true|The location where the user wants to receive the authentication code.<br>The format depends on the ActivationMethod.Type field. If Type is Email, the Value will be the email address. If the Type is Sms, the Value will be the phone number.|
|» authentication_code|body|string|true|Authentication code to provide to the user tokenizing a card.|
|» card_token|body|string|true|Unique identifier for the card being tokenized|
|» created|body|string(date-time)|true|Indicate when the request was received from Mastercard or Visa|
|» tokenization_token|body|string|true|Unique identifier for the tokenization|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » type|EMAIL_TO_CARDHOLDER_ADDRESS|
|» » type|TEXT_TO_CARDHOLDER_NUMBER|

<h3 id="digitalwallettokenizationtwofactorauthenticationcode-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

ApiKeyAuth

## dispute.updated

<a id="opIddisputeUpdatedWebhook"></a>

`POST dispute.updated`

Occurs when a dispute filed through the Chargebacks API (`/v1/disputes`) is created or updated.

This event is not emitted for Managed Disputes. Use `dispute_transaction.created` and `dispute_transaction.updated` instead.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "event_type": "dispute.updated",
  "amount": 200,
  "arbitration_date": null,
  "created": "2023-07-19T18:39:34.768Z",
  "customer_filed_date": "2023-07-20T09:00:00Z",
  "customer_note": "I didn't receive the goods.",
  "network_claim_ids": [
    "CLAIM-001"
  ],
  "network_filed_date": "2023-07-21T11:00:00Z",
  "network_reason_code": "4808",
  "prearbitration_date": null,
  "primary_claim_id": "CLAIM-001",
  "reason": "GOODS_SERVICES_NOT_RECEIVED",
  "representment_date": null,
  "resolution_date": null,
  "resolution_note": null,
  "resolution_reason": null,
  "status": "SUBMITTED",
  "token": "b24230fa-181e-4b31-9a5c-276747e619a0",
  "transaction_token": "12345624-aa69-4cbc-a946-30d90181b621"
}
```

<h3 id="disputeupdated-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» event_type|body|string|true|The type of event that occurred.|
|» amount|body|integer|true|Amount under dispute. May be different from the original transaction amount.|
|» arbitration_date|body|string \| null(date-time)|true|Date dispute entered arbitration.|
|» created|body|string(date-time)|true|Timestamp of when first Dispute was reported.|
|» customer_filed_date|body|string \| null(date-time)|true|Date that the dispute was filed by the customer making the dispute.|
|» customer_note|body|string \| null|true|End customer description of the reason for the dispute.|
|» network_claim_ids|body|[string] \| null|true|Unique identifiers for the dispute from the network.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» network_filed_date|body|string \| null(date-time)|true|Date that the dispute was submitted to the network.|
|» network_reason_code|body|string \| null|true|Network reason code used to file the dispute.|
|» prearbitration_date|body|string \| null(date-time)|true|Date dispute entered pre-arbitration.|
|» primary_claim_id|body|string \| null|true|Unique identifier for the dispute from the network. If there are multiple, this will be the first claim id set by the network|
|» reason|body|string|true|Dispute reason:<br>* `ATM_CASH_MISDISPENSE`: ATM cash misdispense.<br>* `CANCELLED`: Transaction was cancelled by the customer.<br>* `DUPLICATED`: The transaction was a duplicate.<br>* `FRAUD_CARD_NOT_PRESENT`: Fraudulent transaction, card not present.<br>* `FRAUD_CARD_PRESENT`: Fraudulent transaction, card present.<br>* `FRAUD_OTHER`: Fraudulent transaction, other types such as questionable merchant activity.<br>* `GOODS_SERVICES_NOT_AS_DESCRIBED`: The goods or services were not as described.<br>* `GOODS_SERVICES_NOT_RECEIVED`: The goods or services were not received.<br>* `INCORRECT_AMOUNT`: The transaction amount was incorrect.<br>* `MISSING_AUTH`: The transaction was missing authorization.<br>* `OTHER`: Other reason.<br>* `PROCESSING_ERROR`: Processing error.<br>* `REFUND_NOT_PROCESSED`: The refund was not processed.<br>* `RECURRING_TRANSACTION_NOT_CANCELLED`: The recurring transaction was not cancelled.<br>|
|» representment_date|body|string \| null(date-time)|true|Date the representment was received.|
|» resolution_date|body|string \| null(date-time)|true|Date that the dispute was resolved.|
|» resolution_note|body|string \| null|true|Note by Dispute team on the case resolution.|
|» resolution_reason|body|string \| null|true|Reason for the dispute resolution:<br>* `CASE_LOST`: This case was lost at final arbitration.<br>* `NETWORK_REJECTED`: Network rejected.<br>* `NO_DISPUTE_RIGHTS_3DS`: No dispute rights, 3DS.<br>* `NO_DISPUTE_RIGHTS_BELOW_THRESHOLD`: No dispute rights, below threshold.<br>* `NO_DISPUTE_RIGHTS_CONTACTLESS`: No dispute rights, contactless.<br>* `NO_DISPUTE_RIGHTS_HYBRID`: No dispute rights, hybrid.<br>* `NO_DISPUTE_RIGHTS_MAX_CHARGEBACKS`: No dispute rights, max chargebacks.<br>* `NO_DISPUTE_RIGHTS_OTHER`: No dispute rights, other.<br>* `PAST_FILING_DATE`: Past filing date.<br>* `PREARBITRATION_REJECTED`: Prearbitration rejected.<br>* `PROCESSOR_REJECTED_OTHER`: Processor rejected, other.<br>* `REFUNDED`: Refunded.<br>* `REFUNDED_AFTER_CHARGEBACK`: Refunded after chargeback.<br>* `WITHDRAWN`: Withdrawn.<br>* `WON_ARBITRATION`: Won arbitration.<br>* `WON_FIRST_CHARGEBACK`: Won first chargeback.<br>* `WON_PREARBITRATION`: Won prearbitration.<br>|
|» status|body|string|true|Status types:<br>* `NEW` - New dispute case is opened.<br>* `PENDING_CUSTOMER` - Lithic is waiting for customer to provide more information.<br>* `SUBMITTED` - Dispute is submitted to the card network.<br>* `REPRESENTMENT` - Case has entered second presentment.<br>* `PREARBITRATION` - Case has entered prearbitration.<br>* `ARBITRATION` - Case has entered arbitration.<br>* `CASE_WON` - Case was won and credit will be issued.<br>* `CASE_CLOSED` - Case was lost or withdrawn.<br>|
|» token|body|string(uuid)|true|Globally unique identifier.|
|» transaction_token|body|string(uuid)|true|The transaction that is being disputed. A transaction can only be disputed once but may have multiple dispute cases.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» reason|ATM_CASH_MISDISPENSE|
|» reason|CANCELLED|
|» reason|DUPLICATED|
|» reason|FRAUD_CARD_NOT_PRESENT|
|» reason|FRAUD_CARD_PRESENT|
|» reason|FRAUD_OTHER|
|» reason|GOODS_SERVICES_NOT_AS_DESCRIBED|
|» reason|GOODS_SERVICES_NOT_RECEIVED|
|» reason|INCORRECT_AMOUNT|
|» reason|MISSING_AUTH|
|» reason|OTHER|
|» reason|PROCESSING_ERROR|
|» reason|RECURRING_TRANSACTION_NOT_CANCELLED|
|» reason|REFUND_NOT_PROCESSED|
|» resolution_reason|CASE_LOST|
|» resolution_reason|NETWORK_REJECTED|
|» resolution_reason|NO_DISPUTE_RIGHTS_3DS|
|» resolution_reason|NO_DISPUTE_RIGHTS_BELOW_THRESHOLD|
|» resolution_reason|NO_DISPUTE_RIGHTS_CONTACTLESS|
|» resolution_reason|NO_DISPUTE_RIGHTS_HYBRID|
|» resolution_reason|NO_DISPUTE_RIGHTS_MAX_CHARGEBACKS|
|» resolution_reason|NO_DISPUTE_RIGHTS_OTHER|
|» resolution_reason|PAST_FILING_DATE|
|» resolution_reason|PREARBITRATION_REJECTED|
|» resolution_reason|PROCESSOR_REJECTED_OTHER|
|» resolution_reason|REFUNDED|
|» resolution_reason|REFUNDED_AFTER_CHARGEBACK|
|» resolution_reason|WITHDRAWN|
|» resolution_reason|WON_ARBITRATION|
|» resolution_reason|WON_FIRST_CHARGEBACK|
|» resolution_reason|WON_PREARBITRATION|
|» resolution_reason|null|
|» status|ARBITRATION|
|» status|CASE_CLOSED|
|» status|CASE_WON|
|» status|NEW|
|» status|PENDING_CUSTOMER|
|» status|PREARBITRATION|
|» status|REPRESENTMENT|
|» status|SUBMITTED|

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» event_type|body|string|true|The type of event that occurred.|
|» token|body|string(uuid)|true|A globally unique identifier for this record of an external bank account association. If a program links an external bank account to more than one end-user or to both the program and the end-user, then Lithic will return each record of the association|
|» owner|body|string|true|Legal Name of the business or individual who owns the external account. This will appear in statements|
|» routing_number|body|string|true|Routing Number|
|» last_four|body|string|true|The last 4 digits of the bank account. Derived by Lithic from the account number passed|

|» currency|body|string|true|currency of the external account 3-character alphabetic ISO 4217 code|
|» country|body|string|true|The country that the bank account is located in using ISO 3166-1. We will only accept USA bank accounts e.g., USA|
|» account_token|body|string \| null(uuid)|false|Indicates which Lithic account the external account is associated with. For external accounts that are associated with the program, account_token field returned will be null|

|» doing_business_as|body|string \| null|false|Doing Business As|
|» user_defined_id|body|string \| null|false|User Defined ID|

If purchase includes one or more item, this indicator is used for the physical goods; if the purchase only includes digital goods, this indicator is used to describe the most expensive item purchased. Maps to EMV 3DS field `shipIndicator`.|

|» psd2_context|body|object \| null|false|PSD2/SCA context for EEA and UK transactions. Present when Lithic determines the transaction is in scope for PSD2 Strong Customer Authentication. Absent for out-of-scope transactions.|
|» » acquirer_exemption|body|string|false|SCA exemption declared by the acquirer in the 3DS authentication request.<br><br>* `NONE` - No exemption claimed<br>* `TRANSACTION_RISK_ANALYSIS` - Transaction Risk Analysis (TRA) exemption; acquirer asserts low fraud risk<br>* `LOW_VALUE` - Low-value payment exemption; transaction is below the EUR 30 threshold<br>* `RECURRING_PAYMENT` - Recurring payment with a fixed amount to the same payee<br>* `MERCHANT_INITIATED_TRANSACTION` - Merchant-initiated transaction (MIT); cardholder not present<br>* `TRUSTED_BENEFICIARY` - Trusted beneficiary; merchant is on cardholder's whitelist<br>* `STRONG_CUSTOMER_AUTHENTICATION_DELEGATION` - SCA already performed by a delegated third-party authenticator<br>* `SECURE_CORPORATE_PAYMENT` - Secure corporate payment using a dedicated corporate card or process<br>* `AUTHENTICATION_OUTAGE_EXCEPTION` - Authentication outage exception; scheme-level fallback during ACS downtime<br>* `BUNDLED` - Mastercard only; bundled exemption code where the exact exemption type cannot be distinguished|
|» » lithic_exemption_validation|body|string|false|Lithic's validation of the acquirer-declared exemption. Absent when no acquirer exemption was declared.<br><br>* `ACCEPTED` - Lithic signals support the acquirer's claim<br>* `REJECTED` - Lithic signals contradict the claim, or a required signal is missing<br>* `NOT_VALIDATED` - Exemption was declared but Lithic has no basis to evaluate it; treated as `REJECTED` for challenge purposes|
|» three_ds_requestor_challenge_indicator|body|string|true|Indicates whether a challenge is requested for this transaction<br><br>* `NO_PREFERENCE` - No Preference<br>* `NO_CHALLENGE_REQUESTED` - No Challenge Requested<br>* `CHALLENGE_PREFERENCE` - Challenge requested (3DS Requestor preference)<br>* `CHALLENGE_MANDATE` - Challenge requested (Mandate)<br>* `NO_CHALLENGE_RISK_ALREADY_ASSESSED` - No Challenge requested (Transactional risk analysis is already performed)<br>* `DATA_SHARE_ONLY` - No Challenge requested (Data Share Only)<br>* `OTHER` - Other indicators not captured by above. These are rarely used|
|» three_ri_request_type|body|string \| null|false|Type of 3DS Requestor Initiated (3RI) request — i.e., a 3DS authentication that takes place at the initiation of the merchant rather than the cardholder. The most common example of this is where a merchant is authenticating before billing for a recurring transaction such as a pay TV subscription or a utility bill. Maps to EMV 3DS field `threeRIInd`.|
|» token|body|string(uuid)|true|Globally unique identifier for the 3DS authentication. Permitted values: 36-digit version 4 UUID (including hyphens).|
|» transaction|body|object \| null|false|Object containing data about the e-commerce transaction for which the merchant is requesting authentication.|
|» » amount|body|number|true|Amount of the purchase in minor units of currency with all punctuation removed. Maps to EMV 3DS field `purchaseAmount`.|
|» » cardholder_amount|body|number \| null|true|Approximate amount of the purchase in minor units of cardholder currency. Derived from `amount` using a daily conversion rate.|
|» » currency|body|string|true|Currency of the purchase. Maps to EMV 3DS field `purchaseCurrency`. Permitted values: ISO 4217 three-character currency code (e.g., USD).|
|» » currency_exponent|body|number|true|Minor units of currency, as specified in ISO 4217 currency exponent. Maps to EMV 3DS field `purchaseExponent`.|
|» » date_time|body|string(date-time)|true|Date and time when the authentication was generated by the merchant/acquirer's 3DS server. Maps to EMV 3DS field `purchaseDate`. Permitted values: Date string in the ISO 8601 format yyyy-MM-dd'T'hh:mm:ssZ.|
|» » type|body|string \| null|true|Type of the transaction for which a 3DS authentication request is occurring. Maps to EMV 3DS field `transType`.|
|» updated|body|string(date-time)|true|Date and time when the authentication was last updated in Lithic's system. Equal to `created` until the authentication is updated (e.g. a challenge is completed). Permitted values: Date string in the ISO 8601 format yyyy-MM-dd'T'hh:mm:ssZ.|

## three_ds_authentication.updated

<a id="opIdthreeDsAuthenticationUpdatedWebhook"></a>

`POST three_ds_authentication.updated`

Relevant only for SMS_OTP method<br>* CARDHOLDER_TIMEOUT - Cardholder failed to complete the challenge within the given challenge TTL<br>* CANCELED_VIA_CHALLENGE_UI - Cardholder canceled the challenge by selecting "cancel" on the challenge UI<br>* CANCELED_OOB - Cardholder canceled the challenge out of band<br>* ATTEMPTS_EXCEEDED - Cardholder failed the challenge by either entering an incorrect OTP more than the allowed number of times or requesting a new OTP more than the allowed number of times<br>* ABORTED - Merchant aborted authentication after a challenge was requested<br>* ERROR - The challenge failed for a reason different than those documented|

|» » » delivery_email_address|body|string \| null|false|In transactions with electronic delivery, email address to which merchandise is delivered. Maps to EMV 3DS field `deliveryEmailAddress`.|
|» » » delivery_time_frame|body|string \| null|false|The delivery time frame for the merchandise. Maps to EMV 3DS field `deliveryTimeframe`.|
|» » » gift_card_amount|body|integer \| null|false|In prepaid or gift card purchase transactions, purchase amount total in major units (e.g., a purchase of USD $205.10 would be 205). Maps to EMV 3DS field `giftCardAmount`.|
|» » » gift_card_count|body|integer \| null|false|In prepaid or gift card purchase transactions, count of individual prepaid or gift cards/codes purchased. Maps to EMV 3DS field `giftCardCount`.|
|» » » gift_card_currency|body|string \| null|false|In prepaid or gift card purchase transactions, currency code of the gift card. Maps to EMV 3DS field `giftCardCurr`. Permitted values: ISO 4217 three-character currency code (e.g., USD).|
|» » » order_availability|body|string \| null|false|Indicates whether the purchase is for merchandise that is available now or at a future date. Maps to EMV 3DS field `preOrderPurchaseInd`.|
|» » » pre_order_available_date|body|string \| null(date-time)|false|In pre-order purchase transactions, the expected date that the merchandise will be available. Maps to EMV 3DS field `preOrderDate`. Permitted values: Date string in the ISO 8601 format yyyy-MM-dd'T'hh:mm:ssZ|
|» » » reorder_items|body|string \| null|false|Indicates whether the cardholder is reordering previously purchased merchandise. Maps to EMV 3DS field `reorderItemsInd`.|
|» » » shipping_method|body|string \| null|false|Shipping method that the cardholder chose for the transaction. If purchase includes one or more item, this indicator is used for the physical goods; if the purchase only includes digital goods, this indicator is used to describe the most expensive item purchased. Maps to EMV 3DS field `shipIndicator`.|
|» message_category|body|string|true|Either PAYMENT_AUTHENTICATION or NON_PAYMENT_AUTHENTICATION. For NON_PAYMENT_AUTHENTICATION, additional_data and transaction fields are not populated.|
|» psd2_context|body|object \| null|false|PSD2/SCA context for EEA and UK transactions. Present when Lithic determines the transaction is in scope for PSD2 Strong Customer Authentication. Absent for out-of-scope transactions.|
|» » acquirer_exemption|body|string|false|SCA exemption declared by the acquirer in the 3DS authentication request.<br><br>* `NONE` - No exemption claimed<br>* `TRANSACTION_RISK_ANALYSIS` - Transaction Risk Analysis (TRA) exemption; acquirer asserts low fraud risk<br>* `LOW_VALUE` - Low-value payment exemption; transaction is below the EUR 30 threshold<br>* `RECURRING_PAYMENT` - Recurring payment with a fixed amount to the same payee<br>* `MERCHANT_INITIATED_TRANSACTION` - Merchant-initiated transaction (MIT); cardholder not present<br>* `TRUSTED_BENEFICIARY` - Trusted beneficiary; merchant is on cardholder's whitelist<br>* `STRONG_CUSTOMER_AUTHENTICATION_DELEGATION` - SCA already performed by a delegated third-party authenticator<br>* `SECURE_CORPORATE_PAYMENT` - Secure corporate payment using a dedicated corporate card or process<br>* `AUTHENTICATION_OUTAGE_EXCEPTION` - Authentication outage exception; scheme-level fallback during ACS downtime<br>* `BUNDLED` - Mastercard only; bundled exemption code where the exact exemption type cannot be distinguished|
|» » lithic_exemption_validation|body|string|false|Lithic's validation of the acquirer-declared exemption. Absent when no acquirer exemption was declared.<br><br>* `ACCEPTED` - Lithic signals support the acquirer's claim<br>* `REJECTED` - Lithic signals contradict the claim, or a required signal is missing<br>* `NOT_VALIDATED` - Exemption was declared but Lithic has no basis to evaluate it; treated as `REJECTED` for challenge purposes|
|» three_ds_requestor_challenge_indicator|body|string|true|Indicates whether a challenge is requested for this transaction<br><br>* `NO_PREFERENCE` - No Preference<br>* `NO_CHALLENGE_REQUESTED` - No Challenge Requested<br>* `CHALLENGE_PREFERENCE` - Challenge requested (3DS Requestor preference)<br>* `CHALLENGE_MANDATE` - Challenge requested (Mandate)<br>* `NO_CHALLENGE_RISK_ALREADY_ASSESSED` - No Challenge requested (Transactional risk analysis is already performed)<br>* `DATA_SHARE_ONLY` - No Challenge requested (Data Share Only)<br>* `OTHER` - Other indicators not captured by above. These are rarely used|
|» three_ri_request_type|body|string \| null|false|Type of 3DS Requestor Initiated (3RI) request — i.e., a 3DS authentication that takes place at the initiation of the merchant rather than the cardholder. The most common example of this is where a merchant is authenticating before billing for a recurring transaction such as a pay TV subscription or a utility bill. Maps to EMV 3DS field `threeRIInd`.|
|» token|body|string(uuid)|true|Globally unique identifier for the 3DS authentication. Permitted values: 36-digit version 4 UUID (including hyphens).|
|» transaction|body|object \| null|false|Object containing data about the e-commerce transaction for which the merchant is requesting authentication.|
|» » amount|body|number|true|Amount of the purchase in minor units of currency with all punctuation removed. Maps to EMV 3DS field `purchaseAmount`.|
|» » cardholder_amount|body|number \| null|true|Approximate amount of the purchase in minor units of cardholder currency. Derived from `amount` using a daily conversion rate.|
|» » currency|body|string|true|Currency of the purchase. Maps to EMV 3DS field `purchaseCurrency`. Permitted values: ISO 4217 three-character currency code (e.g., USD).|
|» » currency_exponent|body|number|true|Minor units of currency, as specified in ISO 4217 currency exponent. Maps to EMV 3DS field `purchaseExponent`.|
|» » date_time|body|string(date-time)|true|Date and time when the authentication was generated by the merchant/acquirer's 3DS server. Maps to EMV 3DS field `purchaseDate`. Permitted values: Date string in the ISO 8601 format yyyy-MM-dd'T'hh:mm:ssZ.|
|» » type|body|string \| null|true|Type of the transaction for which a 3DS authentication request is occurring. Maps to EMV 3DS field `transType`.|
|» updated|body|string(date-time)|true|Date and time when the authentication was last updated in Lithic's system. Equal to `created` until the authentication is updated (e.g. a challenge is completed). Permitted values: Date string in the ISO 8601 format yyyy-MM-dd'T'hh:mm:ssZ.|

## three_ds_authentication.challenge

<a id="opIdthreeDsAuthenticationChallengeWebhook"></a>

`POST three_ds_authentication.challenge`

The `three_ds_authentication.challenge` event. Upon receiving this request, the Card Program should issue its own challenge to the cardholder. After a cardholder challenge is successfully completed, the Card Program needs to respond back to Lithic by call to [/v1/three_ds_decisioning/challenge_response](https://docs.lithic.com/reference/postthreedschallengeresponse). Then the cardholder must navigate back to the merchant checkout flow to complete the transaction. Some merchants will include an `app_requestor_url` for app-based purchases; Lithic recommends triggering a redirect to that URL after the cardholder completes an app-based challenge.

<h3 id="3ds-decisioning-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» event_type|body|string|true|none|
|» account_type|body|string \| null|true|Type of account/card that is being used for the transaction. Maps to EMV 3DS field `acctType`.|
|» additional_data|body|object \| null|false|Object containing additional data about the 3DS request that is beyond the EMV 3DS standard spec (e.g., specific fields that only certain card networks send but are not required across all 3DS requests).|
|» » network_decision|body|string \| null|false|Mastercard only: Indicates whether the network would have considered the authentication request to be low risk or not.|
|» » network_risk_score|body|integer \| null|false|Mastercard only: Assessment by the network of the authentication risk level, with a higher value indicating a higher amount of risk. Permitted values: Integer between 0-950, in increments of 50.|
|» app|body|object \| null|false|Object containing data about the app used in the e-commerce transaction. Present if the channel is 'APP_BASED'.|
|» » device_info|body|string \| null|false|Raw device information - base64-encoded JSON object. Maps to EMV 3DS field `deviceInfo`.|
|» » ip|body|string \| null|false|IP address of the device.|
|» » platform|body|string \| null|false|Device platform: Android, iOS, Windows, etc.|
|» » device|body|string \| null|false|Device model: e.g. "Apple iPhone 16".|
|» » os|body|string \| null|false|Operating System: e.g. "Android 12", "iOS 17.1".|
|» » locale|body|string \| null|false|Device locale: e.g. "en-US".|
|» » time_zone|body|string \| null|false|Time zone offset in minutes between UTC and device local time.|
|» » screen_width|body|integer \| null|false|Screen width in pixels.|
|» » screen_height|body|integer \| null|false|Screen height in pixels.|
|» » latitude|body|number \| null|false|Latitude coordinate of current device location.|
|» » longitude|body|number \| null|false|Longitude coordinate of current device location.|
|» authentication_request_type|body|string \| null|false|Type of authentication request - i.e., the type of transaction or interaction is causing the merchant to request an authentication. Maps to EMV 3DS field `threeDSRequestorAuthenticationInd`.|
|» authentication_result|body|string|true|Indicates the outcome of the 3DS authentication process.|
|» browser|body|object \| null|false|Object containing data about the browser used in the e-commerce transaction. Present if the channel is 'BROWSER'.|
|» » accept_header|body|string \| null|false|Content of the HTTP accept headers as sent from the cardholder's browser to the 3DS requestor (e.g., merchant or digital wallet).|
|» » ip|body|string(ipv4) \| string(ipv6) \| null|false|IP address of the browser as returned by the HTTP headers to the 3DS requestor (e.g., merchant or digital wallet). Maps to EMV 3DS field `browserIP`.|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string(ipv4)|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string(ipv6)|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» » java_enabled|body|boolean \| null|false|Indicates whether the cardholder's browser has the ability to execute Java. Maps to EMV 3DS field `browserJavaEnabled`.|
|» » javascript_enabled|body|boolean \| null|false|Indicates whether the cardholder's browser has the ability to execute JavaScript. Maps to EMV 3DS field `browserJavascriptEnabled`.|
|» » language|body|string \| null|false|Language of the cardholder's browser as defined in IETF BCP47. Maps to EMV 3DS field `browserLanguage`.|
|» » time_zone|body|string \| null|false|Time zone offset in minutes between UTC and browser local time. Maps to EMV 3DS field `browserTz`.|
|» » user_agent|body|string \| null|false|Content of the HTTP user-agent header. Maps to EMV 3DS field `browserUserAgent`.|
|» card_expiry_check|body|string|true|Indicates whether the expiration date provided by the cardholder during checkout matches Lithic's record of the card's expiration date.|
|» card_token|body|string(uuid)|true|Globally unique identifier for the card on which the 3DS authentication has occurred. Permitted values: 36-digit version 4 UUID (including hyphens).|
|» cardholder|body|object|true|Object containing data about the cardholder provided during the transaction.|
|» » address_match|body|boolean \| null|false|Indicates whether the shipping address and billing address provided by the cardholder are the same. This value - and assessment of whether the addresses match - is provided directly in the 3DS request and is not determined by Lithic. Maps to EMV 3DS field `addrMatch`.|
|» » address_on_file_match|body|[address_match_result](#schemaaddress_match_result)|false|Lithic's evaluation result comparing the transaction's address data with the cardholder KYC data if it exists. In the event Lithic does not have any Cardholder KYC data, or the transaction does not contain any address data, NOT_PRESENT will be returned|
|» » billing_address|body|object|false|Object containing data on the billing address provided during the transaction.|
|» » » address1|body|string \| null|false|First line of the street address provided by the cardholder.|
|» » » address2|body|string \| null|false|Second line of the street address provided by the cardholder.|
|» » » address3|body|string \| null|false|Third line of the street address provided by the cardholder.|
|» » » city|body|string \| null|false|City of the address provided by the cardholder.|
|» » » country|body|string \| null|false|Country of the address provided by the cardholder in ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 format (e.g. USA)|
|» » » postal_code|body|string \| null|false|Postal code (e.g., ZIP code) of the address provided by the cardholder|
|» » email|body|string \| null|false|Email address that is either provided by the cardholder or is on file with the merchant in a 3RI request. Maps to EMV 3DS field `email`.|
|» » name|body|string \| null|false|Name of the cardholder. Maps to EMV 3DS field `cardholderName`.|
|» » phone_number_home|body|string \| null|false|Home phone number in E.164 format provided by the cardholder. Maps to EMV 3DS fields `homePhone.cc` and `homePhone.subscriber`.|
|» » phone_number_mobile|body|string \| null|false|Mobile/cell phone number in E.164 format provided by the cardholder. Maps to EMV 3DS fields `mobilePhone.cc` and `mobilePhone.subscriber`.|
|» » phone_number_work|body|string \| null|false|Work phone number in E.164 format provided by the cardholder. Maps to EMV 3DS fields `workPhone.cc` and `workPhone.subscriber`.|
|» » shipping_address|body|object|false|Object containing data on the shipping address provided during the transaction.|
|» » » address1|body|string \| null|false|First line of the street address provided by the cardholder.|
|» » » address2|body|string \| null|false|Second line of the street address provided by the cardholder.|
|» » » address3|body|string \| null|false|Third line of the street address provided by the cardholder.|
|» » » city|body|string \| null|false|City of the address provided by the cardholder.|
|» » » country|body|string \| null|false|Country of the address provided by the cardholder in ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 format (e.g. USA)|
|» » » postal_code|body|string \| null|false|Postal code (e.g., ZIP code) of the address provided by the cardholder|
|» challenge_metadata|body|object \| null|false|Metadata about the challenge method and delivery. Only present when a challenge is triggered.|
|» » method_type|body|string|true|The type of challenge method used for authentication.|
|» » phone_number|body|string \| null|false|The phone number used for delivering the OTP. Relevant only for SMS_OTP method.|
|» » status|body|string|true|Indicates the status of the challenge<br><br>* SUCCESS - Cardholder completed the challenge successfully<br>* PENDING - Challenge was issued to the cardholder and was not completed yet<br>* SMS_DELIVERY_FAILED - Lithic confirmed undeliverability of the SMS to the provided phone number. Relevant only for SMS_OTP method<br>* CARDHOLDER_TIMEOUT - Cardholder failed to complete the challenge within the given challenge TTL<br>* CANCELED_VIA_CHALLENGE_UI - Cardholder canceled the challenge by selecting "cancel" on the challenge UI<br>* CANCELED_OOB - Cardholder canceled the challenge out of band<br>* ATTEMPTS_EXCEEDED - Cardholder failed the challenge by either entering an incorrect OTP more than the allowed number of times or requesting a new OTP more than the allowed number of times<br>* ABORTED - Merchant aborted authentication after a challenge was requested<br>* ERROR - The challenge failed for a reason different than those documented|
|» challenge_orchestrated_by|body|string \| null|false|Entity that orchestrates the challenge. This won't be set for authentications for which a decision has not yet been made (e.g. in-flight customer decisioning request).|
|» channel|body|string|true|Channel in which the authentication occurs. Maps to EMV 3DS field `deviceChannel`.|
|» created|body|string(date-time)|true|Date and time when the authentication was created in Lithic's system. Permitted values: Date string in the ISO 8601 format yyyy-MM-dd'T'hh:mm:ssZ.|
|» decision_made_by|body|string \| null|false|Entity that made the authentication decision. This won't be set for authentications for which a decision has not yet been made (e.g. in-flight customer decisioning request).|
|» merchant|body|object|true|Object containing data about the merchant involved in the e-commerce transaction.|
|» » country|body|string \| null|false|Country code of the merchant requesting 3DS authentication. Maps to EMV 3DS field `merchantCountryCode`. Permitted values: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code (e.g., USA). May not be present for non-payment authentications.|
|» » id|body|string \| null|false|Merchant identifier as assigned by the acquirer. Maps to EMV 3DS field `acquirerMerchantId`. May not be present for non-payment authentications.|
|» » mcc|body|string \| null|false|Merchant category code assigned to the merchant that describes its business activity type. Maps to EMV 3DS field `mcc`. May not be present for non-payment authentications.|
|» » name|body|string \| null|false|Name of the merchant. Maps to EMV 3DS field `merchantName`. May not be present for non-payment authentications.|
|» » risk_indicator|body|object|true|Object containing additional data indicating additional risk factors related to the e-commerce transaction.|
|» » » delivery_email_address|body|string \| null|false|In transactions with electronic delivery, email address to which merchandise is delivered. Maps to EMV 3DS field `deliveryEmailAddress`.|
|» » » delivery_time_frame|body|string \| null|false|The delivery time frame for the merchandise. Maps to EMV 3DS field `deliveryTimeframe`.|
|» » » gift_card_amount|body|integer \| null|false|In prepaid or gift card purchase transactions, purchase amount total in major units (e.g., a purchase of USD $205.10 would be 205). Maps to EMV 3DS field `giftCardAmount`.|
|» » » gift_card_count|body|integer \| null|false|In prepaid or gift card purchase transactions, count of individual prepaid or gift cards/codes purchased. Maps to EMV 3DS field `giftCardCount`.|
|» » » gift_card_currency|body|string \| null|false|In prepaid or gift card purchase transactions, currency code of the gift card. Maps to EMV 3DS field `giftCardCurr`. Permitted values: ISO 4217 three-character currency code (e.g., USD).|
|» » » order_availability|body|string \| null|false|Indicates whether the purchase is for merchandise that is available now or at a future date. Maps to EMV 3DS field `preOrderPurchaseInd`.|
|» » » pre_order_available_date|body|string \| null(date-time)|false|In pre-order purchase transactions, the expected date that the merchandise will be available. Maps to EMV 3DS field `preOrderDate`. Permitted values: Date string in the ISO 8601 format yyyy-MM-dd'T'hh:mm:ssZ|
|» » » reorder_items|body|string \| null|false|Indicates whether the cardholder is reordering previously purchased merchandise. Maps to EMV 3DS field `reorderItemsInd`.|
|» » » shipping_method|body|string \| null|false|Shipping method that the cardholder chose for the transaction. If purchase includes one or more item, this indicator is used for the physical goods; if the purchase only includes digital goods, this indicator is used to describe the most expensive item purchased. Maps to EMV 3DS field `shipIndicator`.|
|» message_category|body|string|true|Either PAYMENT_AUTHENTICATION or NON_PAYMENT_AUTHENTICATION. For NON_PAYMENT_AUTHENTICATION, additional_data and transaction fields are not populated.|
|» psd2_context|body|object \| null|false|PSD2/SCA context for EEA and UK transactions. Present when Lithic determines the transaction is in scope for PSD2 Strong Customer Authentication. Absent for out-of-scope transactions.|
|» » acquirer_exemption|body|string|false|SCA exemption declared by the acquirer in the 3DS authentication request.<br><br>* `NONE` - No exemption claimed<br>* `TRANSACTION_RISK_ANALYSIS` - Transaction Risk Analysis (TRA) exemption; acquirer asserts low fraud risk<br>* `LOW_VALUE` - Low-value payment exemption; transaction is below the EUR 30 threshold<br>* `RECURRING_PAYMENT` - Recurring payment with a fixed amount to the same payee<br>* `MERCHANT_INITIATED_TRANSACTION` - Merchant-initiated transaction (MIT); cardholder not present<br>* `TRUSTED_BENEFICIARY` - Trusted beneficiary; merchant is on cardholder's whitelist<br>* `STRONG_CUSTOMER_AUTHENTICATION_DELEGATION` - SCA already performed by a delegated third-party authenticator<br>* `SECURE_CORPORATE_PAYMENT` - Secure corporate payment using a dedicated corporate card or process<br>* `AUTHENTICATION_OUTAGE_EXCEPTION` - Authentication outage exception; scheme-level fallback during ACS downtime<br>* `BUNDLED` - Mastercard only; bundled exemption code where the exact exemption type cannot be distinguished|
|» » lithic_exemption_validation|body|string|false|Lithic's validation of the acquirer-declared exemption. Absent when no acquirer exemption was declared.<br><br>* `ACCEPTED` - Lithic signals support the acquirer's claim<br>* `REJECTED` - Lithic signals contradict the claim, or a required signal is missing<br>* `NOT_VALIDATED` - Exemption was declared but Lithic has no basis to evaluate it; treated as `REJECTED` for challenge purposes|
|» three_ds_requestor_challenge_indicator|body|string|true|Indicates whether a challenge is requested for this transaction<br><br>* `NO_PREFERENCE` - No Preference<br>* `NO_CHALLENGE_REQUESTED` - No Challenge Requested<br>* `CHALLENGE_PREFERENCE` - Challenge requested (3DS Requestor preference)<br>* `CHALLENGE_MANDATE` - Challenge requested (Mandate)<br>* `NO_CHALLENGE_RISK_ALREADY_ASSESSED` - No Challenge requested (Transactional risk analysis is already performed)<br>* `DATA_SHARE_ONLY` - No Challenge requested (Data Share Only)<br>* `OTHER` - Other indicators not captured by above. These are rarely used|
|» three_ri_request_type|body|string \| null|false|Type of 3DS Requestor Initiated (3RI) request — i.e., a 3DS authentication that takes place at the initiation of the merchant rather than the cardholder. The most common example of this is where a merchant is authenticating before billing for a recurring transaction such as a pay TV subscription or a utility bill. Maps to EMV 3DS field `threeRIInd`.|
|» token|body|string(uuid)|true|Globally unique identifier for the 3DS authentication. Permitted values: 36-digit version 4 UUID (including hyphens).|
|» transaction|body|object \| null|false|Object containing data about the e-commerce transaction for which the merchant is requesting authentication.|
|» » amount|body|number|true|Amount of the purchase in minor units of currency with all punctuation removed. Maps to EMV 3DS field `purchaseAmount`.|
|» » cardholder_amount|body|number \| null|true|Approximate amount of the purchase in minor units of cardholder currency. Derived from `amount` using a daily conversion rate.|
|» » currency|body|string|true|Currency of the purchase. Maps to EMV 3DS field `purchaseCurrency`. Permitted values: ISO 4217 three-character currency code (e.g., USD).|
|» » currency_exponent|body|number|true|Minor units of currency, as specified in ISO 4217 currency exponent. Maps to EMV 3DS field `purchaseExponent`.|
|» » date_time|body|string(date-time)|true|Date and time when the authentication was generated by the merchant/acquirer's 3DS server. Maps to EMV 3DS field `purchaseDate`. Permitted values: Date string in the ISO 8601 format yyyy-MM-dd'T'hh:mm:ssZ.|
|» » type|body|string \| null|true|Type of the transaction for which a 3DS authentication request is occurring. Maps to EMV 3DS field `transType`.|
|» updated|body|string(date-time)|true|Date and time when the authentication was last updated in Lithic's system. Equal to `created` until the authentication is updated (e.g. a challenge is completed). Permitted values: Date string in the ISO 8601 format yyyy-MM-dd'T'hh:mm:ssZ.|

## dispute_transaction.created

<a id="opIddisputeTransactionCreatedWebhook"></a>

`POST dispute_transaction.created`

Occurs when a new dispute transaction is created for a Managed Disputes case.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "event_type": "dispute_transaction.created",
  "case_id": "ROL12345",
  "token": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
  "card_token": "78ddee49-4558-4a79-80ce-339e12cc141c",
  "account_token": "82d7c408-2bbb-4f63-889a-8a2a2b1601af",
  "claim_token": "0fee7a4e-e6a8-478a-9df9-b2d92b455133",
  "network": "VISA",
  "currency": "USD",
  "created": "2024-02-07T10:00:00Z",
  "updated": "2024-02-07T10:00:00Z",
  "merchant": {
    "acceptor_id": "174030075991",
    "acquiring_institution_id": "191231",
    "descriptor": "COFFEE SHOP",
    "mcc": "5812",
    "city": "NEW YORK",
    "state": "NY",
    "country": "USA"
  },
  "transaction_series": {
    "type": "DISPUTE",
    "related_transaction_token": "98765432-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
    "related_transaction_event_token": "7063f2ae-e806-44dd-9b1f-07e5df61e9e2"
  },
  "liability_allocation": {
    "original_amount": 100000,
    "recovered_amount": 0,
    "written_off_amount": 0,
    "denied_amount": 0,
    "remaining_amount": 100000
  },
  "disposition": null,
  "status": "OPEN",
  "events": [
    {
      "token": "7063f2ae-e806-44dd-9b1f-07e5df61e9e2",
      "type": "WORKFLOW",
      "created": "2024-02-07T10:00:00Z",
      "data": {
        "stage": "CLAIM",
        "action": "OPENED",
        "reason": "Not Sent",
        "amount": 100000,
        "disposition": null
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="disputetransactioncreated-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» event_type|body|string|true|The type of event that occurred.|

|» card_token|body|string(uuid)|true|Token for the card used in the dispute, in UUID format.|
|» account_token|body|string(uuid)|true|Token for the account associated with the dispute, in UUID format.|
|» claim_token|body|string \| null(uuid)|true|Token for the claim this dispute was filed under, in UUID format. Null for disputes not initiated through the Dispute Intake API.|
|» network|body|string|true|Card network handling the dispute.|
|» currency|body|string|true|Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code.|
|» created|body|string(date-time)|true|When the dispute was created.|
|» updated|body|string(date-time)|true|When the dispute was last updated.|
|» merchant|body|[merchant](#schemamerchant)|true|none|
|» transaction_series|body|[transaction-series2](#schematransaction-series2) \| null|true|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[transaction-series2](#schematransaction-series2)|false|Contains identifiers for the transaction and specific event within being disputed; null if no transaction can be identified|
|» » *oneOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» liability_allocation|body|[liability-allocation](#schemaliability-allocation)|true|Current breakdown of how liability is allocated for the disputed amount|
|» status|body|string \| null|true|Current status of the dispute.|
|» disposition|body|string \| null|true|Dispute resolution outcome|
|» events|body|[[event2](#schemaevent2)]|true|Chronological list of events that have occurred in the dispute lifecycle|

```json
{
  "address1": "123 Old Forest Way",

}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|address1|string|true|none|Valid deliverable address (no PO boxes).|
|address2|string|false|none|Unit or apartment number (if applicable).|
|city|string|true|none|Name of city.|
|country|string|true|none|Valid country code, entered in uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 three-character format. The KYB_DELEGATED and KYC_EXEMPT workflows support all countries except BLR, CUB, IRN, PRK, RUS, SDN, SYR, and UKR. Other workflows support USA only.|
|postal_code|string \| null|false|none|Valid postal code. For USA addresses, enter either a five-digit postal code or a nine-digit postal code (ZIP+4) using the format 12345-1234. Required for all countries except the following, which do not use postal codes: ABW, AGO, ARE, ATG, BDI, BEN, BFA, BHS, BLZ, BOL, BWA, CIV, CMR, COD, COG, COK, COM, DJI, DMA, ERI, FJI, GAB, GMB, GNQ, GRD, GUY, HKG, KIR, MAC, MLI, MRT, NIU, NRU, QAT, RWA, SLB, SLE, SSD, SUR, SXM, SYC, TGO, TKL, TLS, TON, TUV, UGA, VUT, YEM, ZWE|
|state|string \| null|false|none|Valid state, province, or subdivision code, entered as the uppercase ISO 3166-2 code for the country without the country prefix. For example, `CA` for California. Optional unless the address is in one of the following countries, where it is required:<br><br> - `USA`<br> - `CAN`<br> - `AUS`<br> - `CHN`<br> - `KOR`<br> - `MEX`<br> - `MYS`<br> - `NZL`|

|created|string(date-time)|true|none|Timestamp of when the account holder was created.|
|email|string|false|none|(Deprecated. Use control_person.email when user_type == "BUSINESS". Use individual.phone_number when user_type == "INDIVIDUAL".)<br>Primary email of Account Holder.<br>|
|exemption_type|string|false|none|The type of KYC exemption for a KYC-Exempt Account Holder.|
|external_id|string|false|none|Customer-provided token that indicates a relationship with an object outside of the Lithic ecosystem.|
|individual|[AccountHolderIndividualResponse](#schemaaccountholderindividualresponse)|false|none|Only present when user_type == "INDIVIDUAL". Information about the individual for which the account is being opened and KYC is being run.|
|naics_code|string|false|none|Only present when user_type == "BUSINESS". 6-digit North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the business.|
|nature_of_business|string|false|none|Only present when user_type == "BUSINESS". User-submitted description of the business.|
|phone_number|string|false|none|(Deprecated. Use control_person.phone_number when user_type == "BUSINESS". Use individual.phone_number when user_type == "INDIVIDUAL".)<br>Primary phone of Account Holder, entered in E.164 format.<br>|
|status|string|false|none|(Deprecated. Use verification_application.status instead)<br><br>KYC and KYB evaluation states.<br><br>Note:<br>* `PENDING_REVIEW` is only applicable for the `KYB_BASIC` workflow.<br>|
|status_reasons|[string]|false|none|(Deprecated. Use verification_application.status_reasons)<br><br>Reason for the evaluation status.<br>|
|token|string(uuid)|true|none|Globally unique identifier for the account holder.|
|user_type|string|false|none|The type of Account Holder. If the type is "INDIVIDUAL", the "individual" attribute will be present.<br>If the type is "BUSINESS" then the "business_entity", "control_person", "beneficial_owner_individuals", "naics_code", "nature_of_business", and "website_url" attributes will be present.|
|verification_application|[AccountHolderVerificationApplication](#schemaaccountholderverificationapplication)|false|none|Information about the most recent identity verification attempt|
|required_documents|[[required-document](#schemarequired-document)]|false|none|Only present for "KYB_BASIC" workflow. A list of documents required for the account holder to be approved.|
|website_url|string|false|none|Only present when user_type == "BUSINESS". Business's primary website.|

If no individual owns 25% of the company you do not need to send beneficial owner information. See [FinCEN requirements](https://www.fincen.gov/sites/default/files/shared/CDD_Rev6.7_Sept_2017_Certificate.pdf) (Section I) for more background on individuals that should be included.|

This can be an executive, or someone who will have program-wide access<br><br>to the cards that Lithic will provide. In some cases, this individual could also be a beneficial owner listed above.|
|naics_code|string|false|none|Only present when user_type == "BUSINESS". 6-digit North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the business.|

|website_url|string|false|none|Only present when user_type == "BUSINESS". Business's primary website.|

|status|[status](#schemastatus)|false|none|(Deprecated. Use verification_application.status instead)<br>KYC and KYB evaluation states.<br><br>Note: `PENDING_RESUBMIT` and `PENDING_DOCUMENT` are only applicable for the `ADVANCED` workflow.<br><br>|
|status_reasons|[[status-reasons](#schemastatus-reasons)]|false|none|(Deprecated. Use verification_application.status_reasons)<br> Reason for the evaluation status.|

Request body for creating a new beneficial owner or replacing the control person entity on an existing KYB account holder.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|address|[address2](#schemaaddress2)|true|none|Individual's current address - PO boxes, UPS drops, and FedEx drops are not acceptable; APO/FPO are acceptable. Only USA addresses are supported for the KYB and KYC workflows.|
|dob|string|true|none|Individual's date of birth, as an RFC 3339 date.|
|email|string|true|none|Individual's email address. If utilizing Lithic for chargeback processing, this customer email address may be used to communicate dispute status and resolution.|
|first_name|string|true|none|Individual's first name, as it appears on government-issued identity documents.|
|last_name|string|true|none|Individual's last name, as it appears on government-issued identity documents.|
|phone_number|string|true|none|Individual's phone number, entered in E.164 format.|
|government_id|string|true|write-only|Government-issued identification number (required for identity verification and compliance with banking regulations). Social Security Numbers (SSN) and Individual Taxpayer Identification Numbers (ITIN) are currently supported, entered as full nine-digits, with or without hyphens|
|type|[entity-type](#schemaentity-type)|true|none|The type of entity to create on the account holder|

|Property|Value|

```json
  },
  "auth_rule_tokens": [
    "string"
  ],
  "cardholder_currency": "USD",
  "spend_limit": {
    "daily": 10000,
    "lifetime": 100000,
    "monthly": 40000
  },
  "state": "ACTIVE",
  "substatus": "FRAUD_IDENTIFIED",
  "comment": "string",
  "token": "b68b7424-aa69-4cbc-a946-30d90181b621",
  "verification_address": {
    "address1": "124 Old Forest Way",
    "address2": "Apt 21",
    "city": "Seattle",
    "country": "USA",
    "postal_code": "98109",
    "state": "WA"
  },
  "created": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_holder|object|false|none|none|
|auth_rule_tokens|[string]|false|none|**Deprecated.** List of identifiers for the Auth Rule(s) that are applied on the account.<br>This field is deprecated and will no longer be populated in the `account_holder` object. The key will be removed from the schema in a future release. Use the `/auth_rules` endpoints to fetch Auth Rule information instead.|
|cardholder_currency|string|false|none|3-character alphabetic ISO 4217 code for the currency of the cardholder.|
|spend_limit|object|true|none|Spend limit information for the user containing the daily, monthly, and lifetime spend limit of the account. Any charges to a card owned by this account will be declined once their transaction volume has surpassed the value in the applicable time limit (rolling). A lifetime limit of 0 indicates that the lifetime limit feature is disabled.<br>|
|state|string|true|none|Account state:<br>  * `ACTIVE` - Account is able to transact and create new cards.<br>  * `PAUSED` - Account will not be able to transact or create new cards. It can be set back<br>to `ACTIVE`.<br>  * `CLOSED` - Account will not be able to transact or create new cards. `CLOSED` accounts<br>are unable to be transitioned to `ACTIVE` or `PAUSED` states. Accounts can be manually set to `CLOSED`, or this can be done by Lithic due to failure to pass KYB/KYC or for risk/compliance reasons. Please contact [support.lithic.com](https://support.lithic.com/) if you believe this was done by mistake.|
|substatus|string \| null|false|none|Account state substatus values:<br>* `FRAUD_IDENTIFIED` - The account has been recognized as being created or used with stolen or fabricated identity information, encompassing both true identity theft and synthetic identities.<br>* `SUSPICIOUS_ACTIVITY` - The account has exhibited suspicious behavior, such as unauthorized access or fraudulent transactions, necessitating further investigation.<br>* `RISK_VIOLATION` - The account has been involved in deliberate misuse by the legitimate account holder. Examples include disputing valid transactions without cause, falsely claiming non-receipt of goods, or engaging in intentional bust-out schemes to exploit account services.<br>* `END_USER_REQUEST` - The account holder has voluntarily requested the closure of the account for personal reasons. This encompasses situations such as bankruptcy, other financial considerations, or the account holder's death.<br>* `ISSUER_REQUEST` - The issuer has initiated the closure of the account due to business strategy, risk management, inactivity, product changes, regulatory concerns, or violations of terms and conditions.<br>* `NOT_ACTIVE` - The account has not had any transactions or payment activity within a specified period. This status applies to accounts that are paused or closed due to inactivity.<br>* `INTERNAL_REVIEW` - The account is temporarily paused pending further internal review. In future implementations, this status may prevent clients from activating the account via APIs until the review is completed.<br>* `OTHER` - The reason for the account's current status does not fall into any of the above categories. A comment should be provided to specify the particular reason.<br>|
|comment|string|false|none|Additional context or information related to the account.|
|token|string(uuid)|true|none|Globally unique identifier for the account. This is the same as the account_token returned by the enroll endpoint. If using this parameter, do not include pagination.<br>|
|verification_address|object|false|none|**Deprecated.**|
|created|string \| null(date-time)|true|none|Timestamp of when the account was created.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|state|ACTIVE|
|state|PAUSED|
|state|CLOSED|
|substatus|FRAUD_IDENTIFIED|
|substatus|SUSPICIOUS_ACTIVITY|
|substatus|RISK_VIOLATION|
|substatus|END_USER_REQUEST|
|substatus|ISSUER_REQUEST|
|substatus|NOT_ACTIVE|
|substatus|INTERNAL_REVIEW|
|substatus|OTHER|

<h2 id="tocS_auth-rule-entity">auth-rule-entity</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaauth-rule-entity"></a>
<a id="schema_auth-rule-entity"></a>
<a id="tocSauth-rule-entity"></a>
<a id="tocsauth-rule-entity"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "PROGRAM"
}
```

An entity that an Auth Rule can apply to. The `type` field determines which other fields are present.

- `PROGRAM`: the entire card program.
- `CARD`: a single card.
- `ACCOUNT`: a single account.
- `BUSINESS_ACCOUNT`: a single business account.
- `CARD_TAG`: every card that carries the given tag (`key` and `value`).

`CARD` and `CARD_TAG` entities can only be used with rules on the `AUTHORIZATION`, `THREE_DS_AUTHENTICATION`, `TOKENIZATION` and `CARD_TRANSACTION_UPDATE` event streams. Rules on the other event streams accept `PROGRAM`, `ACCOUNT` and `BUSINESS_ACCOUNT` only.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|[auth-rule-program-entity](#schemaauth-rule-program-entity)|false|none|The entire card program. Takes no other fields.|
|*oneOf*|[auth-rule-card-entity](#schemaauth-rule-card-entity)|false|none|A single card.|
|*oneOf*|[auth-rule-account-entity](#schemaauth-rule-account-entity)|false|none|A single account.|
|*oneOf*|[auth-rule-business-account-entity](#schemaauth-rule-business-account-entity)|false|none|A single business account.|
|*oneOf*|[auth-rule-card-tag-entity](#schemaauth-rule-card-tag-entity)|false|none|Every card whose `tags` contain `key` set to `value`.|

<h2 id="tocS_auth-rule-type">auth-rule-type</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaauth-rule-type"></a>
<a id="schema_auth-rule-type"></a>
<a id="tocSauth-rule-type"></a>
<a id="tocsauth-rule-type"></a>

```json
"VELOCITY_LIMIT"
```

The type of Auth Rule. For certain rule types, this determines the event stream during which it will be evaluated. For rules that can be applied to one of several event streams, the effective one is defined by the separate `event_stream` field.

- `VELOCITY_LIMIT`: AUTHORIZATION event stream.
- `MERCHANT_LOCK`: AUTHORIZATION event stream.
- `CONDITIONAL_ACTION`: AUTHORIZATION, THREE_DS_AUTHENTICATION, TOKENIZATION, ACH_CREDIT_RECEIPT, ACH_DEBIT_RECEIPT, CARD_TRANSACTION_UPDATE, or ACH_PAYMENT_UPDATE event stream.
- `TYPESCRIPT_CODE`: AUTHORIZATION, THREE_DS_AUTHENTICATION, TOKENIZATION, ACH_CREDIT_RECEIPT, ACH_DEBIT_RECEIPT, CARD_TRANSACTION_UPDATE, or ACH_PAYMENT_UPDATE event stream.
- `OTHER`: A rule whose type is not exposed through this API. Rules of this type are read-only; `OTHER` cannot be used when creating a rule.

```json
  "duration": 10,

}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|none|
|duration|integer|true|none|The size of the trailing window to calculate Spend Velocity over in seconds. The minimum value is 10 seconds, and the maximum value is 7776000 seconds (90 days).|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|Velocity over the current day since 00:00 / 12 AM in Eastern Time|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|Velocity over the current week since 00:00 / 12 AM in Eastern Time on specified `day_of_week`|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|day_of_week|integer|false|none|The day of the week to start the week from. Following ISO-8601, 1 is Monday and 7 is Sunday. Defaults to Monday if not specified.|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|Velocity over the current month since 00:00 / 12 AM in Eastern Time on specified `day_of_month`.|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|day_of_month|integer|false|none|The day of the month to start from. Accepts values from 1 to 31, and will reset at the end of the month if the day exceeds the number of days in the month. Defaults to the 1st of the month if not specified.|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|Velocity over the current year since 00:00 / 12 AM in Eastern Time on specified `month` and `day_of_month`. This validates the month and day of the year to start from is a real date. In the event that February 29th is selected, in non-leap years, the window will start from February 28th.|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|day_of_month|integer|false|none|The day of the month to start from. Defaults to the 1st of the month if not specified.|
|month|integer|false|none|The month to start from. 1 is January and 12 is December. Defaults to January if not specified.|

<h2 id="tocS_rule-feature">rule-feature</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarule-feature"></a>
<a id="schema_rule-feature"></a>
<a id="tocSrule-feature"></a>
<a id="tocsrule-feature"></a>

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "type": "AUTHORIZATION"
}
```

A feature made available to the rule. The `name` field is the variable name used in the rule function signature. The `type` field determines which data the feature provides to the rule at evaluation time.

- `AUTHORIZATION`: The authorization request being evaluated. Only available for AUTHORIZATION event stream rules.
- `AUTHENTICATION`: The 3DS authentication request being evaluated. Only available for THREE_DS_AUTHENTICATION event stream rules.
- `TOKENIZATION`: The tokenization request being evaluated. Only available for TOKENIZATION event stream rules.
- `ACH_RECEIPT`: The ACH receipt being evaluated. Only available for ACH_CREDIT_RECEIPT and ACH_DEBIT_RECEIPT event stream rules.
- `CARD_TRANSACTION`: The card transaction being evaluated. Only available for CARD_TRANSACTION_UPDATE event stream rules.
- `ACH_PAYMENT`: The ACH payment being evaluated. Only available for ACH_PAYMENT_UPDATE event stream rules.
- `EXTERNAL_BANK_ACCOUNT`: The external bank account tied to the ACH payment being evaluated. Only available for ACH_PAYMENT_UPDATE event stream rules.
- `CARD`: The card associated with the event. Available for AUTHORIZATION, THREE_DS_AUTHENTICATION, and CARD_TRANSACTION_UPDATE event stream rules.
- `ACCOUNT_HOLDER`: The account holder associated with the event. Available for AUTHORIZATION, THREE_DS_AUTHENTICATION, CARD_TRANSACTION_UPDATE, and ACH_PAYMENT_UPDATE event stream rules.
- `IP_METADATA`: IP address metadata for the request. Available for THREE_DS_AUTHENTICATION event stream rules.
- `SPEND_VELOCITY`: Spend velocity data for the card or account. Requires `scope`, `period`, and optionally `filters` to configure the velocity calculation. Available for AUTHORIZATION and CARD_TRANSACTION_UPDATE event stream rules.
- `PAYMENT_VELOCITY`: ACH payment velocity data, aggregated over the given scope. Requires `scope`, `period`, and optionally `filters` to configure the velocity calculation. Available for ACH_PAYMENT_UPDATE event stream rules.
- `CONSECUTIVE_DECLINES`: The number of consecutive declined transactions since the last approval for the card or account. Requires `scope`. Available for AUTHORIZATION and CARD_TRANSACTION_UPDATE event stream rules.
- `ACH_PAYMENT_HISTORY`: Windowed settled-amount statistics derived from the financial account's ACH payment history. Requires `scope`. Available for ACH_PAYMENT_UPDATE event stream rules.
- `TRANSACTION_HISTORY_SIGNALS`: Behavioral feature state derived from the entity's transaction history. Requires `scope` to specify whether to load card, account, or business account history. Available for AUTHORIZATION and CARD_TRANSACTION_UPDATE event stream rules.

<h2 id="tocS_auth-rule-entities">auth-rule-entities</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaauth-rule-entities"></a>
<a id="schema_auth-rule-entities"></a>
<a id="tocSauth-rule-entities"></a>
<a id="tocsauth-rule-entities"></a>

```json
{
  "include": [
    {
      "type": "PROGRAM"
    }
  ],
  "exclude": [
    {
      "type": "PROGRAM"
    }
  ]
}
```

The entities an Auth Rule applies to (`include`) and does not apply to (`exclude`). An exclusion overrides an inclusion, so a card excluded here is skipped even when the program, its account or one of its tags is included.

The rule's resulting entities must satisfy these constraints after any write:

- `include` must contain at least one entity.
- If `PROGRAM` is included, it must be the only included entity.
- `PROGRAM` cannot be excluded.
- An entity cannot appear in both `include` and `exclude`, or twice in the same list.
- A rule can have at most 1,000 entities across `include` and `exclude`, not counting `PROGRAM`.
- Entity types must be valid for the rule's event stream.
- `CARD`, `ACCOUNT` and `BUSINESS_ACCOUNT` tokens must belong to your program.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|include|[[auth-rule-entity](#schemaauth-rule-entity)]|false|none|Entities the Auth Rule applies to. Defaults to an empty list in requests.|
|exclude|[[auth-rule-entity](#schemaauth-rule-entity)]|false|none|Entities the Auth Rule does not apply to. Defaults to an empty list in requests.|

<h2 id="tocS_patch-auth-rule-entities-request">patch-auth-rule-entities-request</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapatch-auth-rule-entities-request"></a>
<a id="schema_patch-auth-rule-entities-request"></a>
<a id="tocSpatch-auth-rule-entities-request"></a>
<a id="tocspatch-auth-rule-entities-request"></a>

```json
{
  "add": {
    "include": [
      {
        "type": "PROGRAM"
      }
    ],
    "exclude": [
      {
        "type": "PROGRAM"
      }
    ]
  },
  "remove": {
    "include": [
      {
        "type": "PROGRAM"
      }
    ],
    "exclude": [
      {
        "type": "PROGRAM"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Changes the rule's entities incrementally. `add` adds to the rule's `include` and `exclude` lists, and `remove` removes from them. Adding an entity that is already present, or removing one that is not, has no effect. A request with neither leaves entities unchanged.

The same entity cannot appear twice in one list, in both `add.include` and `remove.include`, or in both `add.exclude` and `remove.exclude`. To move an entity between `include` and `exclude`, remove it from one list and add it to the other in the same request.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|add|[auth-rule-entities](#schemaauth-rule-entities)|false|none|Entities to add to the rule's `include` and `exclude` lists|
|remove|[auth-rule-entities](#schemaauth-rule-entities)|false|none|Entities to remove from the rule's `include` and `exclude` lists|

```json
{
```

```json
  "avg_transaction_amount_7d": 0,

  "approved_txn_count_7d": 0,
  "avg_transaction_amount_30d": 0,

  "approved_txn_count_30d": 0,
  "avg_transaction_amount_90d": 0,
  "stdev_transaction_amount_90d": 0,

  "time_since_last_transaction_days": 0,

    "string"
```
