The Dispute object tracks the progression of a dispute throughout its lifecycle.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|case_id|string \| null|true|none|Identifier assigned by the network for this dispute.|
|token|string(uuid)|true|none|Token assigned by Lithic for the dispute, in UUID format.|
|card_token|string(uuid)|true|none|Token for the card used in the dispute, in UUID format.|
|account_token|string(uuid)|true|none|Token for the account associated with the dispute, in UUID format.|
|claim_token|string \| null(uuid)|true|none|Token for the claim this dispute was filed under, in UUID format. Null for disputes not initiated through the Dispute Intake API.|
|network|string|true|none|Card network handling the dispute.|
|currency|string|true|none|Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code.|
|created|string(date-time)|true|none|When the dispute was created.|
|updated|string(date-time)|true|none|When the dispute was last updated.|
|merchant|[merchant](#schemamerchant)|true|none|none|
|transaction_series|[transaction-series2](#schematransaction-series2) \| null|true|none|none|
|liability_allocation|[liability-allocation](#schemaliability-allocation)|true|none|Current breakdown of how liability is allocated for the disputed amount|
|status|string \| null|true|none|Current status of the dispute.|
|disposition|string \| null|true|none|Dispute resolution outcome|
|events|[[event2](#schemaevent2)]|true|none|Chronological list of events that have occurred in the dispute lifecycle|

|disposition|WITHDRAWN|
|disposition|DENIED|
|disposition|null|

Card Authorization

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchant|[transaction_merchant](#schematransaction_merchant)|true|none|Merchant information including full location details.|
|service_location|null \| [service_location](#schemaservice_location)|true|none|none|
|avs|object|true|none|none|
|card|[asa_request_card](#schemaasa_request_card)|true|none|Card object in ASA|
|cardholder_authentication|[cardholder_authentication](#schemacardholder_authentication)|false|none|none|
|pos|object|false|none|none|
|amount|integer(int64)|true|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated, use `amounts`. Authorization amount of the transaction (in cents), including any acquirer fees. The contents of this field are identical to `authorization_amount`.|
|acquirer_fee|integer(int64)|true|none|Fee (in cents) assessed by the merchant and paid for by the cardholder. Will be zero if no fee is assessed. Rebates may be transmitted as a negative value to indicate credited fees.|
|authorization_amount|integer(int64)|true|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated, use `amounts`. The base transaction amount (in cents) plus the acquirer fee field. This is the amount the issuer should authorize against unless the issuer is paying the acquirer fee on behalf of the cardholder.|
|cardholder_currency|string|true|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated, use `amounts`. 3-character alphabetic ISO 4217 code for cardholder's billing currency.|
|cash_amount|integer(int64)|true|none|The amount of cash requested by the cardholder, in the cardholder billing currency's smallest unit. For purchase-with-cashback transactions this is the cashback portion only; for ATM transactions this is the full amount. This amount includes all acquirer fees.<br><br>If no cash was requested, the value of this field will be 0, and the field will always be present.|
|cashback|integer(int64)|false|none|Deprecated, use `cash_amount`.|
|token_info|null \| [token_info](#schematoken_info)|false|none|none|
|ttl|string(date-time)|false|none|Deprecated: approximate time-to-live for the authorization.|
|conversion_rate|number|false|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated, use `amounts`. If the transaction was requested in a currency other than the settlement currency, this field will be populated to indicate the rate used to translate the merchant_amount to the amount (i.e., `merchant_amount` x `conversion_rate` = `amount`). Note that the `merchant_amount` is in the local currency and the amount is in the settlement currency.|
|created|string(date-time)|true|none|Date and time when the transaction first occurred in UTC.|
|merchant_amount|integer(int64)|true|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated, use `amounts`. The amount that the merchant will receive, denominated in `merchant_currency` and in the smallest currency unit. Note the amount includes `acquirer_fee`, similar to `authorization_amount`. It will be different from `authorization_amount` if the merchant is taking payment in a different currency.|
|merchant_currency|object|true|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated, use `amounts`.|
|network|string|false|none|Card network of the authorization.|
|network_risk_score|[network_risk_score](#schemanetwork_risk_score)|false|none|Network-provided score assessing risk level associated with a given authorization. Scores are on a range of 0-999, with 0 representing the lowest risk and 999 representing the highest risk. For Visa transactions, where the raw score has a range of 0-99, Lithic will normalize the score by multiplying the raw score by 10x.|
|settled_amount|integer(int64)|true|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated, use `amounts`. Amount (in cents) of the transaction that has been settled, including any acquirer fees.|
|amounts|object|true|none|Structured amounts for this authorization. The `cardholder` and `merchant` amounts reflect the original network authorization values. For programs with hold adjustments enabled (e.g., automated fuel dispensers or tipping MCCs), the `hold` amount may exceed the `cardholder` and `merchant` amounts to account for anticipated final transaction amounts such as tips or fuel fill-ups|
|status|[asa_request_status](#schemaasa_request_status)|true|none|The type of authorization request that this request is for. Note that `CREDIT_AUTHORIZATION` and `FINANCIAL_CREDIT_AUTHORIZATION` is only available to users with credit decisioning via ASA enabled.|
|token|string(uuid)|true|none|The provisional transaction group uuid associated with the authorization|
|event_token|string(uuid)|false|none|The event token associated with the authorization. This field is only set for programs enrolled into the beta.|
|fleet_info|[asa_request_fleet_info](#schemaasa_request_fleet_info)|false|none|Optional Object containing information if the Card is a part of a Fleet managed program|
|network_specific_data|[asa_network_specific_data](#schemaasa_network_specific_data)|false|none|Contains raw data provided by the card network, including attributes that provide further context about the authorization. If populated by the network, data is organized by Lithic and passed through without further modification. Please consult the official network documentation for more details about these values and how to use them. This object is only available to certain programs- contact your Customer Success Manager to discuss enabling access.|
|account_type|[account_type](#schemaaccount_type)|false|none|The selected account type for applicable ATM transactions such as cash withdrawals, deposits, or balance inquiries.|
|transaction_initiator|string|true|none|The entity that initiated the transaction.|
|latest_challenge|object|false|none|The latest Authorization Challenge that was issued to the cardholder for this merchant.|
|name_validation|object \| null|true|none|Network name validation data, present when the card network requested name validation for this transaction. Contains the cardholder name provided by the network and Lithic's computed match result against KYC data on file.|

<h2 id="tocS_asa-response">asa-response</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaasa-response"></a>

```json
{
  "result": "APPROVED",
  "token": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "approved_amount": 0,
  "avs_result": "FAIL",
  "balance": {
    "amount": 0,
    "available": 0
  },
  "challenge_phone_number": "string",
  "name_validation_result": {
    "full_name": "MATCH"
  }
}
```

The Auth Stream Access response payload that an ASA responder may respond with in response to a request.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|result|string|true|none|Result of the Authorization decision. Provide `APPROVED` to accept the authorization. Any other response will decline the authorization. Result `CHALLENGE` is valid only for cardholder-initiated transactions. If a value not present in the enumeration is returned the transaction will be declined with the `CUSTOM_ASA_RESULT` detailed result.|
|token|string(uuid)|false|none|The transaction token from the ASA request.|
|approved_amount|integer(int64)|false|none|The amount approved for the transaction. Note that setting this implies a partial approval. This property should not be present if the intention is to fully approve the transaction. See: https://docs.lithic.com/docs/partial-approval#partial-approval|
|avs_result|string|false|none|The ASA responder may return an address verification (AVS) match indicator for evaluation by the acquirer. The merchant can choose whether to proceed with the transaction in the case of an approval with AVS failure. When they do not, this typically appears as a subsequent AUTHORIZATION_REVERSAL event following the AUTHORIZATION. Note that AVS data submitted by merchants can be variable in quality, and we recommend card programs exercise adjust their decisioning logic accordingly.|
|balance|object|false|none|Respective available amount and settled amount values (in cents). These values can be used by merchants for authorization decisions as well as balance display at point of sale or ATM.|
|challenge_phone_number|string|false|none|The phone number to use for sending an Authorization Challenge SMS. Relevant only when the result is `CHALLENGE`. The expected format is E.164 without hyphens. For example, "+15555555555" for a US phone number.|
|name_validation_result|[name_validation_result](#schemaname_validation_result)|false|none|Name validation result returned by the ASA responder. When present, overrides Lithic's internally computed result. If no response is provided, the `name_on_file_match` value sent on the request will be the value returned to the Network.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|result|APPROVED|
|result|AVS_INVALID|
|result|CARD_PAUSED|
|result|INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS|
|result|UNAUTHORIZED_MERCHANT|
|result|VELOCITY_EXCEEDED|
|result|DRIVER_NUMBER_INVALID|
|result|VEHICLE_NUMBER_INVALID|
|result|SUSPECTED_FRAUD|
|result|CHALLENGE|
|avs_result|FAIL|
|avs_result|MATCH|
|avs_result|MATCH_ADDRESS_ONLY|
|avs_result|MATCH_ZIP_ONLY|

Payload for digital wallet tokenization approval requests. Used for both the decisioning responder request (sent to the customer's endpoint for a real-time decision) and the subsequent webhook event (sent after the decision is made). Fields like customer_tokenization_decision, tokenization_decline_reasons, tokenization_tfa_reasons, and rule_results are only populated in the webhook event, not in the initial decisioning request.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_token|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the user tokenizing a card|
|card_token|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the card being tokenized|
|created|string(date-time)|true|none|Indicate when the request was received from Mastercard or Visa|
|device|[device](#schemadevice)|false|none|none|
|issuer_decision|string|true|none|Whether Lithic decisioned on the token, and if so, what the decision was. APPROVED/VERIFICATION_REQUIRED/DENIED.|
|tokenization_channel|string|true|none|The channel through which the tokenization was made.|
|tokenization_source|string|false|none|The source of the tokenization.|
|tokenization_token|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the digital wallet token attempt|
|wallet_decisioning_info|[wallet-decisioning-info](#schemawallet-decisioning-info)|true|none|none|
|digital_wallet_token_metadata|[digital-wallet-token-metadata](#schemadigital-wallet-token-metadata)|true|none|Contains the metadata for the digital wallet being tokenized.|
|customer_tokenization_decision|null \| [customer-tokenization-decision](#schemacustomer-tokenization-decision)|false|none|The customer's tokenization decision outcome. Only populated in webhook events (after decisioning), not in the initial decisioning request|
|event_type|string|true|none|The name of this event|
|tokenization_decline_reasons|[[tokenization-decline-reason](#schematokenization-decline-reason)]|false|none|List of reasons why the tokenization was declined. Only populated in webhook events, not in the initial decisioning request|
|tokenization_tfa_reasons|[[tokenization-tfa-reason](#schematokenization-tfa-reason)]|false|none|List of reasons why two-factor authentication was required. Only populated in webhook events, not in the initial decisioning request|
|rule_results|[[tokenization-rule-result](#schematokenization-rule-result)]|false|none|Results from rules that were evaluated for this tokenization. Only populated in webhook events, not in the initial decisioning request|

The response payload that a Tokenization Decisioning responder may respond with in response to a request.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tokenization_decision|string|true|none|The decision for tokenization|
|phone_number|string|true|none|Phone number of the end user attempting a tokenization. Lithic must pass this to the card networks to pass to the wallets to display for the user as they select an authentication option in their digital wallet. Lithic will always default to using this value for authentication over the account holder information on file. E.164 format without hyphens. For example, "+15555555555" for a US phone number.|
|email|string(email)|true|none|Email address of the end user attempting a tokenization to be used for authentication. Lithic must pass this to the card networks to pass to the wallets to display for the user as they select an authentication option in their digital wallet. Lithic will always default to using this value for authentication over the account holder information on file. Permitted values: Valid email address. For example, "johnny@appleseed.com".|
|mobile_application_name|string|true|none|Name of the mobile application that the digital wallet will open for the end user to complete authentication. For example, "Wells Fargo".|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|tokenization_decision|APPROVE|
|tokenization_decision|AUTHENTICATE|
|tokenization_decision|DECLINE|

```json
{
  "amount": 200,
  "arbitration_date": null,
  "created": "2023-07-19T18:39:34.768Z",
  "customer_filed_date": "2023-07-20T09:00:00Z",
  "customer_note": "I didn't receive the goods.",
  "network_claim_ids": [
    "CLAIM-001"
  ],
  "network_filed_date": "2023-07-21T11:00:00Z",
  "network_reason_code": "4808",
  "prearbitration_date": null,
  "primary_claim_id": "CLAIM-001",
  "reason": "GOODS_SERVICES_NOT_RECEIVED",
  "representment_date": null,
  "resolution_date": null,
  "resolution_note": null,
  "resolution_reason": null,
  "status": "SUBMITTED",
  "token": "b24230fa-181e-4b31-9a5c-276747e619a0",
  "transaction_token": "12345624-aa69-4cbc-a946-30d90181b621"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|true|none|Amount under dispute. May be different from the original transaction amount.|
|arbitration_date|string \| null(date-time)|true|none|Date dispute entered arbitration.|
|created|string(date-time)|true|none|Timestamp of when first Dispute was reported.|
|customer_filed_date|string \| null(date-time)|true|none|Date that the dispute was filed by the customer making the dispute.|
|customer_note|string \| null|true|none|End customer description of the reason for the dispute.|
|network_claim_ids|[string] \| null|true|none|Unique identifiers for the dispute from the network.|
|network_filed_date|string \| null(date-time)|true|none|Date that the dispute was submitted to the network.|
|network_reason_code|string \| null|true|none|Network reason code used to file the dispute.|
|prearbitration_date|string \| null(date-time)|true|none|Date dispute entered pre-arbitration.|
|primary_claim_id|string \| null|true|none|Unique identifier for the dispute from the network. If there are multiple, this will be the first claim id set by the network|
|reason|string|true|none|Dispute reason:<br>* `ATM_CASH_MISDISPENSE`: ATM cash misdispense.<br>* `CANCELLED`: Transaction was cancelled by the customer.<br>* `DUPLICATED`: The transaction was a duplicate.<br>* `FRAUD_CARD_NOT_PRESENT`: Fraudulent transaction, card not present.<br>* `FRAUD_CARD_PRESENT`: Fraudulent transaction, card present.<br>* `FRAUD_OTHER`: Fraudulent transaction, other types such as questionable merchant activity.<br>* `GOODS_SERVICES_NOT_AS_DESCRIBED`: The goods or services were not as described.<br>* `GOODS_SERVICES_NOT_RECEIVED`: The goods or services were not received.<br>* `INCORRECT_AMOUNT`: The transaction amount was incorrect.<br>* `MISSING_AUTH`: The transaction was missing authorization.<br>* `OTHER`: Other reason.<br>* `PROCESSING_ERROR`: Processing error.<br>* `REFUND_NOT_PROCESSED`: The refund was not processed.<br>* `RECURRING_TRANSACTION_NOT_CANCELLED`: The recurring transaction was not cancelled.<br>|
|representment_date|string \| null(date-time)|true|none|Date the representment was received.|
|resolution_date|string \| null(date-time)|true|none|Date that the dispute was resolved.|
|resolution_note|string \| null|true|none|Note by Dispute team on the case resolution.|
|resolution_reason|string \| null|true|none|Reason for the dispute resolution:<br>* `CASE_LOST`: This case was lost at final arbitration.<br>* `NETWORK_REJECTED`: Network rejected.<br>* `NO_DISPUTE_RIGHTS_3DS`: No dispute rights, 3DS.<br>* `NO_DISPUTE_RIGHTS_BELOW_THRESHOLD`: No dispute rights, below threshold.<br>* `NO_DISPUTE_RIGHTS_CONTACTLESS`: No dispute rights, contactless.<br>* `NO_DISPUTE_RIGHTS_HYBRID`: No dispute rights, hybrid.<br>* `NO_DISPUTE_RIGHTS_MAX_CHARGEBACKS`: No dispute rights, max chargebacks.<br>* `NO_DISPUTE_RIGHTS_OTHER`: No dispute rights, other.<br>* `PAST_FILING_DATE`: Past filing date.<br>* `PREARBITRATION_REJECTED`: Prearbitration rejected.<br>* `PROCESSOR_REJECTED_OTHER`: Processor rejected, other.<br>* `REFUNDED`: Refunded.<br>* `REFUNDED_AFTER_CHARGEBACK`: Refunded after chargeback.<br>* `WITHDRAWN`: Withdrawn.<br>* `WON_ARBITRATION`: Won arbitration.<br>* `WON_FIRST_CHARGEBACK`: Won first chargeback.<br>* `WON_PREARBITRATION`: Won prearbitration.<br>|
|status|string|true|none|Status types:<br>* `NEW` - New dispute case is opened.<br>* `PENDING_CUSTOMER` - Lithic is waiting for customer to provide more information.<br>* `SUBMITTED` - Dispute is submitted to the card network.<br>* `REPRESENTMENT` - Case has entered second presentment.<br>* `PREARBITRATION` - Case has entered prearbitration.<br>* `ARBITRATION` - Case has entered arbitration.<br>* `CASE_WON` - Case was won and credit will be issued.<br>* `CASE_CLOSED` - Case was lost or withdrawn.<br>|
|token|string(uuid)|true|none|Globally unique identifier.|
|transaction_token|string(uuid)|true|none|The transaction that is being disputed. A transaction can only be disputed once but may have multiple dispute cases.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|reason|ATM_CASH_MISDISPENSE|
|reason|CANCELLED|
|reason|DUPLICATED|
|reason|FRAUD_CARD_NOT_PRESENT|
|reason|FRAUD_CARD_PRESENT|

|resolution_reason|NO_DISPUTE_RIGHTS_3DS|
|resolution_reason|NO_DISPUTE_RIGHTS_BELOW_THRESHOLD|
|resolution_reason|NO_DISPUTE_RIGHTS_CONTACTLESS|
|resolution_reason|NO_DISPUTE_RIGHTS_HYBRID|

<h2 id="tocS_three-ds-decisioning">three-ds-decisioning</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemathree-ds-decisioning"></a>
<a id="schema_three-ds-decisioning"></a>
<a id="tocSthree-ds-decisioning"></a>
<a id="tocsthree-ds-decisioning"></a>

```json
{
  "three_ds_authentication_decision": "APPROVE",
  "oob_url": "string",
  "exemption_applied": "TRANSACTION_RISK_ANALYSIS"
}
```

Information on whether the Authentication should be approved, declined or challenged.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|three_ds_authentication_decision|string|true|none|* `APPROVE` - Approve the 3DS Transaction and proceed to Authorization<br>* `DECLINE` - Decline the 3DS Transaction ending the transaction<br>* `CHALLENGE_REQUESTED` - Conditional Approval for the 3DS Transaction where a follow-up Challenge will be triggered to further authenticate the Cardholder|
|oob_url|string|false|none|URL which may be used in the presentation of a 3DS Challenge UI to the cardholder. This value will be used by the ACS as the OOB App URL. When applicable, this URL may be used for automatic app switching or rendered directly as an element in the Challenge UI.<br>This field is only used with CHALLENGE_REQUESTED decision and when customer orchestrates the 3DS challenge on their own.|
|exemption_applied|string|false|none|SCA exemption the card program asserts on an `APPROVE` decision. Ignored for `DECLINE` or `CHALLENGE_REQUESTED`.<br><br>When `psd2_context` is present in the decisioning request, this field must be set to approve with<br>an exemption. The card program would do this when they have their own grounds or knowledge that<br>override Lithic's validation. Lithic passes the value to the ACS to generate the correct ECI and<br>authentication value.<br><br>Omit (or send `NONE`) for full SCA with no exemption asserted.<br><br>* `TRANSACTION_RISK_ANALYSIS` - Transaction Risk Analysis (TRA); card program has independent fraud scoring that supports frictionless approval<br>* `RECURRING_PAYMENT` - Recurring payment with a fixed amount to the same payee; card program has explicit mandate data|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|three_ds_authentication_decision|APPROVE|
|three_ds_authentication_decision|DECLINE|
|three_ds_authentication_decision|CHALLENGE_REQUESTED|
|exemption_applied|TRANSACTION_RISK_ANALYSIS|
|exemption_applied|RECURRING_PAYMENT|
